entry.title: Palm Beach Atlantic University celebrates Hispanic heritage through art, music festival
entry.summary: Palm Beach Atlantic University wrapped up its three-day Hispanic Heritage Festival on Saturday, celebrating Hispanic art, culture and music during Hispanic Heritage Month in South Florida. The annual festival featured a contemporary art exhibition and a series of musical performances designed to showcase the cultural contributions and artistic traditions of the Hispanic world. Organizers say the event continues to grow as it enters its 17th year. In a region with a large Hispanic population, organizers say the festival provides an opportunity for students and community members to engage with artists and musicians while learning more about the diversity of Hispanic cultures. Artists from across the Hispanic world The festival began Thursday with an art exhibition featuring artists representing more than 10 countries. Visitors viewed a wide range of artistic styles and mediums, including oil paintings, photography and metalwork. Among the featured artists was Franco Sotillo, a visual artist originally from Lima, Peru, who said his work combines mixed media and reflects both his heritage and personal experiences. 'I'm a visual artist and came from Lima, Peru,' Sotillo said. 'I moved to this country 12 years ago.' Sotillo said his work incorporates materials including oils, paper and other raw elements. He said sharing his art allows him to introduce audiences to Peruvian artistic expression. 'I'm an immigrant, but also bringing my culture to the states to show people how Peruvian art is expressed,' Sotillo said. Festival expands music offerings Festival Director Michael O'Connor said the event continues to evolve each year. 'We're expanding every year,' O'Connor said. O'Connor said this year's festival marked the first time organizers expanded programming beyond art and classical music to also include popular music from Hispanic cultures. 'What we want to do is we want to celebrate the Hispanic artistic heritage, because here in South Florida, especially, we have a very, very large Hispanic population,' O'Connor said. Inspiring students and the community Organizers said they hope attendees leave with a deeper appreciation for Hispanic artistic traditions and the people behind them. 'We hope they'll be inspired too to see the artworks here at the exhibition and to see how the Hispanic world makes itself known through visual arts,' O'Connor said. Hundreds of thousands of people lost power in the wake of the storm, and 430,000 customers remained without power Saturday morning. As of Sunday afternoon, more than 200,000 customers had power restored, DeSantis said. FLP is expected to be largely finished with power restoration efforts by Monday. entry.title: Treasure Coast High School freshman dies after being hit by car while walking to school
entry.summary: A 14-year-old Treasure Coast High School student who was hit by a vehicle while walking to school last week has died from his injuries, according to the Port St. Lucie Police Department. Police said the crash happened the morning of Oct. 7 near the intersection of Southwest Port St. Lucie Boulevard and Southwest Squirrel Avenue. According to police, the freshman was walking northbound along Port St. Lucie Boulevard near the edge of the roadway when he was struck from behind by a 2002 Ford Excursion driven by a 72-year-old man. The teen suffered critical injuries and was transported to a local hospital. Police said he was pronounced clinically deceased on Oct. 9 shortly after 4 p.m. Investigators said the crash remains under investigation as detectives continue to examine the circumstances surrounding what happened. Amid the tragedy, the student's family made the decision to donate his organs in hopes of helping others and honoring their son's memory. 'In the midst of their grief, their decision offers the possibility of hope and healing for other families and individuals whose lives may be changed through this extraordinary gift,' police said in a statement. Treasure Coast High School will provide grief counseling services for students and staff as the school community copes with the loss. The Port St. Lucie Police Department extended its condolences to the student's family, friends, classmates and the entire Treasure Coast High School community. 'We recognize that no words can ease the pain of losing a child, and our thoughts remain with everyone affected by this heartbreaking tragedy,' the department said.

entry.title: No lawyer, no law degree: Port St. Lucie man takes on Flock cameras in federal court - WPEC
entry.summary: No lawyer, no law degree: Port St. Lucie man takes on Flock cameras in federal court    WPEC
entry.article_text: A former surgeon turned Wall Street analyst is taking on his city, its mayor and surveillance technology company Flock Safety in federal court. He has no lawyer and wants the city's license plate cameras gone for good. Steven Greer filed the lawsuit in August against Port St. Lucie, Mayor Shannon Martin and Flock Safety, arguing the technology police use to track criminals also threatens Americans' constitutional rights from privacy to gun ownership. "I was appalled at what I learned," Greer told the CBS12 News I-Team. Greer said he spent much of August researching Flock's technology and preparing the federal lawsuit himself. While he has no formal legal training, he says his years working as a surgeon and later on Wall Street prepared him for the technical research and writing involved in representing himself. Flock's automated license plate readers photograph passing vehicles, recording identifying information along with the time and location. Police can search those records to help identify vehicles connected to crimes, but Greer argues the technology also allows officers to reconstruct someone's movements without obtaining a warrant. His amended complaint alleges Port St. Lucie operated 53 Flock cameras and another 73 Axon license plate readers, for a combined network of 126 devices. See also: Brevard County sheriff’s agent killed in wrong-way crash while responding to shooting Greer argues the collection and sharing of that information violates the Fourth Amendment, which protects against unreasonable searches and seizures. The CBS12 News I-Team has been reporting on Flock cameras since last year, examining how the technology is used by law enforcement and more recently, allegations of misuse. In Fort Pierce, Officer Josepher Crutchfield was arrested after investigators accused him of searching his ex-girlfriend's vehicle 382 times. In another case, a woman was arrested and jailed after investigators mistakenly linked her vehicle to a deadly hit-and-run crash. The charges against her were later dropped. Greer cites both cases in his complaint, but argues the larger problem is the surveillance system itself. During their interview, CBS12 I-Team reporter Katie Bente asked Greer about people who aren't concerned about surveillance because they have nothing to hide. "A lot of people say, you know, 'I'm not doing anything wrong. So what does it really matter?'" Bente asked. "Those are the people who don't deserve freedoms. It's just sheer ignorance. They don't even understand why we have a Fourth Amendment," Greer responded. Law enforcement agencies, however, defend license plate readers as valuable investigative tools, crediting the technology with helping identify suspects, recover stolen vehicles and solve crimes. "I know that police have always argued these Flock cameras really help solve crimes. What would be your response to that?" Bente asked. "That's their number one defense. It's not true," Greer said. His assertion is disputed by law enforcement agencies that have documented cases in which license plate reader information helped investigators. Whether the technology is useful in solving crimes is a separate question from whether particular searches are constitutional. Greer's lawsuit also raises an argument not typically associated with traffic cameras: the right to bear arms. He points to Flock cameras reportedly installed at the entrance to the Ocala Shooting Range, a public gun range in Marion County. Greer argues that recording who visits a shooting range could discourage people from exercising their Second Amendment rights. "When I saw that case where they have Flock cameras in gun ranges, I said, 'Whoa, that's a Second Amendment violation,'" Greer told the I-Team. The key buzzword is chilling. You know, if they scare you away from using your gun rights that's a violation." The complaint also challenges the city's handling of public records requests, alleging officials withheld information about camera locations and system audit logs. It includes claims under Florida's constitutional privacy protections and questions the legality of public spending on the network. Greer has also raised First Amendment concerns following a Sept. Lucie City Council meeting. He told the I-Team that the number of police officers present made him feel intimidated and could discourage residents from speaking out. I'm looking around, I see police officers all over the place," Greer said. Meanwhile, the legal debate over Flock is playing out across the country. In Oklahoma, a federal judge ruled Oct. 1 that a warrantless search of approximately a month of license plate location records violated the Fourth Amendment, suppressing evidence obtained following the search. The ruling concerned the specific circumstances of that case and did not establish that all Flock searches are unconstitutional. Law enforcement agencies have continued to defend the technology, while privacy advocates argue that large networks of searchable cameras allow police to monitor ordinary drivers on a scale that wasn't previously possible. Florida is already seeing changes. The Florida Department of Transportation revoked permits for automated license plate readers on state highway rights-of-way, requiring their removal from those locations. Lucie also voted to remove 18 of its 53 Flock cameras. But for Greer, taking down some cameras isn't enough. When Bente pointed out that Port St. Lucie was already removing cameras, Greer argued that voluntary decisions can be reversed by future administrations. "The end result is to get a consent decree, where the city and Flock agrees to pull the cameras forever," he said. His amended lawsuit seeks a declaration that the city's surveillance program violates constitutional protections and an injunction restricting operation of the network or national data sharing without a warrant supported by probable cause. It also seeks disputed public records, statutory damages under federal privacy law and litigation costs. Greer told the I-Team that his primary goal is a binding court order, not a financial payout. "I'm not running for office. I'm not seeking attention," he said. "It's my way of doing something." The lawsuit still faces significant legal hurdles, including potential motions to dismiss. A federal judge has not ruled that Port St. Lucie's camera program violates the Constitution. Greer says he's willing to accept help from an attorney, but for now, he's prepared to continue the fight himself. "You cannot have this technology and not violate the Fourth Amendment. There's no way around it," he said. "You've got to get rid of it.

entry.title: Treasure Coast travelers say limited transportation options make it 'difficult to get around'
entry.summary: A recent change to a flight out of Vero Beach is sparking a bigger conversation about travel options on the Treasure Coast. Travelers tell WPTV limited flight schedules and a lack of convenient transportation alternatives can make getting in and out of the area difficult, sometimes forcing them to drive to larger airports or rearrange their plans. WATCH: Why Treasure Coast travelers say they need more options At the Vero Beach Regional Airport, travelers shared their frustrations with WPTV reporter Brooke Chau about the challenges of getting where they need to go. In the Treasure Coast area, Vero Beach specifically, it is difficult to get around, said Peter Masella. He pointed to the lack of a Brightline station in Vero Beach, saying people often have to travel to other cities to access additional transportation options. A recent schedule change to Breeze Airways' route between Vero Beach and the New York area has added to those concerns. The flight, which previously departed Vero Beach in the evening, now leaves in the morning. A New York City physician told WPTV the change has affected his work schedule. Im a physician working in New York City and because of the change of flight for Vero Beach, I have had to rearrange my patients schedule two days in a row, he said. Another traveler from Westchester, New York said the change can mean a longer trip. Then I have to take a taxi all the way down and around to Vero Beach. Its very inconvenient, she said. However, Breeze Airways has also been adding destinations from Vero Beach. Last month, the airline introduced nonstop service to Trenton, Baltimore, Pittsburgh and Atlantic City, expanding the airport's commercial flight options. Vero Beach Airport Director, Brandon Dambeck, says airlines regularly evaluate the performance of their routes, which can lead to new destinations as well as schedule or route changes. All of these airlines are monitoring the routes and their gauge of success,' Dambeck said. For travelers, more destinations are welcome, but they say flight times that fit their schedules are just as important.

entry.title: Jupiter HarbourFest brings free music, food and community fun
entry.summary: Jupiter HarbourFest is returning to Harbourside Place this Friday and Saturday, offering two days of live music, local food, vendors and family-friendly fun along the Jupiter waterfront. The festival, presented by Jupiter Medical Center and organized by the Palm Beach North Chamber of Commerce, is free to attend for general admission guests this year. 'It's a great event,' said Brian of the Palm Beach North Chamber of Commerce. 'Thanks to our sponsors, we're able to put on the event for free for general admission.' In addition to free admission, attendees can purchase tickets for special experiences, including the festival's Tastings event and VIP areas. Organizers describe HarbourFest as a coastal country music festival featuring food trucks, local restaurants, vendors and performances spread across two stages. Among the participating restaurants are Tommy Bahama and the Wyndham, both of which showcased dishes ahead of the event. Tommy Bahama will offer some of its most popular menu items, including its coconut shrimp and house-made key lime pie. 'We're going to feature two dishes, kind of the fan favorites of Tommy Bahama,' said Kyle from Tommy Bahama. The Wyndham plans to feature a braised beef shank prepared with Mediterranean spices, saffron cream sauce and orzo pasta. Live music will also be a major part of the festival experience. Local band BOXELDER will perform during the event, bringing its signature sound to the waterfront celebration. Festival organizers say HarbourFest aims to combine music, food and community while highlighting the businesses, restaurants and attractions that make Jupiter a popular destination in northern Palm Beach County. More information, including VIP ticket options, can be found at JupiterHarbourFest.org . entry.title: LET'S HEAR IT: Okeechobee nonprofit hopes to bring Traveling Vietnam Wall to local veterans
entry.summary: At a Lets Hear It event in Okeechobee last month,, WPTV anchor and Navy veteran Mike Trim spoke with a local veteran dedicated to serving fellow vets. Gregg Maynard, an Army veteran and founder of the nonprofit Thank You For Your Service, helps disabled veterans through projects such as building wheelchair ramps and providing other assistance. WATCH: Okeechobee Traveling Vietnam Wall Now, Maynard is working to bring the Traveling Vietnam Memorial Wall to Okeechobee. He hopes the display will give local Vietnam veterans, especially those unable to travel to Washington, D.C., the opportunity to experience the memorial and reflect on their service. Not only does it help those veterans who may never make the trip to D.C., but I think these stories and what these guys went through can also be an educational experience for kids, Maynard told Trim. It gives them a chance to learn. Maynard said it costs thousands of dollars to bring the wall to the area and is raising funds through his nonprofit. Those interested in supporting the effort can contact him at thankyouforyourservice34972@gmail.com . Ultimately, Maynard hopes the memorial will have a meaningful impact on the local Vietnam veteran community. I want them to feel appreciated, Maynard said. But most importantly, if it helps just one Vietnam veteran, then all the work and effort that goes into making this happen will be worth it.

entry.title: Palm Beach Atlantic University celebrates Hispanic heritage through art, music festival
entry.summary: Palm Beach Atlantic University wrapped up its three-day Hispanic Heritage Festival on Saturday, celebrating Hispanic art, culture and music during Hispanic Heritage Month in South Florida. The annual festival featured a contemporary art exhibition and a series of musical performances designed to showcase the cultural contributions and artistic traditions of the Hispanic world. Organizers say the event continues to grow as it enters its 17th year. Palm Beach Atlantic University celebrates Hispanic heritage through art, music festival In a region with a large Hispanic population, organizers say the festival provides an opportunity for students and community members to engage with artists and musicians while learning more about the diversity of Hispanic cultures. Artists from across the Hispanic world The festival began Thursday with an art exhibition featuring artists representing more than 10 countries. Visitors viewed a wide range of artistic styles and mediums, including oil paintings, photography and metalwork. Among the featured artists was Franco Sotillo, a visual artist originally from Lima, Peru, who said his work combines mixed media and reflects both his heritage and personal experiences. 'I'm a visual artist and came from Lima, Peru,' Sotillo said. 'I moved to this country 12 years ago.' Sotillo said his work incorporates materials including oils, paper and other raw elements. He said sharing his art allows him to introduce audiences to Peruvian artistic expression. 'I'm an immigrant, but also bringing my culture to the states to show people how Peruvian art is expressed,' Sotillo said. Festival expands music offerings Festival Director Michael O'Connor said the event continues to evolve each year. 'We're expanding every year,' O'Connor said. O'Connor said this year's festival marked the first time organizers expanded programming beyond art and classical music to also include popular music from Hispanic cultures. 'What we want to do is we want to celebrate the Hispanic artistic heritage, because here in South Florida, especially, we have a very, very large Hispanic population,' O'Connor said. (CBS12) — A misplaced cellphone in a school cafeteria sparked a weapon rumor at Vero Beach High School on Monday morning, but school officials said there was no credible threat. The School District of Indian River County said a student left a cellphone in the cafeteria and rushed back to retrieve it. During the confusion, inaccurate information spread and developed into a rumor involving a weapon. Officials said the reported threat was not credible. entry.summary: Texas Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico returned to the campaign trail over the weekend after a 12-day absence that fueled speculation about his whereabouts. His opponent, Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, and other Republicans questioned Talarico's explanation that he had been home with the flu. At one point, Paxton called for 'proof of life' in a social media post questioning Talarico's whereabouts. The speculation included unsubstantiated claims circulating online that Talarico had been receiving treatment at a mental health facility in Ohio. I had the flu,' Talarico insisted in an interview with MS Now on Sunday. 'This is the craziest thing Ive ever heard. Its wild that someone can just post something on the internet and then the media just runs with it.' The rumors prompted the Lindner Center of HOPE to publicly deny that Talarico had been a patient. 'Representative James Talarico has never received treatment from Lindner Center of Hope,' Lindner Center HOPE posted on X. Talarico responded to the post by saying, 'Ive never even been to Ohio ' Over the weekend, Talarico was seen meeting with potential voters at the Austin City Limits Music Festival. He also attended a Kacey Musgraves concert in Dallas on Saturday, where he met with the country singer. The Texas Senate contest is among the most closely watched races in the country as Democrats seek their first statewide election victory in more than 30 years.

entry.article_text: Lynora's Italian restaurant, a South Florida staple that started as an 800-square-foot pizzeria in Lake Worth in 1976, is marking 50 years in business — and the family behind it is planning to grow beyond Palm Beach County.Angelo Abbenante, son of founders Raffaele and Maria Abbenante, now leads the restaurant brand, which currently has 6 locations spanning Palm Beach County from Jupiter to Boca Raton."From a little hole in the wall in Lake Worth to now we've gotten to the point where we have six locations we have about five more in the pipeline," he said.The expansion will reach beyond Palm Beach County, with Melbourne set to be next."Our next location is going to be Melbourne, Florida and then from there we're going to hit Fort Lauderdale, and then we have Wellington, Royal Palm Beach coming and then Delray," Abbenante said.The Lynora's story begins with Abbenante's parents, who emigrated from Italy and chose South Florida after his mother found the cold weather in New York unbearable."They came to Italy first and stopped in New York and my mom didn't like the cold weather so she decided to go back to Italy or move to a warmer area, so they had the opportunity to come to South Florida and they landed in Lake Worth," he said.Growing up in the family business meant no traditional weekends off."We didn't have the luxury of the typical American weekends off, this was 7 days a week, 24 hours a day, it was really just putting their feet in the ground. Working 7 days a week and really trying to build a great life for the family," Abbenante said.He worked his way through every job in the restaurant."Dishwashing, washing tables, bartending, making pizzas, working with my mom in the line, just doing whatever had to be done," Abbenante said.I reviewed an original menu, a reminder of how it all began. A large pizza was priced at $3.65 to $4.70. Many of those early dishes are still on the menu today."Yeah, we have all the same dishes from our hoagies where we use the same bread to our eggplant parmesan to our chicken and veal parmesan," Abbenante said.Reflecting on 50 years, Abbenante said family unity and commitment to quality are what have set Lynora's apart."We didn't go out on weekends you know me and my brother it was like we were working and helping mom and helping Dad and when you get to that point you think about the business a little differently - we are really united and I think that is what has made Lynora's so special for the last 50 years. Is when you walk into these restaurants…you get that energy and you get that homemade food. And everything is made with love so it's been a great run and we're looking forward to the next 50 years," Abbenante said.The recipes have remained true to their origins, with bread, pasta, and sauces still made in-house."It really brings us back to how it all started right and the food has been the same, we still make our own bread we still make our own pasta and all the dishes we have created have really been from our mom the sauces," Abbenante said.Among Lynora's most distinctive preparations is its signature sauce."One of the things that is really true to us is how our sauces are made our sauces still take 8 hours to make," Abbenante said.The restaurant's famous meatballs carry the same recipes as when Lynora's first opened."These are actually the same recipes that my mom started 50 years ago, you can kind of see our sauce is a little different than most restaurants... our flavors are basically built into the sauce and our meatballs you know they really speak for themselves," Abbenante said.Quality and consistency, Abbenante says, are the foundation of the restaurant's longevity."It's about making sure that we have the quality ingredients, highest quality, and when you make the food - you have to make sure it's done consistent year in and year out, day in and day out, and when you do that, that's the secret sauce," Abbenante said.Each Lynora's location is designed to reflect the personality of its community."So, when you're Jupiter you get that little feel of Jupiter and when you're in Boca you get that feel of Boca," Abbenante said.Lynora's pizza is made in a wood-burning oven using a hybrid style that blends New York and classic Italian techniques."So we do a mixture of New York style and classic Napoletano pizza and so it's a hybrid and the reason we do that is, because of our oven - our oven is not a gas oven it's a wood burning oven," Abbenante said. "We cook our pizzas typically between 700 to 800 degrees."During a demonstration, Abbenante chose his personal favorite to make."So, we're going to make my favorite which is a classic it's Margherita," he said.Community support, Abbenante says, has been a key ingredient in the restaurant's success."Without the community giving us the support we have we wouldn't be where we're at," he said.As Lynora's enters its next chapter, Abbenante says what it takes has never changed."At the end of the day it's a lot of work a lot of sacrifice it's all the little things it's very meticulous and you have to love it. But Rochon said that timing didn’t render the lawsuit moot and ordered the government to halt any further airings as of 6:45 p.m. ET.Earlier, the government said in a filing to the court that it has already spent $19 million in taxpayer money on the ads.The administration allocated $20 million for the ads, which were classified as “public service announcements,” from US Customs and Border Protection, CNN previously reported. An advertising company, LMD Agency Inc., “purchased media buys under the terms of the Order through Sunday, October 11, 2026, at an approximate cost of $19,000,000,” senior Department of Homeland Security official Holly Mehringer said in a sworn declaration in the case.The Department of Homeland Security, which includes CBP, directed LMD “to not make any additional media buys past October 11,” she added. Watchdog groups, including the nonprofit, nonpartisan Common Cause, said the ads mark a clear violation of appropriations law restricting the use of federal funding for propaganda or partisan communications. Common Cause and the Democratic National Committee separately sued the Trump administration over the ads.In a response to the Common Cause lawsuit, the Justice Department said in a filing late Saturday that an effort to halt the spending should be denied because the ads “will not continue past tomorrow.”The judge’s order Sunday would block any further ad buys for two weeks, so if the administration does consider resuming the ad campaign at taxpayer expense, DOJ lawyers would need to get the court order lifted.The coalition that brought the suit praised the judge’s order, writing, “We are pleased the court acted swiftly to prevent more taxpayer dollars from being used for such blatantly unlawful political propaganda.”CNN previously reported that Trump has personally driven the video ads, including helping select the imagery and videos used, according to a source familiar with the matter. messaging — though at least one of them was produced by a pro-Trump meme group.RELATED STORY | Trump defends ad, says MAGA Inc. will cover cost instead of taxpayersMehringer, in the court filing, entry.article_text: A legal battle has erupted in Martin County as the developer behind a massive data center project files a sprawling lawsuit against the Village of Indiantown, its village council, planning board, and local residents. Silver Fox 606 LLC filed the complaint and verified petition for a writ of prohibition, claiming local officials are illegally derailing its $25 million project. Silver Fox purchased the over 600-acre property at 13820 SW Silver Fox Lane in 2025 following zoning verifications confirming that computer and data processing facilities were permitted as an as-of-right use in Heavy Industrial districts. Following the 2026 municipal elections, a newly sworn-in village council attempted to stall or ban data center developments despite what the lawsuit alleges were prior municipal marketing efforts that actively recruited similar tech infrastructure. See also: ICU nurse accused of taking fentanyl from critically ill patient at PSL hospital Indiantown's Community and Economic Development Director administratively approved the Silver Fox plat on September 17. The lawsuit highlights a turbulent political climate, pointing to a September 1 emergency council meeting where the village manager and long-serving village attorney were ousted. Shortly after, an administrative appeal was filed by a local resident seeking to overturn the director's approvals. Silver Fox's legal team argues that the planning, zoning, and appeals board lacks the legal jurisdiction to review the plat approval, citing state statutes rendering recorded plats unassailable without landowner consent. Furthermore, the suit alleges that the Village Council violated Florida's Sunshine Law during the abrupt personnel changes. The developer is seeking emergency injunctive relief, a preliminary injunction halting any stop-work orders or retroactive reviews, and declaratory judgments affirming its vested development rights.

entry.title: 'I had the flu': Talarico returns to campaign trail, dismisses online rumors
entry.summary: Texas Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico returned to the campaign trail over the weekend after a 9-day absence that fueled speculation about his whereabouts. His opponent, Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, and other Republicans questioned Talarico's explanation that he had been home with the flu. At one point, Paxton called for 'proof of life' in a social media post questioning Talarico's whereabouts. The speculation included unsubstantiated claims circulating online that Talarico had been receiving treatment at a mental health facility in Ohio. I had the flu,' Talarico insisted in an interview with MS Now on Sunday. 'This is the craziest thing Ive ever heard. Its wild that someone can just post something on the internet and then the media just runs with it.' The rumors prompted the Lindner Center of HOPE to publicly deny that Talarico had been a patient. 'Representative James Talarico has never received treatment from Lindner Center of Hope,' Lindner Center HOPE posted on X. Talarico responded to the post by saying, 'Ive never even been to Ohio ' Over the weekend, Talarico was seen meeting with potential voters at the Austin City Limits Music Festival. He also attended a Kacey Musgraves concert in Dallas on Saturday, where he met with the country singer. The Texas Senate contest is among the most closely watched races in the country as Democrats seek their first statewide election victory in more than 30 years.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie ICU nurse arrested on charges involving patient's IV - WPBF
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie ICU nurse arrested on charges involving patient's IV    WPBF
entry.article_text: A 54-year-old Jupiter woman is facing felony charges after she allegedly removed fentanyl from a critically ill patient's IV infusion while working at Cleveland Clinic Tradition Hospital, the Port St. Lucie Police Department said Monday. On Thursday, Leslie Pope was arrested in Jupiter in conjunction with the Palm Beach Marshals Task Force and faces three felonies: grand theft of a controlled substance, possession of a controlled substance without a prescription and fraudulently obtaining a controlled substance. Pope was booked into the Palm Beach County Jail on Thursday morning on an out-of-county warrant. She was released on Saturday morning after posting an original bond of $150,000. Pope is not an inmate at the St. "We take these allegations very seriously," Cleveland Clinic spokeswoman Rebecca Astorga told WPBF in a statement. "She individual no longer works with us, and we are fully cooperating with law enforcement. Because this is an active investigation, we are unable to comment further at this time." https://www.facebook.com/PortStLuciePolice/posts/pfbid02W5HqPQihHo4JSGqHsePU1wjBMmTubGN5HyptojT8wtSJU5Pft8YBVYsKgckEN7mDl Port St. Lucie police arrested Pope after an investigation into the allegations. Investigators learned a family member reported witnessing Pope use a syringe to withdraw fluid from the patient's fentanyl infusion, place the syringe in her pocket and leave the room. Pope was not assigned to the patient's care. The next evening, Pope allegedly returned to the patient's room and again approached the IV equipment, police said. The family member intervened. Detectives later reviewed video footage that shows Pope manipulating protective caps on the equipment. No additional medication was removed during the second incident, according to investigators. A 15-page arrest affidavit includes witness interviews, hospital video footage, medical and administrative records, medication transaction reviews and coordination with the Drug Enforcement Administration. "PSLPD takes allegations of criminal misconduct seriously, particularly when they involve individuals entrusted with the safety and well-being of others," the agency said in a news release. "We remain committed to thorough, evidence-based investigations and pursuing accountability when the evidence supports criminal charges." This remains an active criminal case. "Cleveland Clinic doesn’t comment on caregivers," spokeswoman Rebecca Astorga told WPBF. entry.article_text: Police are searching for a hit-and-run cargo van driver accused of fatally striking a man riding a gas scooter before he crashed into a nearby business and ran away in Fort Pierce. Police officers received multiple 911 calls just before 9 p.m. Sunday about a vehicle crash involving a motorcycle, which later was identified as a gas scooter, close to the intersection of Okeechobee Road and 25th Street, near HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital. A white cargo van was behind the scooter, traveling east on Okeechobee Road, Maj. Michael Santiago told WPBF's Angela Rozier at a briefing Monday afternoon. The van driver fled the scene and made a U-turn to drive in the wrong direction across the median on Okeechobee Road, but he crashed into the side of a building, the Kings Queens Unisex Salon. The man then ran from the scene. A second vehicle, a Toyota pickup truck, was also struck, but no one was injured. Police were unable to locate the suspect despite aerial and K-9 units. They are in possession of the van. Anyone with information should call the Fort Pierce Police Department at 772-462-6800 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at 800-273-8477. entry.title: Police search for driver who killed scooter rider, crashed van into Fort Pierce salon - WPEC
entry.summary: Police search for driver who killed scooter rider, crashed van into Fort Pierce salon    WPEC
entry.article_text: Fort Pierce police are searching for a driver who they say hit and killed a man riding a scooter before fleeing the scene, crashing into a salon and running away on foot Sunday night. The deadly crash happened shortly before 9 p.m. on October 11 along Okeechobee Road, just west of South 25th Street. According to Major Michael Santiago with the Fort Pierce Police Department , a man riding a scooter was stopped at a red light behind a Toyota pickup truck when a white van traveling eastbound failed to stop and struck him from behind. "That in turn led to a domino effect where the motorcyclist was ejected from the scooter itself and was thrown into the vehicle in front of the scooter," Santiago said. Lucie County Fire District officials said crews were dispatched at 8:51 p.m. and arrived four minutes later. The scooter rider was pronounced dead at the scene. No other patients were transported. But investigators say the van driver did not remain at the scene. See also: No lawyer, no law degree: Port St. Lucie man takes on Flock cameras in federal court Instead, Santiago said the driver reversed, made a U-turn, briefly traveled westbound in the eastbound lanes of Okeechobee Road, crossed the median and lost control before crashing into Kings & Queens Unisex Salon. "After he crashed into the business, he fled on foot," Santiago said. Police immediately established a perimeter and searched for the driver using K-9 units and assistance from the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office aviation unit, but were unable to locate him. By Monday afternoon, the van had been removed, but significant damage remained. Broken concrete and debris were piled outside the entrance, which was boarded up and surrounded by caution tape. Salon owner Sheila Hampton said she received a phone call about the crash and arrived to find extensive damage to her business. "They just called me at the last minute and I just seen a hole in my wall. Hampton said she was unable to open the salon Monday and was concerned about when she would be allowed to resume business. And I'm just hoping tomorrow will be a better day," she said. Despite the damage to her business, Hampton also expressed sympathy for the family of the man who died. "My condolences from King and Queen Salon. We give out our condolences to the family," she said. "This shouldn't have ever happened." Police searching for driver Santiago said witnesses described the driver as a Hispanic man wearing a dark top and light-colored pants or shorts. Investigators believe he may have been injured in the crash, based on evidence recovered at the scene. Police have recovered the van and identified its registered owner, but have not confirmed who was driving. Santiago said the registered owner lives approximately one to one-and-a-half miles from the crash scene. He also said the owner stopped communicating with investigators after officers began asking who had access to the vehicle. Police have not ruled anyone out as they continue pursuing leads. Investigators are also searching for surveillance footage that could help identify the driver. As of Monday afternoon, Santiago said they had not obtained video showing the suspect himself. "We are desperately needing the public's help in identifying who was behind the wheel of this box van," Santiago said. He urged anyone who saw the white van in the area Sunday night, recognized someone who may have been driving it or captured video of the incident to come forward. The victim's identity has not been released as police work through the family notification process. No arrest had been announced as of Monday afternoon. Anyone with information is asked to contact the Fort Pierce Police Department.

entry.title: Fort Pierce utility crews assist Panhandle recovery after Hurricane Isaias - WPBF
entry.summary: Fort Pierce utility crews assist Panhandle recovery after Hurricane Isaias    WPBF
entry.article_text: South Florida utility crews and first responders are aiding recovery efforts in Florida's Panhandle following Hurricane Isaias. On Saturday, the Fort Pierce Utilities Authority sent seven crew members and five trucks to the area to help restore power. The crew is working with Choctawhatchee Electric Cooperative, also known as CHELCO, alongside other utility companies from across Florida. They are rebuilding power lines, removing damaged equipment, and installing new transformers and distribution lines. The American Public Power Association said nearly 67,000 CHELCO customers lost power during the storm, affecting about 90% of its system. Fort Pierce Utilities said a statewide mutual-aid agreement allows utilities to quickly send crews to areas where they are most needed. This agreement has also brought outside crews to South Florida following previous hurricanes. "Because of the collaboration and the help provided by the mutual aid agreements, we're able to help each other out. And we couldn't do it on our own. It's too much damage, and it gets our customers back up in a shorter amount of time when there's power loss," said Keith Stephens, director of gas and electric for Fort Pierce Utilities Authority. The Fort Pierce crew is expected to remain in the Panhandle throughout this week or as long as the crew's assistance is required. Florida Power Light has also sent thousands of lineworkers to the Gulf Coast to help restore power. Palm Beach County Fire Rescue and Delray Beach Fire Rescue have deployed crews as well, and they are expected to assist with recovery efforts for the next two weeks.

entry.title: Driver flees after fatal motorcycle crash in Fort Pierce, police say
entry.summary: Fort Pierce police are searching for a driver who they say fled after a crash that killed a motorcyclist Sunday night. The crash happened around 8:52 p.m. near South 25th Street and Okeechobee Road. Officers responded after receiving multiple 911 calls about a crash involving a motorcycle. According to preliminary information from the Fort Pierce Police Department, a white box van traveling east on Okeechobee Road struck a blue motorcycle and attempted to leave the scene. Police said the van's driver made a U-turn in the eastbound lanes while fleeing, crossed the westbound lanes and crashed into Kings and Queens Unisex Salon at 2508 Okeechobee Road. The driver then got out of the van and fled north on foot, police said. When officers arrived, they found the motorcyclist in the outside eastbound lane of Okeechobee Road and determined the person had died. St. Lucie County Fire Rescue also responded. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office K-9 and Aviation units assisted Fort Pierce police in searching for the driver, but police said he had not been located as of Monday. Two other vehicles involved in the crash remained at the scene. Police described the driver as an adult Hispanic man wearing a dark-colored top and light-colored pants or shorts. The identity of the person killed has not been confirmed. The Fort Pierce Police Department's Traffic Homicide Unit and Crime Scene Investigations are investigating. Anyone with information about the crash or the driver's identity or whereabouts is asked to contact Fort Pierce police at 772-462-6800 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers.

entry.title: Palm Beach County faith leaders sound alarm on housing affordability crisis
entry.summary: For many working families in Palm Beach County, having a job is no longer enough to guarantee they can afford a place to live. That was the message from faith leaders and community members with People Engaged in Active Community Efforts (PEACE), who gathered Monday at St. Ann Catholic Church to call attention to the countys housing affordability crisis and urge local leaders to take action. WATCH WPTV'S COVERAGE BELOW: Palm Beach County faith leaders sound alarm on housing affordability crisis We are gathered today because across our congregations and our community, we continue to hear the same concern, said the Rev. Latifah Griffin, a PEACE board of trustees member. People who are working here are struggling to live here. PEACE is a coalition of 31 congregations across Palm Beach County. Members say conversations within their congregations reveal a growing number of residents struggling with rising rents, stagnant wages and the possibility of being priced out of the communities where they work and raise their families. Palm Beach County data underscores those concerns. According to the countys January 2025 affordable housing report, the average rent for a two-bedroom apartment increased from $1,899 in 2021 to $2,833 in 2024 a 49.2% increase in three years. The cost of buying a home has also risen. The county report found the median price of a single-family home climbed from $425,000 in late 2020 to $600,000 in late 2024, an increase of 41.2%. Nationally, Redfin reported in August 2026 that households needed an annual income of nearly $110,000 to afford a typical U.S. home. For residents working in service and other modest-wage jobs, those costs can make independent living difficult even when they work consistently. Harry Wolin shared his family's experience at Mondays gathering. He said he and his wife, who are retired and living on a fixed income, help support their adult daughter, a waitress who lives in Lake Worth. Woolen said his daughter has worked in the restaurant industry for more than 20 years, but her income is not enough to afford housing without help from her parents. Shes doing everything that weve told people theyre supposed to do: get a job, work hard, help support your family, Wolin said. And it just doesnt work given the price of housing. He said he worries about workers in similar circumstances who do not have relatives able to help them financially. What do they do if they dont have a family who can help them? Wolin asked. Wolin said hi

entry.title: Indiantown’s data center war escalates as developer takes village to court - WPEC
entry.summary: Indiantown’s data center war escalates as developer takes village to court    WPEC
entry.article_text: A legal battle has erupted in Martin County as the developer behind a massive data center project files a sprawling lawsuit against the Village of Indiantown, its village council, planning board, and local residents. Silver Fox 606 LLC filed the complaint and verified petition for a writ of prohibition, claiming local officials are illegally derailing its $25 million project. Silver Fox purchased the over 600-acre property at 13820 SW Silver Fox Lane in 2025 following zoning verifications confirming that computer and data processing facilities were permitted as an as-of-right use in Heavy Industrial districts. Following the 2026 municipal elections, a newly sworn-in village council attempted to stall or ban data center developments despite what the lawsuit alleges were prior municipal marketing efforts that actively recruited similar tech infrastructure. See also: ICU nurse accused of taking fentanyl from critically ill patient at PSL hospital Indiantown's Community and Economic Development Director administratively approved the Silver Fox plat on September 17. The lawsuit highlights a turbulent political climate, pointing to a September 1 emergency council meeting where the village manager and long-serving village attorney were ousted. Shortly after, an administrative appeal was filed by a local resident seeking to overturn the director's approvals. Silver Fox's legal team argues that the planning, zoning, and appeals board lacks the legal jurisdiction to review the plat approval, citing state statutes rendering recorded plats unassailable without landowner consent. Furthermore, the suit alleges that the Village Council violated Florida's Sunshine Law during the abrupt personnel changes. The developer is seeking emergency injunctive relief, a preliminary injunction halting any stop-work orders or retroactive reviews, and declaratory judgments affirming its vested development rights.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie ICU nurse arrested on charges involving patient's IV - WPBF
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie ICU nurse arrested on charges involving patient's IV    WPBF
entry.article_text: A 54-year-old Jupiter woman is facing felony charges after she allegedly removed fentanyl from a critically ill patient's IV infusion while working at Cleveland Clinic Tradition Hospital, the Port St. Lucie Police Department said Monday. On Thursday, Leslie Pope was arrested in Jupiter in conjunction with the Palm Beach Marshals Task Force and faces three felonies: grand theft of a controlled substance, possession of a controlled substance without a prescription and fraudulently obtaining a controlled substance. Pope was booked into the Palm Beach County Jail on Thursday morning on an out-of-county warrant. She was released on Saturday morning after posting an original bond of $150,000. Pope is not an inmate at the St. "We take these allegations very seriously," Cleveland Clinic spokeswoman Rebecca Astorga told WPBF in a statement. "She individual no longer works with us, and we are fully cooperating with law enforcement. Because this is an active investigation, we are unable to comment further at this time." https://www.facebook.com/PortStLuciePolice/posts/pfbid02W5HqPQihHo4JSGqHsePU1wjBMmTubGN5HyptojT8wtSJU5Pft8YBVYsKgckEN7mDl Port St. Lucie police arrested Pope after an investigation into the allegations. Investigators learned a family member reported witnessing Pope use a syringe to withdraw fluid from the patient's fentanyl infusion, place the syringe in her pocket and leave the room. Pope was not assigned to the patient's care. The next evening, Pope allegedly returned to the patient's room and again approached the IV equipment, police said. The family member intervened. Detectives later reviewed video footage that shows Pope manipulating protective caps on the equipment. No additional medication was removed during the second incident, according to investigators. A 15-page arrest affidavit includes witness interviews, hospital video footage, medical and administrative records, medication transaction reviews and coordination with the Drug Enforcement Administration. "PSLPD takes allegations of criminal misconduct seriously, particularly when they involve individuals entrusted with the safety and well-being of others," the police agency said in a news release. "We remain committed to thorough, evidence-based investigations and pursuing accountability when the evidence supports criminal charges." This remains an active criminal case. "Cleveland Clinic doesn’t comment on caregivers," spokeswoman Rebecca Astorga told WPBF. entry.title: Police search for driver who killed scooter rider, crashed van into Fort Pierce salon - WPEC
entry.summary: Police search for driver who killed scooter rider, crashed van into Fort Pierce salon    WPEC
entry.article_text: Fort Pierce police are searching for a driver who they say hit and killed a man riding a scooter before fleeing the scene, crashing into a salon and running away on foot Sunday night. The deadly crash happened shortly before 9 p.m. on October 11 along Okeechobee Road, just west of South 25th Street. According to Major Michael Santiago with the Fort Pierce Police Department , a man riding a scooter was stopped at a red light behind a Toyota pickup truck when a white van traveling eastbound failed to stop and struck him from behind. "That in turn led to a domino effect where the motorcyclist was ejected from the scooter itself and was thrown into the vehicle in front of the scooter," Santiago said. Lucie County Fire District officials said crews were dispatched at 8:51 p.m. and arrived four minutes later. The scooter rider was pronounced dead at the scene. No other patients were transported. But investigators say the van driver did not remain at the scene. See also: No lawyer, no law degree: Port St. Lucie man takes on Flock cameras in federal court Instead, Santiago said the driver reversed, made a U-turn, briefly traveled westbound in the eastbound lanes of Okeechobee Road, crossed the median and lost control before crashing into Kings & Queens Unisex Salon. "After he crashed into the business, he fled on foot," Santiago said. Police responded to multiple 911 calls reporting the crash around 8:42 p.m. and immediately established a perimeter, searching for the driver using K-9 units and assistance from the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office aviation unit. Despite their efforts, they were unable to locate him. Two additional vehicles involved in the crash remained at the scene, according to police. The department's Traffic Homicide Unit, Crime Scene Investigations and other personnel processed the scene as part of the ongoing investigation. By Monday afternoon, the van had been removed, but significant damage remained. Broken concrete and debris were piled outside the entrance, which was boarded up and surrounded by caution tape. Salon owner Sheila Hampton said she received a phone call about the crash and arrived to find extensive damage to her business. "They just called me at the last minute and I just seen a hole in my wall. Hampton said she was unable to open the salon Monday and was concerned about when she would be allowed to resume business. And I'm just hoping tomorrow will be a better day," she said. Despite the damage to her business, Hampton also expressed sympathy for the family of the man who died. "My condolences from King and Queen Salon. We give out our condolences to the family," she said. "This shouldn't have ever happened." Police searching for driver Santiago said witnesses described the driver as a Hispanic man wearing a dark top and light-colored pants or shorts. Investigators believe he may have been injured in the crash, based on evidence recovered at the scene. Police have recovered the van and identified its registered owner, but have not confirmed who was driving. Santiago said the registered owner lives approximately one to one-and-a-half miles from the crash scene. He also said the owner stopped communicating with investigators after officers began asking who had access to the vehicle. Police have not ruled anyone out as they continue pursuing leads. Investigators are also searching for surveillance footage that could help identify the driver. As of Monday afternoon, Santiago said they had not obtained video showing the suspect himself. "We are desperately needing the public's help in identifying who was behind the wheel of this box van," Santiago said. He urged anyone who saw the white van in the area Sunday night, recognized someone who may have been driving it or captured video of the incident to come forward. The victim's identity has not been released as police work through the family notification process. No arrest had been announced as of Monday afternoon. Anyone with information is asked to contact the Fort Pierce Police Department.

entry.title: Fort Pierce ends lease with Crabby's Dockside operator over unpaid bills - WPBF
entry.summary: Fort Pierce ends lease with Crabby's Dockside operator over unpaid bills    WPBF
entry.article_text: Fort Pierce city commissioners voted unanimously to end their lease with the former operator of Crabby's Dockside and begin searching for a new operator for the waterfront restaurant. The restaurant, located along Avenue A at the Fort Pierce Marina, closed in February. The city said its operator, Winking Starfish, owed more than $418,000 in rent, taxes, and late fees. After recalculating the balance, the city now says the amount owed is nearly $334,000. Winking Starfish identified a potential new operator for the restaurant, but city officials said the proposal sought favorable terms. City Manager Richard Chess told commissioners that the city would allow interested restaurateurs to compete for the location. The city plans to set requirements for potential operators, with the city commission making the final decision. "Our marina is very, very successful, and we're very proud of it, and that location, that Crabby's location, is a very critical part of the marina," Mayor Linda Hudson said. Chess also said during the meeting that a new agreement would combine rent and other payments into one amount, based on the property's market value. entry.title: Police search for driver who killed scooter rider, crashed van into Fort Pierce salon - WPEC
entry.summary: Police search for driver who killed scooter rider, crashed van into Fort Pierce salon    WPEC
entry.article_text: Fort Pierce police are searching for a driver who they say hit and killed a man riding a scooter before fleeing the scene, crashing into a salon and running away on foot Sunday night. The deadly crash happened shortly before 9 p.m. on October 11 along Okeechobee Road, just west of South 25th Street. According to Major Michael Santiago with the Fort Pierce Police Department , a man riding a scooter was stopped at a red light behind a Toyota pickup truck when a white van traveling eastbound failed to stop and struck him from behind. "That in turn led to a domino effect where the motorcyclist was ejected from the scooter itself and was thrown into the vehicle in front of the scooter," Santiago said. Lucie County Fire District officials said crews were dispatched at 8:51 p.m. and arrived four minutes later. The scooter rider was pronounced dead at the scene. No other patients were transported. But investigators say the van driver did not remain at the scene. See also: No lawyer, no law degree: Port St. Lucie man takes on Flock cameras in federal court Instead, Santiago said the driver reversed, made a U-turn, briefly traveled westbound in the eastbound lanes of Okeechobee Road, crossed the median and lost control before crashing into Kings & Queens Unisex Salon. "After he crashed into the business, he fled on foot," Santiago said. Police responded to multiple 911 calls reporting the crash around 8:42 p.m. and immediately established a perimeter, searching for the driver using K-9 units and assistance from the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office aviation unit. Despite their efforts, they were unable to locate him. Two additional vehicles involved in the crash remained at the scene, according to police. The department's Traffic Homicide Unit, Crime Scene Investigations and other personnel processed the scene as part of the ongoing investigation. By Monday afternoon, the van had been removed, but significant damage remained. Broken concrete and debris were piled outside the entrance, which was boarded up and surrounded by caution tape. Salon owner Sheila Hampton said she received a phone call about the crash and arrived to find extensive damage to her business. "They just called me at the last minute and I just seen a hole in my wall. Hampton said she was unable to open the salon Monday and was concerned about when she would be allowed to resume business. And I'm just hoping tomorrow will be a better day," she said. Despite the damage to her business, Hampton also expressed sympathy for the family of the man who died. "My condolences from King and Queen Salon. We give out our condolences to the family," she said. "This shouldn't have ever happened." Police searching for driver Santiago said witnesses described the driver as a Hispanic man wearing a dark top and light-colored pants or shorts. Investigators believe he may have been injured in the crash, based on evidence recovered at the scene. Police have recovered the van and identified its registered owner, but have not confirmed who was driving. Santiago said the registered owner lives approximately one to one-and-a-half miles from the crash scene. He also said the owner stopped communicating with investigators after officers began asking who had access to the vehicle. Police have not ruled anyone out as they continue pursuing leads. Investigators are also searching for surveillance footage that could help identify the driver. As of Monday afternoon, Santiago said they had not obtained video showing the suspect himself. "We are desperately needing the public's help in identifying who was behind the wheel of this box van," Santiago said. He urged anyone who saw the white van in the area Sunday night, recognized someone who may have been driving it or captured video of the incident to come forward. The victim's identity has not been released as police work through the family notification process. No arrest had been announced as of Monday afternoon. Anyone with information is asked to contact the Fort Pierce Police Department.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie family chooses organ donation after teen's death, creating hope through tragedy
entry.summary: A Port St. Lucie family is turning unimaginable loss into hope after choosing organ donation following the death of their 14-year-old son , who was struck by a vehicle while walking to school, according to police. Port St. Lucie police said the teen was walking along Port St. Lucie Boulevard near Squirrel Avenue on Oct. 7 when he was struck from behind. He died from his injuries two days later. WATCH: Port St. Lucie Teen's Legacy Lives On Through Donation Port St. Lucie Teen's Legacy Lives On Through Donation | WPTV Now, the family's decision to donate his organs could help multiple people waiting for lifesaving transplants while creating a lasting legacy in his memory. Organ donation advocates say the family's choice highlights an ongoing need for registered donors. According to transplant advocates, more than 100,000 people nationwide are currently waiting for an organ transplant, and 15 lives are lost each day while patients remain on waiting lists. Family's decision offers hope to others The teen's family chose organ donation in the days following his death, a decision supporters say can have a profound impact on recipients and their families. 'It's a courageous thing for them to do, and I think it's the right thing,' said St. Lucie County Tax Collector Chris Craft. Craft has worked with Donate Life Florida through the tax collector's office to encourage organ donor registration and raise awareness about the need for donors. Transplant recipient shares personal perspective For Tyre Gray, a kidney transplant recipient and the chief administrative and legal officer for South Florida Donor Network, the family's decision carries special meaning. 'Organ donation is one of the few places where grief and gratitude exist in the same place,' Gray told WPTV. Gray said he spent five years waiting for a kidney transplant before receiving the life-saving organ he needed. 'I know for a fact that I wouldn't be here without a family making that election in their deepest moment of despair,' he said. Gray described years of uncertainty while waiting for a match. 'That's five years of uncertainty, five years of being paralyzed, five years of not being able to grow,' he said. entry.title: 'I had the flu': Talarico returns to campaign trail, dismisses online rumors
entry.summary: Texas Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico returned to the campaign trail over the weekend after a 9-day absence that fueled speculation about his whereabouts. His opponent, Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, and other Republicans questioned Talarico's explanation that he had been home with the flu. Talarico returns to the campaign trail, and midterm spending heats up At one point, Paxton called for 'proof of life' in a social media post questioning Talarico's whereabouts. The speculation included unsubstantiated claims circulating online that Talarico had been receiving treatment at a mental health facility in Ohio. I had the flu,' Talarico insisted in an interview with MS Now on Sunday. 'This is the craziest thing Ive ever heard. Its wild that someone can just post something on the internet and then the media just runs with it.' The rumors prompted the Lindner Center of HOPE to publicly deny that Talarico had been a patient. 'Representative James Talarico has never received treatment from Lindner Center of Hope,' Lindner Center HOPE posted on X. Talarico responded to the post by saying, 'Ive never even been to Ohio ' Over the weekend, Talarico was seen meeting with potential voters at the Austin City Limits Music Festival. He also attended a Kacey Musgraves concert in Dallas on Saturday, where he met with the country singer. The Texas Senate contest is among the most closely watched races in the country as Democrats seek their first statewide election victory in more than 30 years.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie ICU nurse arrested on charges involving patient's IV - WPBF
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie ICU nurse arrested on charges involving patient's IV    WPBF
entry.article_text: A 54-year-old Jupiter woman is facing felony charges after she allegedly removed fentanyl from a critically ill patient's IV infusion while working at Cleveland Clinic Tradition Hospital, the Port St. Lucie Police Department said Monday. On Thursday, Leslie Pope was arrested in Jupiter in conjunction with the Palm Beach Marshals Task Force and faces three felonies: grand theft of a controlled substance, possession of a controlled substance without a prescription and fraudulently obtaining a controlled substance. Pope was booked into the Palm Beach County Jail on Thursday morning on an out-of-county warrant. She was released on Saturday morning after posting an original bond of $150,000. Pope is not an inmate at the St. "We take these allegations very seriously," Cleveland Clinic spokeswoman Rebecca Astorga told WPBF in a statement. "She individual no longer works with us, and we are fully cooperating with law enforcement. Because this is an active investigation, we are unable to comment further at this time." https://www.facebook.com/PortStLuciePolice/posts/pfbid02W5HqPQihHo4JSGqHsePU1wjBMmTubGN5HyptojT8wtSJU5Pft8YBVYsKgckEN7mDl Port St. Lucie police arrested Pope after an investigation into the allegations. Investigators learned a family member reported witnessing Pope use a syringe to withdraw fluid from the patient's fentanyl infusion, place the syringe in her pocket and leave the room. Pope was not assigned to the patient's care. The next evening, Pope allegedly returned to the patient's room and again approached the IV equipment, police said. The family member intervened. Detectives later reviewed video footage that shows Pope manipulating protective caps on the equipment. No additional medication was removed during the second incident, according to investigators. A 15-page arrest affidavit includes witness interviews, hospital video footage, medical and administrative records, medication transaction reviews and coordination with the Drug Enforcement Administration. "PSLPD takes allegations of criminal misconduct seriously, particularly when they involve individuals entrusted with the safety and well-being of others," the police agency said in a news release. "We remain committed to thorough, evidence-based investigations and pursuing accountability when the evidence supports criminal charges." This remains an active criminal case. "Cleveland Clinic doesn’t comment on caregivers," spokeswoman Rebecca Astorga told WPBF. entry.title: Van driver sought after fleeing fatal crash involving scooter in Fort Pierce - WPBF
entry.summary: Van driver sought after fleeing fatal crash involving scooter in Fort Pierce    WPBF
entry.article_text: Police are searching for a hit-and-run cargo van driver accused of fatally striking a man riding a gas scooter before he crashed into a nearby business and ran away in Fort Pierce. Police officers received multiple 911 calls just before 9 p.m. Sunday about a vehicle crash involving a motorcycle, which later was identified as a gas scooter, close to the intersection of Okeechobee Road and 25th Street, near HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital. A white cargo van was behind the scooter, traveling east on Okeechobee Road, Maj. Michael Santiago told WPBF's Angela Rozier at a briefing Monday afternoon. The van driver fled the scene and made a U-turn to drive in the wrong direction across the median on Okeechobee Road, but he crashed into the side of a building, the Kings Queens Unisex Salon. The man then ran from the scene. Salon owner Sheila Hampton showed the damage, and is thankful no one was inside at the time. Hampton said she feels for the victim and his family. "His family told me he was just leaving from one of his friend's houses and just going home," she said. A second vehicle, a Toyota pickup truck, was also struck, but no one was injured. Lucie County Sheriff's Office K-9 Unit and Aviation Unit assisted Fort Pierce police and the K-9 Unit in efforts to locate the driver. They are in possession of the van. Police described the driver as a Hispanic man wearing a dark-colored top with light-colored pants or shorts. "So, that in itself proves intent that that person knew exactly what they were doing at the time and was just trying to simply get away," Santiago said. Anyone with information should call the Fort Pierce Police Department at 772-462-6800 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at 800-273-8477. Stay up-to-date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25

entry.title: Port St. Lucie city council approves site plan for Costco
entry.summary: On Monday, Port St. Lucie City Council approved three major site plans for projects along the Southern Grove, a developing jobs corridor in the city. One of those plans: the long-awaited Costco retail store. 'This is something that we have been looking forward to for a long time, Scott Samples with the City of Port St. Lucie said. Samples and Wes McCurry, president and CEO of St. Lucie County Economic Development Council said the 163,000-square-foot store is just the beginning for a new phase of growth in western Port St. Lucie. 'This is getting closer to the finish line, Samples said. The Costco will join other companies like Amazon, Tamco and Cheney Brothers, calling the Southern Grove area home. McCurry said since the jobs are now here, new commercial development will follow. 'They see all the all the development that's occurring here, along with the demographics that they like to see, said McCurry. It only makes sense that Costco opens a retail store here.' City council approved two other major site plans for the area, including a 5.5-acre site making up the first phase of the Tradition Entertainment District set to bring restaurants and retail. This area has historically been largely under-served by restaurants and retail, and especially entertainment facilities, McCurry said. It's kind of catching up to the rooftops that are happening. You know, rooftops always drive that demand, but there's more to come. The other plan is space for an acute care rehabilitation hospital, featuring inpatient and outpatient services with 42 beds in a more than 55 thousand square foot building. 'Growing area needs services, and that's just another component of services that are coming into the area is expanded healthcare access, McCurry said. McCurry said the plans for retail, healthcare and entertainment is fulfilling the citys master plan for what Southern Grove was destined to become. 'The plan is coming together. The vision is coming together. What everyone saw 20 years ago is now starting to happen, McCurry said. Samples said Costco still must close on the land, move on to construction design planning and permitting before any shovels hit the ground.

entry.title: ATF drops registration requirements for suppressors, short-barreled firearms
entry.summary: The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives announced Friday it will no longer enforce National Firearms Act registration and approval requirements for suppressors, short-barreled rifles and short-barreled shotguns. The move eliminates what was often a months-long process that required buyers to obtain federal approval, register the items with the government and pay a tax stamp before taking possession. Federal background checks are still required. For firearm retailers in West Palm Beach, the change is already having an impact. At We Kick Brass, owner Mike Perez said customers previously had to navigate a lengthy approval process to legally purchase suppressors and certain firearms regulated under the National Firearms Act. 'People were legally able to own these firearms,' Perez said. 'They just had to wait a longer process. It had to get ATF approval.' ATF drops registration requirements for suppressors, short-barreled firearmsWhat changed? For decades, suppressors and short-barreled rifles and shotguns were subject to National Firearms Act requirements that included registration, federal approval and a tax stamp. The ATF announced Friday it will no longer enforce those requirements for those items. The move follows a federal court ruling in Texas involving National Firearms Act registration requirements and comes after Congress reduced the tax stamp fee from $200 to zero. Perez said the biggest change is the amount of paperwork buyers no longer have to complete. 'The biggest change is less paperwork,' Perez said. 'It's a lot easier for someone to come in here and purchase a firearm and feel safe about it and secure about it.' He said some customers who once faced waits stretching nine months, 14 months or longer may now be able to take possession much sooner. 'They no longer have to wait 14 months, or nine months, or even more than a day if they have a concealed weapon firearm permit,' Perez said. In 2018, he was involved in a self-defense shooting in which he used one."I used a short-barreled rifle to save my mother's life," Perez said. "They are just simply put the best and most effective tools."Asked what could happen if a future administration attempted to reverse the policy, Perez said he believes current owners would likely be protected."I imagine that they would be grandfathered in," Perez said. "You can't make millions of Americans felons overnight by the flick of a pen. It just makes no sense."The ATF's policy change does not eliminate all National Firearms Act regulations.Machine guns and destructive devices, including bombs, rockets and grenades, remain subject to federal requirements.Customers purchasing firearms must also continue to undergo background checks and comply with all applicable federal and state laws.For those concerned about expanded access to suppressors and short-barreled firearms, Perez said the changes affect law-abiding citizens."We are just allowing people, law-abiding citizens, the ability to protect themselves with the right firearm to do so," Perez said.Florida gun owners should also be aware that state law prohibits short-barreled rifles and short-barreled shotguns unless they are lawfully owned under federal law. entry.title: Indiantown’s data center war escalates as developer takes village to court - WPEC
entry.summary: Indiantown’s data center war escalates as developer takes village to court    WPEC
entry.article_text: A legal battle has erupted in Martin County as the developer behind a massive data center project files a sprawling lawsuit against the Village of Indiantown, its village council, planning board, and local residents. Silver Fox 606 LLC filed the complaint and verified petition for a writ of prohibition, claiming local officials are illegally derailing its $25 million project. Silver Fox purchased the over 600-acre property at 13820 SW Silver Fox Lane in 2025 following zoning verifications confirming that computer and data processing facilities were permitted as an as-of-right use in Heavy Industrial districts. Following the 2026 municipal elections, a newly sworn-in village council attempted to stall or ban data center developments despite what the lawsuit alleges were prior municipal marketing efforts that actively recruited similar tech infrastructure. See also: ICU nurse accused of taking fentanyl from critically ill patient at PSL hospital Indiantown's Community and Economic Development Director administratively approved the Silver Fox plat on September 17. The lawsuit highlights a turbulent political climate, pointing to a September 1 emergency council meeting where the village manager and long-serving village attorney were ousted. Shortly after, an administrative appeal was filed by a local resident seeking to overturn the director's approvals. Silver Fox's legal team argues that the planning, zoning, and appeals board lacks the legal jurisdiction to review the plat approval, citing state statutes rendering recorded plats unassailable without landowner consent. Furthermore, the suit alleges that the Village Council violated Florida's Sunshine Law during the abrupt personnel changes. The developer is seeking emergency injunctive relief, a preliminary injunction halting any stop-work orders or retroactive reviews, and declaratory judgments affirming its vested development rights.
