entry.title: Port St. Lucie family chooses organ donation after teen's death, creating hope through tragedy - WFLX
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie family chooses organ donation after teen's death, creating hope through tragedy    WFLX
entry.article_text: Lucie family is turning unimaginable loss into hope after choosing organ donation following the death of their 14-year-old son , who was struck by a vehicle while walking to school, according to police. Lucie police said the teen was walking along Port St. Lucie Boulevard near Squirrel Avenue on Oct. 7 when he was struck from behind. He died from his injuries two days later. Now, the family’s decision to donate his organs could help multiple people waiting for lifesaving transplants while creating a lasting legacy in his memory. Organ donation advocates say the family’s choice highlights an ongoing need for registered donors. According to transplant advocates, more than 100,000 people nationwide are currently waiting for an organ transplant, and 15 lives are lost each day while patients remain on waiting lists. The teen’s family chose organ donation in the days following his death, a decision supporters say can have a profound impact on recipients and their families. “It’s a courageous thing for them to do, and I think it’s the right thing,” said St. Lucie County Tax Collector Chris Craft. Craft has worked with Donate Life Florida through the tax collector’s office to encourage organ donor registration and raise awareness about the need for donors. For Tyre Gray, a kidney transplant recipient and the chief administrative and legal officer for South Florida Donor Network, the family’s decision carries special meaning. “Organ donation is one of the few places where grief and gratitude exist in the same place,” Gray told WPTV. Gray said he spent five years waiting for a kidney transplant before receiving the life-saving organ he needed. “I know for a fact that I wouldn’t be here without a family making that election in their deepest moment of despair,” he said. Gray described years of uncertainty while waiting for a match. “That’s five years of uncertainty, five years of being paralyzed, five years of not being able to grow,” he said. Organ donation advocates say the need for donors continues across Florida and the United States. Gray noted that a single donor has the potential to save multiple lives and help many more patients through tissue donation. “One donor is to save upwards of nine lives and to be able to heal another 75 lives,” Gray said. Behind those numbers are people awaiting a second chance, he said. “Let’s all be heroes and save lives,” Gray added. Advocates say organ donation often allows families to find meaning during some of life’s most difficult moments. “I would hope that they could see the lasting impact that a selfless act can make on others,” Craft said. “If you can help somebody else, it’s an amazing thing.” For transplant recipients, organ donation can mean more time with family, additional milestones and opportunities. In the midst of tragedy, one Port St. Lucie family’s decision could now help save lives and ensure their son’s legacy continues through the people he may help. entry.title: City council approves lease agreement to bring hotel to Vero Beach Regional Airport area
entry.summary: WPTV has been reporting extensively on the growth at the Vero Beach Regional Airport when it comes to flights. But on Tuesday, Vero Beach City Council approved a lease agreement to bring a four-story, 116-room Marriott hotel to the airport. 'We've been in negotiations with this for the last three years, Brian Dembeck, interim airport director, said. 'This is something that is going to dramatically improve the passenger experience.' Dembeck took WPTV to the site, which sits just outside the gates of the terminal along Aviation Boulevard. 'They're going to have a hotel right next door that they can come, they can stay, wait for their flight, and then go right over to the terminal.' But the lodging is more than just for passengers. Brian Cartland, vice-president of economic development for the Indian River County Chamber of Commerce, said the hotel could attract more businesses to the city of Vero Beach and beyond. 'The hotel is going to serve multiple purposes, said Cartland. 'This hotel is going to help target industry growth by giving those companies that are looking at the area some additional alternatives for some great high-end options.' While the hotel is close to the airport, Chad Maxey, senior vice president of Diversified Companies, the developer of the project, said one big need for the extra lodging is just down the street at the Jackie Robinson Training Complex. 'We feel this is a great location to have a hotel that's going to be able to provide amenities to the airport and also to the families and kids that are going to play baseball, Maxey said. Maxey said the hotel will also feature a homerun dugout amenity for families. 'Kids can play virtual baseball in the hotel as they're getting ready to go across the street and actually hit the diamond over there and play with the major league baseball players, Maxey said. Developers said the hotel will break ground next year and expected to be completed by end of 2028.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie city council approves site plan for Costco
entry.summary: On Monday, Port St. Lucie City Council approved three major site plans for projects along the Southern Grove, a developing jobs corridor in the city. One of those plans: the long-awaited Costco retail store. WATCH BELOW: Port St. Lucie City Council approves site plan for Costco Port St Lucie approves site plan for Costco 'This is something that we have been looking forward to for a long time, Scott Samples with the City of Port St. Lucie said. Samples and Wes McCurry, president and CEO of the St. Lucie County Economic Development Council, said the 163,000-square-foot store is just the beginning for a new phase of growth in western Port St. Lucie. 'This is getting closer to the finish line,' Samples said. The Costco will join other companies like Amazon, Tamco and Cheney Brothers, calling the Southern Grove area home. McCurry said since the jobs are now here, new commercial development will follow. 'They see all the development that's occurring here, along with the demographics that they like to see, said McCurry. 'It only makes sense that Costco opens a retail store here.' City council approved two other major site plans for the area, including a 5.5-acre site making up the first phase of the Tradition Entertainment District set to bring restaurants and retail. 'This area has historically been largely underserved by restaurants and retail, and especially entertainment facilities, McCurry said. 'It's kind of catching up to the rooftops that are happening. You know, rooftops always drive that demand, but there's more to come.' The other plan is space for an acute care rehabilitation hospital, featuring inpatient and outpatient services with 42 beds in a more than 55,000-square-foot building. 'A growing area needs services, and that's just another component of services that are coming into the area is expanded healthcare access,' McCurry said. McCurry said the plans for retail, healthcare and entertainment are fulfilling the citys master plan for what Southern Grove was destined to become. 'The plan is coming together. The vision is coming together. What everyone saw 20 years ago is now starting to happen,' McCurry said. Samples said Costco still must close on the land, move on to construction design planning and permitting before any shovels hit the ground.

entry.title: Martin County moves closer to restoring bus services after sudden shutdown - WPBF
entry.summary: Martin County moves closer to restoring bus services after sudden shutdown    WPBF
entry.article_text: Just days after MARTY public bus services abruptly shut down in Martin County, county commissioners voted unanimously Tuesday to allow the county administrator to negotiate a new contract with a company that could restore service. The vote gives county administration the green light to begin negotiations with MTM Transit, a company that previously operated the county’s public bus system. For former MARTY bus driver Bill Lawrence, Tuesday’s decision offered a sign of hope after he and several other drivers suddenly lost their jobs last Thursday. “I’m hoping that we get this back on the road soon. We need our employees, our drivers, to get back to work,” Lawrence said. Lawrence was among the drivers impacted when Martin County Transit LLC, the company previously operating MARTY, abruptly stopped services last Thursday. The company cited rising operating costs, including fuel and maintenance, as reasons for its decision to discontinue service. During Tuesday’s county commission meeting, Martin County Public Works Director Jim Gorton explained that county officials had spent the past several days exploring options to restore service. “We reached out to a number of vendors; a number of vendors reached out to us,” Gorton said. According to Gorton, the county evaluated several proposals before identifying MTM Transit as its preferred option. Under the county’s emergency procurement rules, the proposed agreement would be a one-year contract costing approximately $3 million. During that year, county officials would work toward establishing a standard multi-year contract through the county’s normal competitive bidding process. One of the county’s priorities during negotiations is bringing back the drivers who lost their jobs following last week’s shutdown. “We absolutely want to use those same drivers and get them back to work as quickly as possible,” Gorton said. Commissioners also authorized county administration to move forward with terminating its previous contract with Martin County Transit LLC. County officials say they are hopeful negotiations with MTM Transit can be finalized by the end of this week, potentially allowing buses to begin operating again next week. entry.article_text: Fort Pierce police are searching for a driver who they say hit and killed a man riding a scooter before fleeing the scene, crashing into a salon and running away on foot Sunday night. The deadly crash happened shortly before 9 p.m. on October 11 along Okeechobee Road, just west of South 25th Street. According to Major Michael Santiago with the Fort Pierce Police Department , a man riding a scooter was stopped at a red light behind a Toyota pickup truck when a white van traveling eastbound failed to stop and struck him from behind. "That in turn led to a domino effect where the motorcyclist was ejected from the scooter itself and was thrown into the vehicle in front of the scooter," Santiago said. Obtained 911 recordings capture the frantic moments following the crash. In one call, a person inside the Toyota pickup truck described the aftermath. "We got hit, and it's like, there's blood all over our car," the caller told a dispatcher. Another caller reported seeing the white van crash into the nearby building while trying to get away. Lucie County Fire District officials said crews were dispatched at 8:51 p.m. and arrived four minutes later. The scooter rider was pronounced dead at the scene. No other patients were transported. But investigators say the van driver did not remain at the scene. See also: No lawyer, no law degree: Port St. Lucie man takes on Flock cameras in federal court Instead, Santiago said the driver reversed, made a U-turn, briefly traveled westbound in the eastbound lanes of Okeechobee Road, crossed the median and lost control before crashing into Kings & Queens Unisex Salon. "After he crashed into the business, he fled on foot," Santiago said. According to a police news release, the driver ran northbound after crashing into the salon, located at 2508 Okeechobee Road. Police responded to multiple 911 calls reporting the crash around 8:52 p.m. and immediately established a perimeter, searching for the driver using K-9 units and assistance from the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office aviation unit. Despite their efforts, they were unable to locate him. Two additional vehicles involved in the crash remained at the scene, according to police. The department's Traffic Homicide Unit, Crime Scene Investigations and other personnel processed the scene as part of the ongoing investigation. By Monday afternoon, the van had been removed, but significant damage remained. Broken concrete and debris were piled outside the entrance, which was boarded up and surrounded by caution tape. Salon owner Sheila Hampton said she received a phone call about the crash and arrived to find extensive damage to her business. "They just called me at the last minute and I just seen a hole in my wall. Hampton said she was unable to open the salon Monday and was concerned about when she would be allowed to resume business. And I'm just hoping tomorrow will be a better day," she said. Despite the damage to her business, Hampton also expressed sympathy for the family of the man who died. "My condolences from King and Queen Salon. We give out our condolences to the family," she said. "This shouldn't have ever happened." Police searching for driver Santiago said witnesses described the driver as a Hispanic man wearing a dark top and light-colored pants or shorts. Investigators believe he may have been injured in the crash, based on evidence recovered at the scene. Police have recovered the van and identified its registered owner, but have not confirmed who was driving. Santiago said the registered owner lives approximately one to one-and-a-half miles from the crash scene. He also said the owner stopped communicating with investigators after officers began asking who had access to the vehicle. Police have not ruled anyone out as they continue pursuing leads. Investigators are also searching for surveillance footage that could help identify the driver. As of Monday afternoon, Santiago said they had not obtained video showing the suspect himself. "We are desperately needing the public's help in identifying who was behind the wheel of this box van," Santiago said. He urged anyone who saw the white van in the area Sunday night, recognized someone who may have been driving it or captured video of the incident to come forward. Police said the victim's identity had not yet been confirmed as of Monday, and confirmation was still pending before next of kin could be notified. No arrest had been announced as of Monday afternoon. Anyone with information about the crash or the driver's whereabouts is asked to contact the Fort Pierce Police Department at 772-462-6800 or submit a tip through Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers .

entry.title: Martin County approves emergency transit plan to restore MARTY bus service after abrupt shutdown
entry.summary: Martin County commissioners have approved emergency measures aimed at restoring MARTY bus service after an abrupt shutdown last week left hundreds of riders without transportation and dozens of drivers without jobs. County leaders voted Tuesday to terminate their contract with Martin County Transit and begin negotiating an emergency one-year operating agreement with MTM Transit, a company that previously operated the county's transit system. WATCH: Martin County moves to restore MARTY buses Martin County moves to restore MARTY bus service The move comes as the county works to quickly restore public transportation service for residents who rely on MARTY buses to get to work, medical appointments and other essential destinations. County moves forward with emergency contract The emergency action follows last week's sudden shutdown of MARTY bus service, which county officials say disrupted transportation across the community. 'We're doing it under our emergency procurement rules, and we will have a one-year contract,' said Martin County Public Works Director Jim Gorton. The proposed agreement with MTM Transit would serve as a temporary solution while county leaders develop a longer-term plan for public transportation service. County officials say restoring service is a top priority. 'The next vendor needs to have a contract to be able to hire the drivers back,' Gorton said. Drivers hope to return to work The shutdown has created uncertainty for employees who suddenly found themselves without work. 'It was shocking. This company has pulled out and left 28 employees unemployed, and not knowing what tomorrow is going to be like is very devastating,' said Joey Acevedo, president of ATU Local 1577. Former MARTY bus driver Bill Lawrence said workers are eager to get back behind the wheel and resume serving the community. 'I'm very hopeful. I've always been hopeful. We have people behind us that give us hope,' Lawrence said. entry.title: Barack Obama to campaign with Ohio Democrats as he expands his outreach ahead of Election Day
entry.summary: Former President Barack Obama is heading to Ohio to shore up support for Democratic candidates in the Senate and governor's races, both of which have been highly competitive and brought a flood of campaign cash into the state. Obama is set to campaign in Cleveland on Oct. 24 with three-term former Sen. Sherrod Brown, who is looking to oust Republican Sen. Jon Husted from the seat formerly held by Vice President JD Vance. He's also set to appear with Dr. Amy Acton, the Democratic nominee for governor, who has been focusing her campaign on parts of the state that have been voting Republican in recent elections. She and tech billionaire and former presidential candidate Vivek Ramaswamy are vying to succeed term-limited Republican Gov. Mike DeWine. entry.title: St. Lucie County fire chief faces calls to resign after overwhelming no-confidence vote
entry.summary: A St. Lucie County Fire District board member is calling on Fire Chief Jeff Lee to resign after firefighters delivered an overwhelming vote of no confidence in district leadership, the latest fallout from a hazing investigation that led to the firing of three veteran firefighters. More than 74% of firefighters who participated in the union vote said they had no confidence in Lee. About 92% said they had no confidence in Assistant Chief Brian Gonzalez, while 97% said the same of district attorney Kim Sabol. 'They've sent their message, and now it's, again, up for the board to take action.' When investigative reporter Kate Hussey asked whether he believed that action should include Lee's resignation, Clasby said yes. 'I don't know how you could possibly recover from getting such an overwhelming vote of no confidence,' he said. Vote follows hazing investigation The vote is the latest fallout from an investigation earlier this year into videos involving firefighters at Station 1A. A third-party investigator concluded the videos depicted hazing. One showed firefighters using a modified bug zapper to shock probationary employees. Veteran firefighters Doug Boudrias, Jordan Hutchinson and Chris Baldwin were fired following the investigation. The three have maintained the activity was consensual and 'all in good fun.' 'It was just us in our downtime, joking around, having fun,' Hutchinson previously told WPTV. 'We're all still friends,' Boudrias said. Their terminations sparked pushback from firefighters and members of the community, which eventually led to the union's no-confidence vote. 'The amount that voted no confidence really sends a message that we have, in their opinion, a lack of confidence in their leadership,' union representative Ryan Sapp said. Sapp is representing the three firefighters in their fight for reinstatement. entry.title: City council approves lease agreement to bring hotel to Vero Beach Regional Airport area
entry.summary: WPTV has been reporting extensively on the growth at the Vero Beach Regional Airport when it comes to flights. But on Tuesday, Vero Beach City Council approved a lease agreement to bring a four-story, 116-room Marriott hotel to the airport. 'We've been in negotiations with this for the last three years, Brian Dembeck, interim airport director, said. 'This is something that is going to dramatically improve the passenger experience.' Dembeck took WPTV to the site, which sits just outside the gates of the terminal along Aviation Boulevard. 'They're going to have a hotel right next door that they can come, they can stay, wait for their flight, and then go right over to the terminal.' But the lodging is more than just for passengers. Brian Cartland, vice-president of economic development for the Indian River County Chamber of Commerce, said the hotel could attract more businesses to the city of Vero Beach and beyond. 'The hotel is going to serve multiple purposes, said Cartland. 'This hotel is going to help target industry growth by giving those companies that are looking at the area some additional alternatives for some great high-end options.' While the hotel is close to the airport, Chad Maxey, senior vice president of Diversified Companies, the developer of the project, said one big need for the extra lodging is just down the street at the Jackie Robinson Training Complex. 'We feel this is a great location to have a hotel that's going to be able to provide amenities to the airport and also to the families and kids that are going to play baseball, Maxey said. Maxey said the hotel will also feature a homerun dugout amenity for families. 'Kids can play virtual baseball in the hotel as they're getting ready to go across the street and actually hit the diamond over there and play with the Major League Baseball players, Maxey said. Developers said the hotel will break ground next year and is expected to be completed by the end of 2028.

entry.title: Road back open after PBSO deputy fatally shoots robbery suspect near Boynton Beach
entry.summary: A 54-year-old man suspected of robbing a pizza delivery driver was fatally shot by a Palm Beach County sheriff's deputy Tuesday after a pursuit ended near Jog and Woolbright roads, Sheriff Ric Bradshaw said. Bradshaw said the investigation began after a pizza delivery driver was robbed around 10 p.m. Monday. The suspect allegedly ordered a pizza to a Lake Worth location and told the driver he only had a $100 bill. When the driver pulled out money to make change, the suspect allegedly grabbed him, and the two struggled over the cash. WATCH REPORT BELOW: 'Serious bad guy' shot dead near Boynton Beach, sheriff says The delivery driver provided investigators with a description of the suspect's vehicle and a license plate number, Bradshaw said. Investigators entered that information into license plate readers and received an alert Tuesday that the vehicle was in the Lake Park area. PBSO tactical units located the vehicle and conducted surveillance to confirm the registered owner was driving, according to Bradshaw. When deputies attempted a traffic stop, the driver fled, Bradshaw said. The pursuit traveled south on Interstate 95, with the Florida Highway Patrol becoming involved, before ending near Jog and Woolbright roads. Bradshaw said the driver crossed a median, apparently blew multiple tires and crashed into a fence. BREAKING NEWS: Deputy fatally shoots robbery suspect after chase PBSO deputy fatally shoots robbery suspect after chase ends near Boynton Beach A PBSO helicopter was overhead as the man got out of the vehicle and began running along Jog Road, Bradshaw said. Something was wrapped around his right hand, and deputies in the helicopter believed he might have been holding a firearm. Bradshaw said the man attempted to take cover behind concrete light poles as deputies tried to stop him using two types of less-lethal weapons. Three less-lethal rounds struck him but had no effect, according to the sheriff. Bradshaw said the man repeatedly yelled at deputies, 'You're gonna have to kill me.' When the man reached a second pole, Bradshaw said he got into a kneeling position and raised his hands in what appeared to be a shooting position. A deputy then opened fire, striking the man. He died at the scene. Bradshaw later confirmed investigators did not find a firearm on the man. entry.title: Martin County moves closer to restoring bus services after sudden shutdown - WPBF
entry.summary: Martin County moves closer to restoring bus services after sudden shutdown    WPBF
entry.article_text: Just days after MARTY public bus services abruptly shut down in Martin County, county commissioners voted unanimously Tuesday to allow the county administrator to negotiate a new contract with a company that could restore service. The vote gives county administration the green light to begin negotiations with MTM Transit, a company that previously operated the county’s public bus system. For former MARTY bus driver Bill Lawrence, Tuesday’s decision offered a sign of hope after he and several other drivers suddenly lost their jobs last Thursday. “I’m hoping that we get this back on the road soon. We need our employees, our drivers, to get back to work,” Lawrence said. Lawrence was among the drivers impacted when Martin County Transit LLC, the company previously operating MARTY, abruptly stopped services last Thursday. The company cited rising operating costs, including fuel and maintenance, as reasons for its decision to discontinue service. During Tuesday’s county commission meeting, Martin County Public Works Director Jim Gorton explained that county officials had spent the past several days exploring options to restore service. “We reached out to a number of vendors; a number of vendors reached out to us,” Gorton said. According to Gorton, the county evaluated several proposals before identifying MTM Transit as its preferred option. Under the county’s emergency procurement rules, the proposed agreement would be a one-year contract costing approximately $3 million. During that year, county officials would work toward establishing a standard multi-year contract through the county’s normal competitive bidding process. One of the county’s priorities during negotiations is bringing back the drivers who lost their jobs following last week’s shutdown. “We absolutely want to use those same drivers and get them back to work as quickly as possible,” Gorton said. Commissioners also authorized county administration to move forward with terminating its previous contract with Martin County Transit LLC. County officials say they are hopeful negotiations with MTM Transit can be finalized by the end of this week, potentially allowing buses to begin operating again next week. entry.title: Port St. Lucie nurse accused of stealing fentanyl from ICU patient’s IV bag - WPBF
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie nurse accused of stealing fentanyl from ICU patient’s IV bag    WPBF
entry.article_text: A nurse at Cleveland Clinic Tradition Hospital in Port St. Lucie is under investigation after allegedly stealing fentanyl from a critically ill patient’s IV bag on June 24 and 25, according to police. "They did an internal investigation where the Department of Health was then notified, in turn notifying PSLPD where we started our investigation in early August," said Officer Brittany McNally, public information officer for the Port St. Police said a family member of the patient reported seeing 54-year-old Leslie Pope use a syringe to withdraw fluid from the patient’s fentanyl infusion, place the syringe in her pocket, and leave the room. "That’s not standard procedure, from what I understand at the hospital," McNally said. "But again, she’s not even assigned that patient. And there was no initial justification for her to even be in that room at the time." Investigators said Pope returned the following evening and approached the IV equipment again, but the family member intervened and stopped her. Hospital video reportedly showed Pope manipulating protective caps on the IV equipment, but investigators said she did not remove any fluid during the second incident. Stay up-to-date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25 "The patient was on a specific monitor for the situation that he was in the ICU. And this individual had this monitor that had video recordings, which was a key piece of evidence in this case and completely contradicted what her recollection was," McNally said. Police said Pope denied the allegations and did not admit to using the fentanyl for personal consumption. "From my understanding, she did not admit that she was using it for personal consumption and essentially denied all the allegations that were made, but there was an overwhelming amount of evidence to prove otherwise," McNally said. Cleveland Clinic released a statement regarding the arrest, saying, "We take these allegations very seriously. The individual no longer works with us, and we are fully cooperating with law enforcement. Because this is an active investigation, we are unable to comment further at this time." The investigation remains ongoing.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie city council approves site plan for Costco - WFLX
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie city council approves site plan for Costco    WFLX
entry.article_text: Lucie City Council approved three major site plans for projects along the Southern Grove, a developing jobs corridor in the city. One of those plans: the long-awaited Costco retail store. “This is something that we have been looking forward to for a long time,” Scott Samples with the City of Port St. Samples and Wes McCurry, president and CEO of the St. Lucie County Economic Development Council, said the 163,000-square-foot store is just the beginning for a new phase of growth in western Port St. “This is getting closer to the finish line,” Samples said. The Costco will join other companies like Amazon, Tamco and Cheney Brothers, calling the Southern Grove area home. McCurry said since the jobs are now here, new commercial development will follow. “They see all the development that’s occurring here, along with the demographics that they like to see,” said McCurry. “It only makes sense that Costco opens a retail store here.” City council approved two other major site plans for the area, including a 5.5-acre site making up the first phase of the Tradition Entertainment District set to bring restaurants and retail. “This area has historically been largely underserved by restaurants and retail, and especially entertainment facilities,” McCurry said. “It’s kind of catching up to the rooftops that are happening. You know, rooftops always drive that demand, but there’s more to come.” The other plan is space for an acute care rehabilitation hospital, featuring inpatient and outpatient services with 42 beds in a more than 55,000-square-foot building. “A growing area needs services, and that’s just another component of services that are coming into the area is expanded healthcare access,” McCurry said. McCurry said the plans for retail, healthcare and entertainment are fulfilling the city’s master plan for what Southern Grove was destined to become. “The plan is coming together. The vision is coming together. What everyone saw 20 years ago is now starting to happen,” McCurry said. Samples said Costco still must close on the land, move on to construction design planning and permitting before any shovels hit the ground.

entry.title: Neighbors call for pedestrian safety after Port St. Lucie teen’s death - WPEC
entry.summary: Neighbors call for pedestrian safety after Port St. Lucie teen’s death    WPEC
entry.article_text: Lucie Boulevard say more needs to be done to protect pedestrians as construction continues on the busy road. Their concerns come after a 14-year-old Treasure Coast High School student died from injuries he suffered when he was hit by an SUV while walking to school. Police say the freshman was walking along the edge of Southwest Port St. Lucie Boulevard near Squirrel Avenue on the morning of Oct. 7 when he was struck from behind. He was pronounced clinically deceased two days later. His family chose to donate his organs . Much of the roadway remains under construction, and there are no sidewalks along large sections of the corridor. Recent heavy rain also left portions of the shoulder flooded, further limiting space for pedestrians. "He was just going to school," said neighbor Irene Ange. "He was just starting his high school year. He had the right to be safe." Irene Ange, who has lived near the boulevard for more than two decades, says students often walk or bike close to traffic, sometimes before sunrise. The stretch of road is dangerous, Ange said. It’s very dark, and drivers are not following the speed limits. Ange said she saw first responders rushing to the crash site and was heartbroken for the student and his family. See also: Suspect booked into Martin County Jail after undercover drug sting, sheriff says The teen’s mother told CBS12 by phone that her son was a people person who made friends easily. She said the family does not want this to happen to another child. The Florida Department of Transportation is widening the southern portion of Port St. Lucie Boulevard from two lanes to four and adding sidewalks on both sides of the road. FDOT says the sidewalks will be eight to 10 feet wide. The project is expected to be completed in winter 2028, with an estimated cost of about $25.6 million. CBS 12 saw crews building sidewalks several blocks from where the crash happened. FDOT did not respond to questions about what pedestrian safety measures are in place while construction continues. "No accountability with that response because now there's another death," Ange said. Ange says more needs to be done now to keep children safe on their way to school. "This did not have to happen to this family," Ange said. The family now have to mourn him." The driver initially told officers he believed he had struck a construction barrel and has been cooperating with investigators. It remains unclear whether any charges will be filed.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie family chooses organ donation after teen's death, creating hope through tragedy
entry.summary: A Port St. Lucie family is turning unimaginable loss into hope after choosing organ donation following the death of their 14-year-old son , who was struck by a vehicle while walking to school, according to police. Port St. Lucie police said the teen was walking along Port St. Lucie Boulevard near Squirrel Avenue on Oct. 7 when he was struck from behind. He died from his injuries two days later. WATCH: Port St. Lucie Teen's Legacy Lives On Through Donation Port St. Lucie Teen's Legacy Lives On Through Donation | WPTV Now, the family's decision to donate his organs could help multiple people waiting for lifesaving transplants while creating a lasting legacy in his memory. Organ donation advocates say the family's choice highlights an ongoing need for registered donors. According to transplant advocates, more than 100,000 people nationwide are currently waiting for an organ transplant, and 15 lives are lost each day while patients remain on waiting lists. Family's decision offers hope to others The teen's family chose organ donation in the days following his death, a decision supporters say can have a profound impact on recipients and their families. 'It's a courageous thing for them to do, and I think it's the right thing,' said St. Lucie County Tax Collector Chris Craft. entry.title: Martin County moves closer to restoring bus services after sudden shutdown - WPBF
entry.summary: Martin County moves closer to restoring bus services after sudden shutdown    WPBF
entry.article_text: Just days after MARTY public bus services abruptly shut down in Martin County, county commissioners voted unanimously Tuesday to allow the county administrator to negotiate a new contract with a company that could restore service. The vote gives county administration the green light to begin negotiations with MTM Transit, a company that previously operated the county’s public bus system. For former MARTY bus driver Bill Lawrence, Tuesday’s decision offered a sign of hope after he and several other drivers suddenly lost their jobs last Thursday. “I’m hoping that we get this back on the road soon. We need our employees, our drivers, to get back to work,” Lawrence said. Lawrence was among the drivers impacted when Martin County Transit LLC, the company previously operating MARTY, abruptly stopped services last Thursday. The company cited rising operating costs, including fuel and maintenance, as reasons for its decision to discontinue service. During Tuesday’s county commission meeting, Martin County Public Works Director Jim Gorton explained that county officials had spent the past several days exploring options to restore service. “We reached out to a number of vendors; a number of vendors reached out to us,” Gorton said. According to Gorton, the county evaluated several proposals before identifying MTM Transit as its preferred option. Under the county’s emergency procurement rules, the proposed agreement would be a one-year contract costing approximately $3 million. During that year, county officials would work toward establishing a standard multi-year contract through the county’s normal competitive bidding process. One of the county’s priorities during negotiations is bringing back the drivers who lost their jobs following last week’s shutdown. “We absolutely want to use those same drivers and get them back to work as quickly as possible,” Gorton said. Commissioners also authorized county administration to move forward with terminating its previous contract with Martin County Transit LLC. County officials say they are hopeful negotiations with MTM Transit can be finalized by the end of this week, potentially allowing buses to begin operating again next week. entry.title: Port St. Lucie nurse accused of stealing fentanyl from ICU patient’s IV bag - WPBF
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie nurse accused of stealing fentanyl from ICU patient’s IV bag    WPBF
entry.article_text: A nurse at Cleveland Clinic Tradition Hospital in Port St. Lucie is under investigation after allegedly stealing fentanyl from a critically ill patient’s IV bag on June 24 and 25, according to police. "They did an internal investigation where the Department of Health was then notified, in turn notifying PSLPD where we started our investigation in early August," said Officer Brittany McNally, public information officer for the Port St. Police said a family member of the patient reported seeing 54-year-old Leslie Pope use a syringe to withdraw fluid from the patient’s fentanyl infusion, place the syringe in her pocket, and leave the room. "That’s not standard procedure, from what I understand at the hospital," McNally said. "But again, she’s not even assigned that patient. And there was no initial justification for her to even be in that room at the time." Investigators said Pope returned the following evening and approached the IV equipment again, but the family member intervened and stopped her. Hospital video reportedly showed Pope manipulating protective caps on the IV equipment, but investigators said she did not remove any fluid during the second incident. Stay up-to-date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25 "The patient was on a specific monitor for the situation that he was in the ICU. And this individual had this monitor that had video recordings, which was a key piece of evidence in this case and completely contradicted what her recollection was," McNally said. Police said Pope denied the allegations and did not admit to using the fentanyl for personal consumption. "From my understanding, she did not admit that she was using it for personal consumption and essentially denied all the allegations that were made, but there was an overwhelming amount of evidence to prove otherwise," McNally said. Cleveland Clinic released a statement regarding the arrest, saying, "We take these allegations very seriously. The individual no longer works with us, and we are fully cooperating with law enforcement. Because this is an active investigation, we are unable to comment further at this time." The investigation remains ongoing.

entry.title: Van driver sought after fleeing fatal crash involving scooter in Fort Pierce - WPBF
entry.summary: Van driver sought after fleeing fatal crash involving scooter in Fort Pierce    WPBF
entry.article_text: Police are searching for a hit-and-run cargo van driver accused of fatally striking a 44-year-old man riding a gas scooter before he crashed into a nearby business and ran away in Fort Pierce. On Tuesday, the victim was identified as Andy Ramon Martinez-Pantoja. Police officers received multiple 911 calls just before 9 p.m. Sunday about a vehicle crash involving a motorcycle, which later was identified as a gas scooter, close to the intersection of Okeechobee Road and 25th Street, near HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital. A white cargo van was behind the scooter, traveling east on Okeechobee Road, Maj. Michael Santiago told WPBF's Angela Rozier at a briefing Monday afternoon. The van driver fled the scene and made a U-turn to drive in the wrong direction across the median on Okeechobee Road, but he crashed into the side of a building, the Kings Queens Unisex Salon. The man then ran from the scene. Salon owner Sheila Hampton showed the damage, and is thankful no one was inside at the time. Hampton said she feels for the victim and his family. "His family told me he was just leaving from one of his friend's houses and just going home," she said. A second vehicle, a Toyota pickup truck, was also struck, but no one was injured. Lucie County Sheriff's Office K-9 Unit and Aviation Unit assisted Fort Pierce police and the K-9 Unit in efforts to locate the driver. They are in possession of the van. Police described the driver as a Hispanic man wearing a dark-colored top with light-colored pants or shorts. "So, that in itself proves intent that that person knew exactly what they were doing at the time and was just trying to simply get away," Santiago said. Anyone with information should call the Fort Pierce Police Department at 772-462-6800 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at 800-273-8477. Stay up-to-date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25

entry.title: Police search for driver who killed scooter rider, crashed van into Fort Pierce salon - cw34.com
entry.summary: Police search for driver who killed scooter rider, crashed van into Fort Pierce salon    cw34.com
entry.article_text: Fort Pierce police are searching for a driver who they say hit and killed a man riding a scooter before fleeing the scene, crashing into a salon and running away on foot Sunday night. The deadly crash happened shortly before 9 p.m. on October 11 along Okeechobee Road, just west of South 25th Street. According to Major Michael Santiago with the Fort Pierce Police Department , a man riding a scooter was stopped at a red light behind a Toyota pickup truck when a white van traveling eastbound failed to stop and struck him from behind. "That in turn led to a domino effect where the motorcyclist was ejected from the scooter itself and was thrown into the vehicle in front of the scooter," Santiago said. Obtained 911 recordings capture the frantic moments following the crash. In one call, a person inside the Toyota pickup truck described the aftermath. "We got hit, and it's like, there's blood all over our car," the caller told a dispatcher. Another caller reported seeing the white van crash into the nearby building while trying to get away. Lucie County Fire District officials said crews were dispatched at 8:51 p.m. and arrived four minutes later. The scooter rider was pronounced dead at the scene. No other patients were transported. But investigators say the van driver did not remain at the scene. See also: No lawyer, no law degree: Port St. Lucie man takes on Flock cameras in federal court Instead, Santiago said the driver reversed, made a U-turn, briefly traveled westbound in the eastbound lanes of Okeechobee Road, crossed the median and lost control before crashing into Kings & Queens Unisex Salon. "After he crashed into the business, he fled on foot," Santiago said. According to a police news release, the driver ran northbound after crashing into the salon, located at 2508 Okeechobee Road. Police responded to multiple 911 calls reporting the crash around 8:52 p.m. and immediately established a perimeter, searching for the driver using K-9 units and assistance from the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office aviation unit. Despite their efforts, they were unable to locate him. Two additional vehicles involved in the crash remained at the scene, according to police. The department's Traffic Homicide Unit, Crime Scene Investigations and other personnel processed the scene as part of the ongoing investigation. By Monday afternoon, the van had been removed, but significant damage remained. Broken concrete and debris were piled outside the entrance, which was boarded up and surrounded by caution tape. Salon owner Sheila Hampton said she received a phone call about the crash and arrived to find extensive damage to her business. "They just called me at the last minute and I just seen a hole in my wall. Hampton said she was unable to open the salon Monday and was concerned about when she would be allowed to resume business. And I'm just hoping tomorrow will be a better day," she said. Despite the damage to her business, Hampton also expressed sympathy for the family of the man who died. "My condolences from King and Queen Salon. We give out our condolences to the family," she said. "This shouldn't have ever happened." Police searching for driver Santiago said witnesses described the driver as a Hispanic man wearing a dark top and light-colored pants or shorts. Investigators believe he may have been injured in the crash, based on evidence recovered at the scene. Police have recovered the van and identified its registered owner, but have not confirmed who was driving. Santiago said the registered owner lives approximately one to one-and-a-half miles from the crash scene. He also said the owner stopped communicating with investigators after officers began asking who had access to the vehicle. Police have not ruled anyone out as they continue pursuing leads. Investigators are also searching for surveillance footage that could help identify the driver. As of Monday afternoon, Santiago said they had not obtained video showing the suspect himself. "We are desperately needing the public's help in identifying who was behind the wheel of this box van," Santiago said. He urged anyone who saw the white van in the area Sunday night, recognized someone who may have been driving it or captured video of the incident to come forward. Police said the victim's identity had not yet been confirmed as of Monday, and confirmation was still pending before next of kin could be notified. No arrest had been announced as of Monday afternoon. Anyone with information about the crash or the driver's whereabouts is asked to contact the Fort Pierce Police Department at 772-462-6800 or submit a tip through Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers .

entry.title: Road, flight restrictions set to take effect near Mar-a-Lago this weekend
entry.summary: A major stretch of South Ocean Boulevard in Palm Beach is scheduled to close Friday morning until further notice, prompting traffic changes for residents and commuters in the area. According to the Town of Palm Beach's website, South Ocean Boulevard (State Road A1A) will close between South County Road and Southern Boulevard beginning at 5 a.m. Friday, Oct. 16. The closure will remain in effect until further notice. Town officials said information about traffic checkpoints, modified bridge-opening schedules and temporary marine security zones is available on the town's Planned Traffic Impacts webpage . The closure announcement comes as federal aviation officials issued a Temporary Flight Restriction, or TFR, for VIP movement in the West Palm Beach area. The notice is scheduled to take effect Saturday, Oct. 17, and remain in place through Sunday, Oct. 18. Similar road and airspace restrictions have been implemented in the past during visits by former President Donald Trump to his Mar-a-Lago residence. At this time, neither the Town of Palm Beach nor federal authorities have publicly confirmed whether Trump is expected to be in Palm Beach this weekend. Motorists are encouraged to plan ahead and expect delays in the area surrounding the closure.

entry.title: Scripps News poll: 40% of voters say they’ve been fooled by AI ads this campaign
entry.summary: Many Americans say theyve been confused or even fooled by political ads using artificial intelligence this campaign season, and want more rules governing how the technology is used, according to a new Scripps News/Talker Research poll. More than four-in-ten registered voters say theyve seen something they thought was real in a political ad, only to later find it was AI-generated. Another 30% said they saw something they werent sure was real or AI. Some of the most talked about ads of the campaign have featured AI-generated candidates like Sen. Jon Ossoff in a beauty salon , James Talarico reciting old quotes out of context , and Sherrod Brown overstaying his welcome at a birthday party . More than half of survey respondents (56%) said they have seen Republicans using AI ads, compared with 49% saying they have seen ads for Democrats. IN CASE YOU MISSED IT | 'I had the flu': Talarico returns to campaign trail, dismisses online rumors And more than three-quarters of voters say there should be rules around how the technology is used in politics. In the absence of federal regulation, states have passed their own laws aimed at curbing the influence of AI or deepfakes in campaign advertising. Some states require disclosures or bar deepfake videos from being published in the weeks leading up to Election Day. But many of the regulations fail to keep up with the evolving use of what can be a cheap and effective new tool. An analysis from the Wesleyan Media Project from early September found AI tools had been used in at least 164 ads, 69% of which did not disclose AI was used. Eighty percent were from Republicans or Republican-leaning groups. Still, a similar amount of voters in both parties say there should be rules around how the technology is used, according to the Scripps News/Talker Research poll, including 77% of Democrats and 79% of Republicans. Concerns about how AI could impact areas outside politics also cut across party lines. Large swaths of the country worry about the impact AI could have on their jobs (61%), government institutions (83%), financial institutions (81%), and their physical safety (57%). Nearly 80% say they see content they believe was generated by AI at least once per day. entry.title: Republicans are flooding Senate races with ad money, but paying a premium
entry.summary: Republicans are spending hundreds of millions of dollars on advertising in battleground Senate races as they scramble to defend increasingly competitive GOP seats in the final stretch of the midterms. But when it comes to how far they can stretch a dollar, theyre effectively paying premium prices at Whole Foods while Democrats are shopping deals at Costco. The disparity comes down to a difference in strategy. Republicans are relying heavily on outside groups, like super PACs, that pay elevated rates for ads and are making big buys late in the campaign, when inventory is stretched. By contrast, Democrats are taking advantage of discounted rates for candidates and earlier, less expensive reservations. At this stage in the game, Republicans are spending more to get less, which means the shock and awe of their massive dollar advantage isnt necessarily translating to an actual impact on the ground, according to veteran Republican strategist John Thomas. Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico’s campaign spent a little under $4 million to air its most aired ad, casting Paxton as “the most corrupt politician in Texas,” about 8,000 times. That amounts to less than one-fifth the spending for about half the airtime.Lauren French, communications director for Senate Majority PAC, a leading Democratic super PAC, also emphasized that buying TV late in the cycle becomes exorbitantly expensive. “The nitty-gritty of campaigning is that not all ad space costs the same,” she said.“If you are buying something in February, it’s going to be a lot cheaper, and you’re going to get a lot more bang for your buck than, say, if you’re buying it in September. So that’s why you’re seeing this huge disconnect between what Republicans are paying and what Democrats are paying on average in some of these races,” French said.In seven of the top nine Senate races by total TV and radio ad spending in September, Democrats paid less per GRP than Republicans.The two exceptions were New Hampshire and Alaska. Confident in their nominees, Republicans were able to secure comparable or better rates in both states’ key markets. In New Hampshire, this was reinforced by Republicans allocating relatively more to cheaper secondary markets.“Broadly speaking, Republicans are using their money pretty ineffectively, and public polling is saying that people are not seeing their ads as much as one would expect. So, by that definition alone, some of their money is being set on fire. We are being outspent in a lot of these states, which means we have to make more strategic decisions,” French said.Thomas said that Texas, in particular, was emblematic of this effect, with GOP outside groups mounting an urgent rescue effort for Paxton and pouring money into the state. He noted that Paxton allies had taken to buying ad time on national NFL broadcasts because local markets had grown so crowded. That’s why people across the country are seeing Texas Senate ads in games that don’t include the Dallas Cowboys or Houston Texans.RELATED STORY | Barack Obama to campaign with Ohio Democrats as he expands his outreach ahead of Election Day“In some cases, because the commercial rate is so high in a local, like a Houston spot, it actually sometimes can be cheaper to buy a national spot,” he said.Democrats’ efficiency advantage might have been much greater, given their candidates have consistently raised more money their Republican opponents on a campaign-to-campaign basis, allowing them to spend more directly on their own ads at cheap rates.But thanks to a recent Supreme Court ruling, for the first time this year, national party committees can take advantage of candidate ad rates through coordinated buys.This means well-funded national committees like the National Republican Congressional Committee or National Republican Senate Committee can team up with candidates – like Mike Rogers in Michigan or Sen. Jon Husted in Ohio – and foot the bill for pricey ad campaigns while getting candidate discounts.The expansion of coordinated buying has allowed Republicans to blunt the Democratic candidate fundraising advantage. Democrats can do the same, but the GOP has taken to it far more aggressively: In September, GOP advertisers spent more than $30 million on coordinated ad buys, compared to about $5 million from Democrats.Outside groups like super PACs still play a dominant role, however, due to their unique ability to accept unlimited donations and make unlimited expenditures.“The money is actually very, very inefficient, but the benefit, even with the inefficiency of a super PAC, is one or two people can cut checks and fund the whole thing,” Thomas said.

entry.title: Local non-profit all about recycling gets community boost
entry.summary: WPTV Morning Anchor Ashley Glass is following up at the Resource Depot in West Palm Beach, which is the site of a Let's Hear It community meet-up, and learning that the non-profit, all about recycling and repurposing everyday items, just received a big boost of community support. 'This place is amazing,' Craig Goldenfarb, Esq., Founder and CEO of GOLDLAW, said. WATCH Local non-profit all about recycling gets community boost Resource Depot gets community boost The Resource Depot is one of 65 local non-profit organizations benefiting from the law firm's GOLDEN 100 program, in which $100,000 in funding was donated. 'To support my community is really special,' Goldenfarb said. 'Putting money back into the non-profit is something that strikes me close to the heart. Staff at the Resource Depot take in 20,000 pounds of donated materials each month and repurpose them for sale. Glass asked the Resource Depot's Executive Director, Jennifer O'Brien, how the funding will be used. 'AI training for our staff,' she responded. 'We have a small but mighty staff, and were looking for ways we might work more efficiently. O'Brien also told Glass that when the community is invested, it gives her entire staff the energy to keep pushing forward with their non-profit work and saving an immeasurable amount of what could be trash from landfills.

entry.title: City council approves lease agreement to bring hotel to Vero Beach Regional Airport area - WPTV
entry.summary: City council approves lease agreement to bring hotel to Vero Beach Regional Airport area    WPTV
entry.article_text: WPTV has been reporting extensively on the growth at the Vero Beach Regional Airport when it comes to flights.But on Tuesday, Vero Beach City Council approved a lease agreement to bring a four-story, 116-room Marriott hotel to the airport."We've been in negotiations with this for the last three years,” Brian Dembeck, interim airport director, said. "This is something that is going to dramatically improve the passenger experience."Dembeck took WPTV to the site, which sits just outside the gates of the terminal along Aviation Boulevard."They're going to have a hotel right next door that they can come, they can stay, wait for their flight, and then go right over to the terminal."But the lodging is more than just for passengers.Brian Cartland, vice-president of economic development for the Indian River County Chamber of Commerce, said the hotel could attract more businesses to the city of Vero Beach and beyond."The hotel is going to serve multiple purposes,” said Cartland. "This hotel is going to help target industry growth by giving those companies that are looking at the area some additional alternatives for some great high-end options."While the hotel is close to the airport, Chad Maxey, senior vice president of Diversified Companies, the developer of the project, said one big need for the extra lodging is just down the street at the Jackie Robinson Training Complex."We feel this is a great location to have a hotel that's going to be able to provide amenities to the airport and also to the families and kids that are going to play baseball,” Maxey said.Maxey said the hotel will also feature a “homerun dugout amenity” for families."Kids can play virtual baseball in the hotel as they're getting ready to go across the street and actually hit the diamond over there and play with the Major League Baseball players,” Maxey said.Developers said the hotel will break ground next year and is expected to be completed by the end of 2028.

entry.title: Martin County commissioners unanimously move forward with 1-year moratorium on data centers
entry.summary: Martin County commissioners voted Tuesday unanimously to move forward with a one-year moratorium on data centers as county leaders consider how to handle future development of the facilities. Martin County Commissioner Edward Ciampi explained it's 'an opportunity to say, 'pause,' let's hear from people, lets have the opportunity for experts to come and speak to us on both sides. Watch report from Cassandra Garcia: Martin County commissioners unanimously move forward with 1-year moratorium on data centers Commissioners explained they would consider extending the moratorium later if they need more time. If it takes a year, a year and a half, two years, whatever it takes, whatever it takes, we should be doing this, said Martin County Commissioner Eileen Vargas. Tuesday's vote marked the first of two hearings scheduled this month on the proposed moratorium. PREVIOUS COVERAGE: Martin County eyes pause on data center development Martin County eyes pause on data center development Commissioners are expected to revisit the issue on Oct. 27, when another vote will be required. Martin County resident Scott Butler added, 'The fear of the use of all this water we have [...] and understanding what these data center[s] are going to use. entry.title: Port St. Lucie family chooses organ donation after teen's death, creating hope through tragedy
entry.summary: A Port St. Lucie family is turning unimaginable loss into hope after choosing organ donation following the death of their 14-year-old son , who was struck by a vehicle while walking to school, according to police. Port St. Lucie police said the teen was walking along Port St. Lucie Boulevard near Squirrel Avenue on Oct. 7 when he was struck from behind. He died from his injuries two days later. WATCH: Port St. Lucie Teen's Legacy Lives On Through Donation Port St. Lucie Teen's Legacy Lives On Through Donation | WPTV Now, the family's decision to donate his organs could help multiple people waiting for lifesaving transplants while creating a lasting legacy in his memory. Organ donation advocates say the family's choice highlights an ongoing need for registered donors. According to transplant advocates, more than 100,000 people nationwide are currently waiting for an organ transplant, and 15 lives are lost each day while patients remain on waiting lists. Family's decision offers hope to others The teen's family chose organ donation in the days following his death, a decision supporters say can have a profound impact on recipients and their families. 'It's a courageous thing for them to do, and I think it's the right thing,' said St. Lucie County Tax Collector Chris Craft. Craft has worked with Donate Life Florida through the tax collector's office to encourage organ donor registration and raise awareness about the need for donors. Transplant recipient shares personal perspective For Tyre Gray, a kidney transplant recipient and the chief administrative and legal officer for South Florida Donor Network, the family's decision carries special meaning. 'Organ donation is one of the few places where grief and gratitude exist in the same place,' Gray told WPTV. Gray said he spent five years waiting for a kidney transplant before receiving the life-saving organ he needed. 'I know for a fact that I wouldn't be here without a family making that election in their deepest moment of despair,' he said. Gray described years of uncertainty while waiting for a match. 'That's five years of uncertainty, five years of being paralyzed, five years of not being able to grow,' he said. entry.title: Suspected fentanyl supplier linked to overdose death arrested after chase on I-95
entry.summary: A suspected drug trafficker linked to a deadly fentanyl overdose investigation is behind bars after investigators say he fled from detectives, hit a law enforcement vehicle and led authorities on a high-speed chase on I-95 in St. Lucie and Martin counties. Investigators said the arrest of James Arthur Green, 43, came after a weeks-long narcotics investigation that also uncovered a suspected connection to a fatal fentanyl overdose. According to the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office, detectives with the Special Investigations Division conducted multiple undercover purchases of drugs, gathering evidence during those operations that identified Green as the suspected supplier of fentanyl to a person who later died from an overdose. On Oct. 13, detectives used the deceased victim's cellphone during another controlled narcotics operation and placed an order for fentanyl. Investigators said Green returned to the victim's residence, delivered about two grams of fentanyl and sent a photograph showing where he left the drugs. Later that day, detectives conducted a separate undercover operation in which Green allegedly participated in a transaction involving about two ounces of fentanyl and one pound of methamphetamine. When detectives attempted to arrest him, Green fled, allegedly hitting a sheriff's office vehicle and fleeing onto southbound I-95. Authorities said the pursuit reached speeds of approximately 115 mph. During the chase, detectives reported seeing Green throw suspected narcotics and a cellphone out of his vehicle. The Florida Highway Patrol and Martin County Sheriff's Office joined the pursuit as it entered Martin County. Troopers deployed stop sticks before performing a PIT maneuver near Kanner Highway, bringing the chase to an end. Investigators recovered the one pound of methamphetamine and two ounces of fentanyl associated with the controlled purchase, along with an additional 22 grams of methamphetamine, two grams of crack cocaine and one gram of fentanyl. As part of the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office investigation, Green faces charges including trafficking of fentanyl, trafficking of cocaine, four counts of trafficking methamphetamine, sale of cocaine and unlawful use of a two-way communication device. Investigators said Green returned to the victim's residence, delivered about two grams of fentanyl and sent a photograph showing where he left the drugs.Later that day, detectives conducted a separate undercover operation in which Green allegedly participated in a transaction involving about two ounces of fentanyl and one pound of methamphetamine.When detectives attempted to arrest him, Green fled, allegedly hitting a sheriff's office vehicle and fleeing onto southbound I-95.Authorities said the pursuit reached speeds of approximately 115 mph. entry.title: Road, flight restrictions set to take effect near Mar-a-Lago this weekend
entry.summary: A major stretch of South Ocean Boulevard in Palm Beach is scheduled to close Friday morning until further notice, prompting traffic changes for residents and commuters in the area. According to the Town of Palm Beach's website, South Ocean Boulevard (State Road A1A) will close between South County Road and Southern Boulevard beginning at 5 a.m. Friday, Oct. 16. The closure will remain in effect until further notice. Town officials said information about traffic checkpoints, modified bridge-opening schedules and temporary marine security zones is available on the town's Planned Traffic Impacts webpage . The closure announcement comes as federal aviation officials issued a Temporary Flight Restriction, or TFR, for VIP movement in the West Palm Beach area. The notice is scheduled to take effect Saturday, Oct. 17, and remain in place through Sunday, Oct. 18. Similar road and airspace restrictions have been implemented in the past during visits by President Donald Trump to his Mar-a-Lago residence. At this time, neither the Town of Palm Beach nor federal authorities have publicly confirmed whether Trump is expected to be in Palm Beach this weekend. Motorists are encouraged to plan ahead and expect delays in the area surrounding the closure.

entry.title: Scripps News poll: 43% of voters say they’ve been fooled by AI ads this campaign
entry.summary: Many Americans say theyve been confused or even fooled by political ads using artificial intelligence this campaign season, and want more rules governing how the technology is used, according to a new Scripps News/Talker Research poll. More than four-in-ten registered voters say theyve seen something they thought was real in a political ad, only to later find it was AI-generated. Another 30% said they saw something they werent sure was real or AI. Some of the most talked about ads of the campaign have featured AI-generated candidates like Sen. Jon Ossoff in a beauty salon , James Talarico reciting old quotes out of context , and Sherrod Brown overstaying his welcome at a birthday party . More than half of survey respondents (56%) said they have seen Republicans using AI ads, compared with 49% saying they have seen ads for Democrats. IN CASE YOU MISSED IT | 'I had the flu': Talarico returns to campaign trail, dismisses online rumors And more than three-quarters of voters say there should be rules around how the technology is used in politics. In the absence of federal regulation, states have passed their own laws aimed at curbing the influence of AI or deepfakes in campaign advertising. Some states require disclosures or bar deepfake videos from being published in the weeks leading up to Election Day. But many of the regulations fail to keep up with the evolving use of what can be a cheap and effective new tool. An analysis from the Wesleyan Media Project from early September found AI tools had been used in at least 164 ads, 69% of which did not disclose AI was used. Eighty percent were from Republicans or Republican-leaning groups. Still, a similar amount of voters in both parties say there should be rules around how the technology is used, according to the Scripps News/Talker Research poll, including 77% of Democrats and 79% of Republicans. Concerns about how AI could impact areas outside politics also cut across party lines. Large swaths of the country worry about the impact AI could have on their jobs (61%), government institutions (83%), financial institutions (81%), and their physical safety (57%). Nearly 80% say they see content they believe was generated by AI at least once per day. This random double-opt-in online survey of 1,000 U.S. registered voters was commissioned by Scripps News and conducted by market research company Talker Research, in accordance with the Market Research Societys code of conduct. entry.title: West Palm Beach nonprofit all about recycling gets community boost
entry.summary: WPTV Morning Anchor Ashley Glass is following up at the Resource Depot in West Palm Beach, home to a Let's Hear It community meet-up, and learning that the non-profit, which focuses on recycling and repurposing everyday items, just received a major boost in community support. 'This place is amazing,' Craig Goldenfarb, Esq., Founder and CEO of GOLDLAW, said. WATCH Local non-profit all about recycling gets community boost Resource Depot gets community boost The Resource Depot is one of 65 local non-profit organizations benefiting from the law firm's GOLDEN 100 program, in which $100,000 in funding was donated. 'To support my community is really special,' Goldenfarb said. 'Putting money back into the non-profit is something that strikes me close to the heart. Staff at the Resource Depot take in 20,000 pounds of donated materials each month and repurpose them for sale. Glass asked the Resource Depot's Executive Director, Jennifer O'Brien, how the funding will be used. 'AI training for our staff,' she responded. 'We have a small but mighty staff, and were looking for ways we might work more efficiently. O'Brien also told Glass that when the community is invested, it gives her entire staff the energy to keep pushing forward with their non-profit work and saving an immeasurable amount of what could be trash from landfills.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie family chooses organ donation after teen's death, creating hope through tragedy - WPTV
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie family chooses organ donation after teen's death, creating hope through tragedy    WPTV
entry.article_text: Lucie family is turning unimaginable loss into hope after choosing organ donation following the death of their 14-year-old son, who was struck by a vehicle while walking to school, according to police.Port St. Lucie police said the teen was walking along Port St. Lucie Boulevard near Squirrel Avenue on Oct. 7 when he was struck from behind. He died from his injuries two days later.WATCH: Port St. Lucie Teen's Legacy Lives On Through DonationNow, the family's decision to donate his organs could help multiple people waiting for lifesaving transplants while creating a lasting legacy in his memory.Organ donation advocates say the family's choice highlights an ongoing need for registered donors. According to transplant advocates, more than 100,000 people nationwide are currently waiting for an organ transplant, and 15 lives are lost each day while patients remain on waiting lists.The teen's family chose organ donation in the days following his death, a decision supporters say can have a profound impact on recipients and their families."It's a courageous thing for them to do, and I think it's the right thing," said St. Lucie County Tax Collector Chris Craft.Craft has worked with Donate Life Florida through the tax collector's office to encourage organ donor registration and raise awareness about the need for donors.For Tyre Gray, a kidney transplant recipient and the chief administrative and legal officer for South Florida Donor Network, the family's decision carries special meaning."Organ donation is one of the few places where grief and gratitude exist in the same place," Gray told WPTV.Gray said he spent five years waiting for a kidney transplant before receiving the life-saving organ he needed."I know for a fact that I wouldn't be here without a family making that election in their deepest moment of despair," he said.Gray described years of uncertainty while waiting for a match."That's five years of uncertainty, five years of being paralyzed, five years of not being able to grow," he said.Organ donation advocates say the need for donors continues across Florida and the United States.Gray noted that a single donor has the potential to save multiple lives and help many more patients through tissue donation."One donor is to save upwards of nine lives and to be able to heal another 75 lives," Gray said.Behind those numbers are people awaiting a second chance, he said."Let's all be heroes and save lives," Gray added.Advocates say organ donation often allows families to find meaning during some of life's most difficult moments."I would hope that they could see the lasting impact that a selfless act can make on others," Craft said. "If you can help somebody else, it's an amazing thing."For transplant recipients, organ donation can mean more time with family, additional milestones and opportunities.In the midst of tragedy, one Port St. Lucie family's decision could now help save lives and ensure their son's legacy continues through the people he may help.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. Our editorial team verifies all reporting on all platforms for fairness and accuracy.

entry.article_text: Fort Pierce police are searching for a driver who they say fled after a crash that killed a motorcyclist Sunday night.The crash happened around 8:52 p.m. near South 25th Street and Okeechobee Road. Officers responded after receiving multiple 911 calls about a crash involving a motorcycle.According to preliminary information from the Fort Pierce Police Department, a white box van traveling east on Okeechobee Road struck a blue motorcycle and attempted to leave the scene.Police said the van's driver made a U-turn in the eastbound lanes while fleeing, crossed the westbound lanes and crashed into Kings and Queens Unisex Salon at 2508 Okeechobee Road.The driver then got out of the van and fled north on foot, police said.When officers arrived, they found the motorcyclist in the outside eastbound lane of Okeechobee Road and determined the person had died. Lucie County Fire Rescue also responded.The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office K-9 and Aviation units assisted Fort Pierce police in searching for the driver, but police said he had not been located as of Monday. Two other vehicles involved in the crash remained at the scene.Police described the driver as an adult Hispanic man wearing a dark-colored top and light-colored pants or shorts.The identity of the person killed has not been confirmed.The Fort Pierce Police Department's Traffic Homicide Unit and Crime Scene Investigations are investigating.Anyone with information about the crash or the driver's identity or whereabouts is asked to contact Fort Pierce police at 772-462-6800 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers.

entry.title: Trump made Alaska push for Sullivan with Senate control at stake
entry.summary: Its a long way from Washington, has a small population and hasn't backed a Democrat for Senate in nearly 20 years. Yet President Donald Trump on Tuesday devoted a big chunk of his dwindling time ahead of crucial midterm elections to head to Alaska attempting to bolster a Republican incumbent senator in another sign of GOP fears about retaining control of Congress after Election Day on Nov. 3. Trump headlined a rally for Sen. Dan Sullivan in Wasilla, about 45 miles north of Anchorage famous for being the hometown of former Republican vice presidential nominee Sarah Palin and the headquarters of the Iditarod sled dog race across the state. Trump's stop is part of a western swing also taking him to rallies in Arizona and Montana on Wednesday. The president noted to the crowd that he had flown eight hours to rally for Sullivan, whom he called one of the best and most respected senators in D.C. Sullivan, seeking a third term, faces Democrat Mary Peltola, a former congresswoman who is running to put Alaska first and emphasizing cost-of-living issues. During Tuesday's rally, Trump announced that Taiwan would purchase gas from a proposed mega-gas project that he has been highlighting amid Sullivan's campaign and that it would invest more than $4 billion. There was no immediate confirmation from Taiwan, the self-governing island that China claims as its own. The White House did not immediately provide further details. Trump also said the Federal Communications Commission would vote in the coming weeks on investing an additional $162 million in expanding high-speed internet access in Alaska. And he announced pardons for two men who had pleaded guilty in 2022 to Clean Air Act violations for tampering with federally mandated monitoring devices on certain vehicles.
