entry.article_text: A welfare check on an 88-year-old Okeechobee County veteran led to the discovery of a homicide and the arrest of the victim's grandson following an early-morning police chase in Indian River County, Sheriff Eric Flowers and Chief Deputy Michael Hazellief said Thursday during a press conference.WATCH BELOW: Sheriff, chief deputy announce arrest of wanted suspectPaul Eugene Baker, a longtime Okeechobee County resident and veteran, was found dead on his property after his daughter-in-law called for a welfare check. His grandson, 35-year-old Earl Douglas Wadlington III, was taken into custody after deputies pursued him through a Walmart parking lot at approximately 4 a.m."What started off as a simple welfare check of an 88-year-old veteran in our county has turned into a tragedy and a family tragedy," Hazellief said.Baker's daughter-in-law had not seen or heard from him in several days. She went to his residence and found the house in disarray, which investigators said was highly unusual."She hadn't seen him or talked to him in several days. She went by to check on the residence. She found the house in disarray, became concerned, and it was highly unusual for him to not be around or for the house to be in this manner," Hazellief said.Law enforcement obtained and executed a search warrant for the property. Baker was found dead on the property. Investigators said the manner and location of his death made it immediately evident that it was a homicide.Baker's only vehicle was also missing from the residence, along with other property. Investigators learned that Wadlington had recently been living with Baker.The daughter-in-law told investigators that Wadlington had a history with the criminal justice system and that no other family member would allow him to live with them. Wadlington has over 800 felonies in his criminal background, the chief deputy said."The daughter-in-law also explained to us that he had been in and out of prison, that he had challenges that nobody else in the family would allow him to live with him, but the grandfather had allowed him to stay there," Hazellief said.Because the daughter-in-law also held power of attorney for Baker, law enforcement was able to enter the missing vehicle into the ALPR system — a license plate reader network connected to partner agencies across the Treasure Coast area — as stolen. The vehicle was flagged as connected to a homicide suspect. Investigators tracked the vehicle leaving the area but chose not to issue a public alert."We didn't put anything out publicly at that time because we did not want to startle. We wanted the suspect to stay in the vehicle. Quite honestly, we wanted to keep driving," Hazellief said.WATCH BELOW: Dashcam video of chase, bodycam video of arrest in Indian River CountyInvestigators noted that while the agency was required this past month to remove Flock cameras from state roads and permitted locations per a state DOT order, cameras in other qualifying locations remained operational and allowed investigators to move forward with the case."To be specific with the language, we still have them in place in places that don't meet that criteria, and because of that, we were able to really move forward with this case," Hazellief said.Senior detective Ashley Rojas and her team led the investigation, the chief deputy said.The stolen vehicle was detected by Indian River County's Flock camera system this morning, leading investigators to the suspect's location.Indian River County Sheriff Flowers described the early-morning pursuit caught on video, in which Wadlington fled from deputies through a Walmart parking lot."One of the particular things that's interesting is it's 4 o'clock in the morning. He's running from our deputies. He's running through the Walmart parking lot. You see that our deputies were able to deploy stop sticks. The reason that he ultimately stopped and got out and ran is because his truck was going to stop working. That stolen vehicle is going to stop working," Flowers said.Sebastian Police Department also responded and assisted Indian River County deputies throughout the pursuit."Doesn't matter if the uniform is green or blue, doesn't matter what color it is. We're all going to go after the bad guys," Flowers said.Flowers praised the Flock camera system and said the county will continue using it despite public criticism."For all the naysayers and all the people who don't like flock and who don't like it, we're going to continue to use it. We're going to continue to put bad guys in jail because of it," Flowers said.Flowers noted that Indian River County cameras not covered by the state DOT order remain in operation. He said the Flock system has aided in other cases, including one involving a missing elderly woman.Wadlington was arrested on fleeing and eluding charges, deputies said, in addition to driving a stolen a vehicle. Both agencies said they are working very closely with the state attorney's office to obtain a warrant for his arrest for the homicide very soon."This guy is the definition of somebody who needs to stay behind bars," Flowers said.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. entry.title: Treasure Coast water tank in the running for a national award - WPBF
entry.summary: Treasure Coast water tank in the running for a national award    WPBF
entry.article_text: A water tank at Jaycee Park has been transformed into a colorful tribute to Florida’s native wildlife thanks to Stuart-born and raised artist Christian Stanley and his wife, Jessica. "We keep an eye on the happenings that are going on here in Fort Pierce and saw that there was an open call to artists and put together a design that we thought was a strong submission and submitted it, and we're fortunately selected to come out here and paint the tank," said Stanley, co-owner of C. The decades-old, 22-foot-tall tank that can hold a million gallons of water is owned by Fort Pierce Utilities Authority. It was once a bright shade of white; now it features colorful paintings of manatees, dolphins, turtles, fish and pelicans, along with a sunset. "The great joy that I get out of being of mural artist is taking stuff from the ocean, from the forest, whatever, and bringing it out to the streets for people to see in a much larger-than-life fashion," he said. "So, when I knew the call was interested in being kind of native Florida wildlife, I knew that we could really bring something together that would be really impactful for the community." On Tuesday, Stanley and his wife traveled from Central Florida to the Treasure Coast to apply a UV clear coat to help protect the artwork against the harsh environment of the shore. The two originally began painting the tank in August, completing the mural within a month. He said they then decided to enter their work into Tnemec Company, Inc.'s 2026 Tank of the Year, not expecting much. But became the only South Florida water tank in the running against dozens across the state and the country. "We're so excited," Stanley said.

entry.title: South Florida fitness company brings personal trainers directly to clients
entry.summary: Having access to a gym is one thing. Actually using it is another. For Jennifer Fink, working out at home means avoiding some of the things she dislikes about going to a traditional gym. WATCH BELOW: Fitness at Your Door brings fitness trainers to your doorstep Fitness at Your Door: South Florida fitness company brings personal trainers directly to clients 'I don't really like the gym, and I usually work out at home,' Fink said. 'You don't have to wait for machines or deal with people at the gym if you don't want to.' It's one of the barriers Kashawn Fraser is trying to address through Fitness at Your Door, a South Florida wellness company that brings personal trainers directly to clients. Fraser said the company has grown to more than 250 certified personal trainers who undergo background checks, serving clients from Miami to Jupiter. The program is also expanding to the Treasure Coast. 'You can order Uber food to your door ... but to have someone show up for you where it matters the most, that's why this company was born,' Fraser said. WPTV reporter Christy Waite connected with Fraser to learn why he founded the organization. After playing professional football in the Canadian Football League and having multiple knee surgeries, he shifted his focus from his own fitness to helping others with theirs. 'I had three reconstructive knee surgeries back to back,' Fraser said. 'I have been in your shoes. I've been hurt, I've been down, I've been out of shape, I've been in shape.' For clients like Fink, having a trainer come to them can also take some of the anxiety out of going to a gym. 'You don't want to be on one of those YouTube videos where you are doing it wrong, and people are laughing at you,' Fink said. The program also works with people living in 55-and-older communities. Fraser said staying active can be especially meaningful for people approaching retirement who want the energy to enjoy time with their families. 'You work so hard to get to retirement to enjoy your kids and grandkids and have the best energy you can,' Fraser said. Across residential communities, gyms, fitness centers and clubhouses can go underused, even though residents have those amenities close to home. Fraser saw an opportunity to bring the workout into those spaces by having personal trainers meet clients where they already live.

entry.summary: The Palm Beach County School District's Advisory Boundary Committee (ABC) will hold a public meeting on Thursday, Oct. 22 to discuss proposed attendance zone changes affecting several elementary schools beginning in the 2027-2028 school year. WATCH: New $48 million school coming to Westlake, set to open August 2027 New $48 million school coming to Westlake, set to open August 2027 The meeting begins at 6:30 p.m. at the Fulton-Holland Educational Services Center Board Room located at 3300 Forest Hill Boulevard in West Palm Beach. entry.title: Okeechobee County Sheriff's Office seeks public's help on homicide suspect's movements before arrest
entry.summary: The Okeechobee County Sheriff's Office is asking for the public's assistance in gathering additional information regarding the movements of homicide suspect Earl Douglas Wadlington III prior to his arrest . WATCH: Sheriff, chief deputy announce arrest of wanted suspect Indian River, Okeechobee sheriffs announce apprehension of suspect Wadlington was arrested early Thursday morning in Indian River County following an early-morning deputy chase. Deputies said a welfare check on 88-year-old Paul Eugene Baker, an Okeechobee County veteran, led to the discovery of his death and the arrest of Wadlington, the victim's grandson. Deputies are asking anyone who may have encountered Wadlington, observed him, or has information regarding his whereabouts between Sunday, Oct. 11, and his arrest in Indian River County on Thursday, Oct. 15 at approximately 3 a.m., to please come forward. Authorities said they are particularly interested in any sightings or interactions in Palm Beach, Martin and St. Lucie counties during this timeframe. WATCH: Suspect tracked down using license plate readers, deputies say Okeechobee homicide suspect tracked down using license plate readers, deputies say Photographs show Wadlington on the day he left Okeechobee and at the time of his arrest, deputies said, and they want the community to pay special attention to the noticeable change in his hairstyle and overall appearance. Deputies said even the smallest detail could help investigators establish a more complete timeline of his movements. Anyone who saw Wadlington, spoke with him, or have any information that may assist in their investigation, please contact Senior Detective Ashley Rojas with the Okeechobee County Sheriff's Office at 863-763-3117 Ext 5108.

entry.title: Palm Beach County launches new voter app ahead of 2026 General Election
entry.summary: Palm Beach County voters now have a new way to check their voter information, find voting locations and track vote-by-mail ballots ahead of the 2026 General Election. Palm Beach County Supervisor of Elections Wendy Sartory Link announced the launch of the free Vote Palm Beach mobile app ahead of Election Day on Tuesday, Nov. 3. SPECIAL SECTION: More election coverage, early voting locations The app is available through the Apple App Store and Google Play Store and is designed to give voters access to election information and services from their phones. 'Whether you're at home, at work, or on the go, we want to make it as easy as possible for every Palm Beach County voter to access accurate, reliable election information,' Link said in a Friday news release. According to the Supervisor of Elections Office, voters can use the app to: Check their voter information and registration Find voting locations View election dates and deadlines Track a vote-by-mail ballot Access information directly from the Palm Beach County Supervisor of Elections Office 'With the 2026 General Election approaching, our new mobile app puts another trusted resource right in the palm of your hand,' Link said. 'It's all about meeting voters where they are and giving them the tools they need to vote with confidence.' The Elections Office said the launch follows a recent overhaul of its website and the introduction of the Palm Beach County Voter Dashboard, which also provides access to voter information and election services. The Vote Palm Beach app is available for free through the Apple App Store and Google Play Store. Voters can find additional information at VotePalmBeach.gov or call the Supervisor of Elections Office at 561-656-6200.

entry.article_text: A shooting in the Banner Lake area of Hobe Sound on Wednesday night left one person dead, according to the Martin County Sheriff’s Office. Deputies responded to the scene along Southeast Citrus Way and spent hours investigating. Authorities said one person was detained for questioning. Harriet Ford Greg, who said the victim was her grandson, shared that he lived with her. She recalled hearing three gunshots while she was in bed and immediately worrying about him, knowing he was out that night. When she stepped outside, she said she saw him on the ground as first responders tried to save him. " laying on the ground out there and the police officer was reviving him," Greg said. "I thought that he's not going to make it. Somebody shot him." Greg said she is trying to stay strong for her family but admitted she cannot bring herself to walk into the room where her grandson stayed, saying none of this feels real. entry.title: American Heritage Delray senior Domenick Swanson commits to play football at Army while chasing a state title
entry.summary: The American Heritage Stallions are chasing a back-to-back 4A state football championship, and one of the players anchoring their offensive line has already secured his spot at the next level. Domenick Swanson, a senior at American Heritage in Delray, has committed to play college football at the United States Military Academy at West Point, New York. WATCH BELOW: American Heritage Delray offensive lineman commits to play football at Army American Heritage Delray offensive lineman commits to play football at Army 'I will be going to West Point to play football,' Swanson said. 'It is a great opportunity. I went up there, and I was talking to coaches, and everyone says it's an amazing campus. It's beautiful. I mean, it's such a great opportunity to join the military and serve my country and the ability to play college football. I'm very excited about it.' Swanson wears No. 66 and plays center a role he and his coach describe as the quarterback of the offensive line. 'You know, a big reason why our coach likes me at center is that it's like the leader of the offensive line. Being there for the guys and helping with all the plays, and it's a really important part,' Swanson said. Swanson also has family support behind him, his cousin Lily, saying Swanson is a football superstar. 'Lily's my biggest cheerleader.' Swanson said. As his high school career winds down, Swanson said what he will miss most is the bonds he has built with his teammates. 'Really just the relationships and bonds that I've made with my team. You know, I just, it's going to be sad to leave them all behind. Of course, you know, I'll always have my brothers, you know, we'll always be together, but playing football with them, it'll definitely be a big change.' Swanson said. At the college level, Swanson said he looks forward to performing on a bigger stage and playing in front of thousands of people. Before he gets there, he has one goal left for this season. 'I would love to see us just go win every other game. That's kind of an obvious answer. But then, you know, we got our state championship. Hopefully we can go back-to-back,' Swanson said. The Stallions are 7-1 heading into their Friday night game vs. Lakeland Christian.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie residents could pay about $11 more a month for trash - WPBF
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie residents could pay about $11 more a month for trash    WPBF
entry.article_text: Lucie residents are being asked in a straw poll whether they would support paying more for an additional weekly trash pickup, with the proposal adding at least $131 annually to the residential solid-waste assessment. Stay up to date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25 Right now, residents receive one garbage pickup per week. The proposed change would increase costs by about $11 per month, with service potentially starting in 2028 if the city moves forward. “This is something that is nonbinding, but it gives City Council an opportunity to get a sense of the will of the people and what they would prefer to see,” said Scott Samples, spokesperson for the city of Port St. The city emphasized that the poll is not a final decision. A "yes" vote would indicate support for the additional cost, while a "no" vote would signal opposition. However, the results will not automatically change the current trash pickup schedule. City Council controls the trash contract and service levels, meaning any changes would require council approval and an updated agreement with the current waste management provider, FCC Environmental Services. The city also noted that a second pickup would be an ongoing expense and could increase with inflation. “City Council would take this up. They would have to work with the vendor to understand what the logistics of that would be. And then, the City Council would then vote on whether or not to move forward with this,” Samples said. The poll aims to provide city leaders with insight into residents' preferences, but the final decision will rest with the City Council. Get the latest news updates with the WPBF 25 News app.

entry.title: Fort Pierce police investigate after body found in Lincoln Park lake - cw34.com
entry.summary: Fort Pierce police investigate after body found in Lincoln Park lake    cw34.com
entry.article_text: A man in his 30s was found dead in a lake at Lincoln Park in Fort Pierce Wednesday morning, and police are investigating how he ended up in the water. An officer was flagged down by a citizen just after 9 a.m. who reported seeing a body floating in the lake near the 400 block of North 13th Street, Fort Pierce Police Major Michael Santiago said. Officers say they arrived and found a man face down in the water. Rescue crews pulled him out, but he was pronounced dead. Police identified the man but are waiting to notify his next of kin. Santiago described him as a Black man believed to be between 30 and 32 years old. Investigators are working to determine how the man entered the water and what he was doing before his death. See also: Man fatally shot by PBSO deputy after Boynton Beach pursuit identified There were no apparent signs of trauma to the man's body, Santiago said, but he noted the body appeared to have been in the water for some time. Police are canvassing the area, speaking with potential witnesses and looking for surveillance footage that could help investigators determine how the man ended up in the lake, per FPPD. Santiago said investigators are also looking into whether currents in the waterway could have played a role in where the body was found. It is too early to determine whether foul play or drugs were involved. Investigators are waiting for the medical examiner's findings, including autopsy and toxicology results, to help determine the cause of death. CBS12 News will provide updates as more information becomes available.

entry.title: Will Port St. Lucie see more floods this weekend? - WPEC
entry.summary: Will Port St. Lucie see more floods this weekend?    WPEC
entry.article_text: This weekend we're expected to see more heavy rain in our area. This may be exactly the kind of weekend forecast that many people in Port St. Lucie do not want to hear. Last week, parts of the city flooded when torrential rains hit Port St. According to our Stormtrac meteorologists, the city got about four inches of rain in a 48 hour period last week. Roads turned into lakes, water levels in canals rose quickly, and some drivers took their chances and drove through standing water deep enough to possibly leave them stalled with nowhere to go. One homeowner, who has a canal directly behind his house, says the flooding was unlike anything he had ever seen in the two years he's lived in Port St. See also: Trump expected at Mar-a-Lago as Palm Beach road closures, No Kings rallies are planned "When I came out, I was like, Oh, my God. I've never seen it like this before!" said Peter Rodriguez, who lives at the intersection of SW Todd Avenue and SW Broadview Street in Port St. How concerned is he about the possibility of another flood this weekend? "I don't think it's gonna get that high. If it starts getting that high, then I'm gonna start to pray. Not another flood," he said. A city spokesman says they'll have public works employees on standby this weekend if heavy rain comes, and they need to clear storm drains or move pumps into position to lower water levels in certain areas such as near the intersection of Savona Boulevard California Boulevard.

entry.title: Palm Beach County launches new voter app ahead of 2026 General Election
entry.summary: Palm Beach County voters now have a new way to check their voter information, find voting locations and track vote-by-mail ballots ahead of the 2026 General Election. Palm Beach County Supervisor of Elections Wendy Sartory Link announced the launch of the free Vote Palm Beach mobile app ahead of Election Day on Tuesday, Nov. 3. SPECIAL SECTION: More election coverage, early voting locations The app is available through the Apple App Store and Google Play Store and is designed to give voters access to election information and services from their phones. 'Whether you're at home, at work, or on the go, we want to make it as easy as possible for every Palm Beach County voter to access accurate, reliable election information,' Link said in a Friday news release. According to the Supervisor of Elections Office, voters can use the app to: Check their voter information and registration Find voting locations View election dates and deadlines Track a vote-by-mail ballot Access information directly from the Palm Beach County Supervisor of Elections Office 'With the 2026 General Election approaching, our new mobile app puts another trusted resource right in the palm of your hand,' Link said. 'It's all about meeting voters where they are and giving them the tools they need to vote with confidence.' The Elections Office said the launch follows a recent overhaul of its website and the introduction of the Palm Beach County Voter Dashboard, which also provides access to voter information and election services. The Vote Palm Beach app is available for free through the Apple App Store and Google Play Store. Voters can find additional information at VotePalmBeach.gov or call the Supervisor of Elections Office at 561-656-6200.

entry.title: Young Stuart divers take a leap toward college scholarships, international competition and Olympic dreams
entry.summary: In life, they say, take a leap of faith. Well, a group of kids in Stuart are doing just that on a diving board. WATCH BELOW: Stuart divers take leap toward big dreams Stuart's Atlantic Diving Team teaches the Olympic sport of diving to kids of all ages,experience levels 'There are different things for different people. Some people prefer platform diving, which is much higher but fun, which I prefer. Something Ive grown to love is all the friendships that I make throughout the years,' said Grace Erickson, a local diver, who admits diving has always been her passion. 'On my preschool poster I wrote what I wanted to be when I got older was a diver,' Erickson said. That preschooler who could only dream of being a diver is fulfilling her dream as an eighth grader. 'Its been really exciting; it's new things every twist and turn, both in your head and diving off the board,' Erickson said. Her longtime coach, Osvaldo 'Pito' Alberty, thanks her for her courage and wants to see Erickson and her teammates take the sport to new levels. 'We are like a family here. We treat each other with respect and courtesy, and we push each other to do better than everyone else,' said Pito, whose passion is sharing his experience, knowledge and love for diving with young athletes with the Atlantic Diving Team in Stuart. Atlantic takes divers of all ages, backgrounds and experience levels and teaches them the Olympic sport of diving. 'The younger we get them, the better it is because over time they can get scholarships. If they want to do international diving, they can qualify for international competitions or even the Olympics,' Pito said. For divers like Erickson, she wants to take her talents to the college level, but there's a new diver whos just learning the sport, Carissa Smith. 'I was recently a gymnast and just about two months ago I started diving,' said Smith. Smith is a natural-born acrobat. At 14, she hasn't participated in her first competition because she wants to learn the basics. But for now, she admits diving is pretty fun. 'It feels like you're flying; it's exhilarating just being able to get better at my diving,' said Smith.

entry.article_text: A shooting in the Banner Lake area of Hobe Sound on Wednesday night left one person dead, according to the Martin County Sheriff’s Office. Deputies responded to the scene along Southeast Citrus Way and spent hours investigating. Authorities said one person was detained for questioning. Harriet Ford Greg, who said the victim was her grandson, shared that he lived with her. She recalled hearing three gunshots while she was in bed and immediately worrying about him, knowing he was out that night. When she stepped outside, she said she saw him on the ground as first responders tried to save him. " laying on the ground out there and the police officer was reviving him," Greg said. "I thought that he's not going to make it. Somebody shot him." Greg said she is trying to stay strong for her family but admitted she cannot bring herself to walk into the room where her grandson stayed, saying none of this feels real. entry.title: Drinking, threats and guns: New information released in fatal shooting of 21-year-old in Hobe Sound - WPBF
entry.summary: Drinking, threats and guns: New information released in fatal shooting of 21-year-old in Hobe Sound    WPBF
entry.article_text: A 21-year-old man was fatally shot Wednesday night in the Banner Lake neighborhood of Hobe Sound, and authorities are investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident. Martin County sheriff's deputies responded to the scene along Southeast Citrus Way, where they found Jarvis Preston with three gunshot wounds to the chest. "I know you're going to ask me, was it a stand your ground? And the answer is, I don't know right now," Sheriff John Budensiek said. Budensiek explained that Preston and the shooter were friends. Witnesses reported that Preston had been drinking heavily throughout the day and began threatening the shooter and others while armed with a gun. "He's talking, I'm going to shoot you, I'm going to hurt you. The shooter walks towards him, now they're at the edge of the road, at which point the deceased starts to pull out a handgun. The shooter pulls out his AR-15, actually it's a rifle, shoots him three times in the chest, and he drops right there," Budensiek said. The sheriff said the shooter called 911 and attempted life-saving efforts before Preston was flown to St. Mary’s Hospital, where he died. Preston’s grandmother, Harriet Ford Gregg, said she heard the gunshots and later saw her grandson lying on the ground. "It was Jarvis laying on the ground out there, and the police officer was reviving him," Gregg said. She shared her grief over losing Preston, who lived with her, saying his empty bedroom is now too painful to face. I'm not going in there," Gregg said. entry.title: Investigators question if fatal shooting in Hobe Sound falls under stand-your-ground law - WPBF
entry.summary: Investigators question if fatal shooting in Hobe Sound falls under stand-your-ground law    WPBF
entry.article_text: Investigators in Martin County are working to determine whether a fatal shooting in the Banner Lake neighborhood of Hobe Sound was a crime or if the shooter acted within Florida's stand-your-ground law. The Martin County Sheriff’s Office said the shooter told them he and his friend were on Southeast Citrus Way on Wednesday night when an argument escalated. According to the shooter, his friend repeatedly threatened to shoot him and even showed him a gun. "The deceased starts to pull out a handgun. The shooter pulls out his AR-15, actually, it's a rifle, shoots him three times in the chest, and he drops right there," Sheriff John Budensiek said. Family members identified the deceased as Jarvis Preston. The sheriff’s office has not released the identity of the shooter. "I know you're going to ask me, was it a stand-your-ground? And the answer is, I don't know right now," Budensiek said. Dave Aronberg, the former Palm Beach County state attorney who is not involved in this case but has experience with stand-your-ground cases, said the shooter’s account suggests it could fall under the law. "The shooter must have reasonably believed that firing the weapon was immediately necessary to prevent imminent death or great bodily harm," Aronberg said. However, Aronberg noted that if Preston did not pull a gun, never had a gun, or if the shooter was the aggressor, the stand your ground defense would not apply. "You can't start a fight, provoke the confrontation and then shoot your way out of it," Aronberg said. The sheriff said investigators are still working to locate and interview witnesses to the shooting. He added that the final decision on whether charges will be filed will be made in collaboration with the state attorney’s office. entry.title: Amendment 3 could bring rush of Florida homebuyers, impact property values
entry.summary: Amendment 3 aims to change the property tax structure in Florida by saving money for homeowners and cutting revenue for cities and counties. It could have an impact on the Florida real estate market. A 2025 study by Realtor.com suggests home values in Florida could rise 7% to 9% if the referendum passes, and some real estate professionals say there will likely be an impact. WATCH BELOW: Amendment 3 could shake up Florida housing market Amendment 3 and Real Estate 'I don't see them going up to like the 7, 8, 9, 10 percent,' says Jeff Lichtenstein of Echo Fine Properties in Palm Beach Gardens. However, he does see a possible rush of buyers entering the market. 'You better be prepared because if it happens, it will happen fast,' Lichtenstein said. 'I think there will be a mad rush to get in here, because if not, then you're waiting five years.' That's because the referendum requires homeowners to be homesteaded in Florida by Dec 31 to receive the full tax savings right away. New home buyers entering the state would have a five-year waiting period to get the full homestead exemption. The Florida Realtors is publicly supporting Amendment 3 but isn't convinced about property values rising quickly. 'The cost of home is economically driven,' Florida Realtors CEO Margy Grant. 'It's a supply and demand conversation, and when inventory increases, prices stabilize and we've seen that in recent months.' Amendment 3 needs 60% of the vote to pass on November 3.

"I think there will be a mad rush to get in here, because if not, then you're waiting five years."That's because the referendum requires homeowners to be homesteaded in Florida by Dec 31 to receive the full tax savings right away.New home buyers entering the state would have a five-year waiting period to get the full homestead exemption.The Florida Realtors is publicly supporting Amendment 3 but isn't convinced about property values rising quickly."The cost of home is economically driven," Florida Realtors CEO Margy Grant. "It's a supply and demand conversation, and when inventory increases, prices stabilize and we've seen that in recent months."Amendment 3 needs 60% of the vote to pass on November 3.

entry.title: 33 years after uncle's murder, family asks Gov. Ron DeSantis to sign killer's death warrant
entry.summary: Thirty-three years after his uncle was murdered, Brian Kunkel is still waiting for what he considers justice. 'There's a whole host of emotions with this,' Kunkel said. 'There's a tremendous amount of anger, and now as we speak, it kind of starts to build back up again.' WATCH BELOW: 'It's time': Family seeks execution 33 years after loved one murdered Family seeks execution 33 years after man killed in West Palm Beach His uncle, Richard Kunkel, was a 32-year-old local florist remembered by his family as outgoing, generous and full of life. 'Richard was a fun-loving guy,' Brian Kunkel said. 'He had a great spirit. Very friendly. Very outgoing the type of person that literally would give you the shirt off his back.' In 1993, Richard Kunkel went to Roosters nightclub in West Palm Beach. Court records show Ronald Knight and two other men went to the gay bar looking for a man to lure away, rob and beat. 'This was all premeditated,' Brian Kunkel said. 'He knew what he was doing.' Court records show the men befriended Kunkel and convinced him to leave with them. Knight then drove him to a secluded area, where he shot and killed him. The men robbed Kunkel, stole his car and burglarized his home. 'Richard begged for his life,' Brian Kunkel said. 'He pleaded not to be shot. He was murdered in cold blood.' Two years later, Knight was charged in another killing. In May 1995, 22-year-old Brendan Meehan was lured from Heartbreakers, then a gay nightclub on Olive Avenue in West Palm Beach, taken to a secluded area and killed. Knight was convicted of both murders and sentenced to death in 1998. 'These people had purposes in life, and it's gone,' Kunkel said. A family waiting for an execution More than three decades after Richard Kunkel's murder, Knight remains on death row. Now, Kunkel is asking Gov. Ron DeSantis to sign his death warrant. 'It's been a long and arduous process,' he said. 'My grandparents are gone. They've passed without closure, and I know, at least in my grandmother's case, she died of really a broken heart.' 'This needs to be done. It needs to be finalized,' Kunkel added. His request comes as Florida carries out executions at a pace rarely seen in the state. Florida executed a record 19 people in 2025. Seventeen people have been executed so far in 2026, with two more executions scheduled. That pace has drawn concern from death penalty opponents and defense attorneys, who warn increasingly compressed timelines could put additional strain on the appeals

entry.title: Port St. Lucie tests new water sensors as weekend rain threatens flood-prone areas
entry.summary: More rain is expected this weekend across South Florida and the Treasure Coast, and WPTV is learning that Port St. Lucie Public Works is preparing. Scott Samples, communications manager with the City of Port St. Lucie, said crews spent the week clearing debris from drains and grates. WATCH BELOW: Port St. Lucie prepares for rain, flooding concerns Port St. Lucie prepares for rain, flooding concerns Samples added that water levels in retention ponds and canals are at an adequate level and won't need to be lowered. Staff have also been testing their new pilot water sensors, which will send alerts to select staff if water levels rise. 'It's a way for us to respond faster to very specific locations,' Samples said. Jennifer Collins, owner of Pets Play Grooming off California and Savona boulevards, said her staff is preparing too. 'We're nervous about this storm coming up this week,' Collins said. 'Every time it rains, we get scared.' Collins is no stranger to flooding on California and Savona boulevards. She said flooding has occurred there for years. WPTV was there when water levels rose at the intersection last week. Collins said she already sent messages to her customers for Saturday. 'We may have to reschedule their dogs. We may have to push them off to next week,' Collins said. 'Saturdays are one of our busiest days, so it does really affect us as a small business.' For long-term solutions at the intersection, the city is working on a large-scale drainage project for the Oak Hammock neighborhood, which includes raising portions of the roadway. 'When this project is completed, those problems won't be problems anymore,' Samples said. The drainage project is still in data collection before moving on to design. 'We can't work if it's raining, and that's in Florida,' Collins said. 'That's just not OK.' The project may take years until completion, but Collins said she already thought about moving her business. 'We've also talked about possibly moving, and you know that would be hard too,' Collins said. 'I just feel like it's not, not getting better.'

entry.article_text: This weekend we're expected to see more heavy rain in our area. This may be exactly the kind of weekend forecast that many people in Port St. Lucie do not want to hear. Last week, parts of the city flooded when torrential rains hit Port St. According to our Stormtrac meteorologists, the city got about four inches of rain in a 48 hour period last week. Roads turned into lakes, water levels in canals rose quickly, and some drivers took their chances and drove through standing water deep enough to possibly leave them stalled with nowhere to go. One homeowner, who has a canal directly behind his house, says the flooding was unlike anything he had ever seen in the two years he's lived in Port St. See also: Trump expected at Mar-a-Lago as Palm Beach road closures, No Kings rallies are planned "When I came out, I was like, Oh, my God. entry.title: 'He just tried to ram me': Port St. Lucie man arrested after a chase ends on South Hutchinson Island - WPBF
entry.summary: 'He just tried to ram me': Port St. Lucie man arrested after a chase ends on South Hutchinson Island    WPBF
entry.article_text: Lucie man was arrested Thursday night after leading St. Lucie County deputies on a high-speed chase that ended on South Hutchinson Island. The pursuit began in the 9600 block of South Ocean Boulevard when a Patrol Operations deputy attempted to stop the driver of a pickup truck for a traffic violation. Andrew Bolonka, the director of communications for the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office, said the driver fled instead of stopping, making a U-turn and spinning donuts in the roadway, forcing other motorists to take evasive action. Deep Dive: WPBF 25 News Investigates After briefly stopping, the driver made another U-turn, cut across lanes of traffic, and accelerated toward the deputy's patrol vehicle. "The deputy tries to stop the vehicle; all of a sudden, the vehicle lunges, takes off, accelerates, does another U-turn, and then starts allegedly heading straight toward the deputy. Which you can see in the body-worn camera, where the deputy makes an evasive maneuver and says, 'Oh, he almost hit me,'" Bolonka said. Members of the department's Special Investigations Unit and deputies in the air assisted in the pursuit. The driver continued to flee even after stop sticks were deployed. Deputies eventually executed a PIT maneuver along Seaway Drive, bringing the vehicle to a stop. Despite repeated verbal commands to exit the truck, the driver refused, prompting deputies to deploy pepper balls into the vehicle. The driver then surrendered and was taken into custody without further incident. The suspect, identified as 37-year-old Joshua Gallagher of Port St. Lucie, faces several charges, including aggravated assault with a deadly weapon, possession of a controlled substance without a prescription, and resisting arrest without violence. He remains in custody at the St. "When people make decisions like this, and they commit an act that puts not only the deputies and other law enforcement officers in peril, but they are also putting the general public in peril. If we can do so safely, we're going to put it to an end," Bolonka said. Authorities expressed relief that no one was injured during the incident. entry.article_text: The person shot during a shooting in Hobe Sound died Thursday, according to the Martin County Sheriff’s Office. The victim's mother identifies the shooting victim as Jarvis Preston, 21, of Hobe Sound. She says her son was shot by his best friend. She says she does not know what led to the shooting. She says Preston was not married, and he was the father of a small child. "It's just, it's dreadful, like, I can't, I can't understand what, why it expired to the way it did, because they, best friends. What escalated this to happen when it did?" said Ebony Preston, the mother of the shooting victim. The sheriff’s office began investigating the shooting Wednesday after it happened on Southeast Citrus Way, off Florida Avenue, in the Banner Lake neighborhood. Neighbors said they heard three gunshots around 8 p.m. Sheriff's Officials say Preston was armed with a handgun with a 30-clip magazine, which was recovered at the scene of the shooting Wednesday night. And they say Preston was shot and killed by his friend, who shot him from 10 feet away with an AR15 assault rifle. Now, what I gotta do, what? I gotta, like, it's horrible," Ebony Preston said. Preston's stepfather also wants answers. That's what I don't understand how it come about, 'cause they best friends," said Rodney Clemon, the victim's stepfather. Sheriff John Budensiek, Preston and his friend had been drinking earlier in the day, and Preston tried to rob his friend near their homes. "Multiple witnesses have now told us that he made threats to all kinds of people out on the street. He was yelling loudly, was extremely intoxicated, acting belligerent," Sheriff Budensiek said. The friend, who was armed with an AR15 assault rifle, came out of his house twice with his girlfriend. The second time, the friend and Jarvis Preston--who was armed with a handgun-- got into a confrontation that ended in gunfire. "The deceased (Preston) starts to pull out a handgun. Actually, it's a rifle, shoots him three times in the chest and he (Preston) drops right there," Sheriff Budensiek explained. Mary’s Medical Center in West Palm Beach and did not survive. Sheriff Budensiek says they have not determined yet if the shooting was self-defense or a murder. The victim's mother says it's devastating. "It's lot of unanswered questions. But my son is dead, so how do we go from there?" Ebony Preston said. See also: Funding for schools in Palm Beach County on your November ballot No one has been arrested. The Sheriff says they're working carefully with the State Attorney's Office to determine if anyone will be charged in this shooting or if it was a case of stand your ground, and if the shooter acted in self-defense. He says the individual who shot Preston attempted to render aid to the victim and remained at the scene following the shooting. The name of the shooter has not been released because the matter is still under investigation.

entry.title: Prima Vista Boulevard safety plan in St. Lucie County would add raised median after 578 crashes since 2020
entry.summary: WPTV is learning that potential road improvements are coming to a busy road in Port St. Lucie. St. Lucie County staff are sharing designs and want to hear input from neighbors about a proposed project on Prima Vista Boulevard. WATCH BELOW: Neighbors weigh in on Prima Vista Boulevard changes St. Lucie County wants input on improvements to this busy road They plan to improve a section of the roadway from Airoso Boulevard to U.S. Highway 1 by removing the center left turn lanes Dan Zrallack, county engineer, said their plan is to replace the center left-turn lanes with a raised median. 'The center turn lane is often referred to as a suicide lane,' Zrallack said. 'The more turning movements you have, the more chances you have for accidents by restricting access and putting in the median turn lanes. We can kind of control where those turning movements are and protect the drivers as well as pedestrians walking along the roadway.'  According to the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office, there have been 578 crashes on that section of the Prima Vista Boulevard since 2020.  Zrallack said the median will make the road safer.  'Statistically, the safety improves by up to like 40 percent or more,' Zrallack said.  But not every neighbor is sold on the improvements.  Kadaysha Wilkins lives on Prima Vista Boulevard and told WPTV the median will make traveling more complicated.  'Adding medians or anything else is going to cause more chaos than good,' Wilkins said. 'Ten to 12 years of living here, I've never seen an issue with our turning lane.'  Wilkins said it'll make it more difficult to take her niece and nephew to school by using the median instead of driving across the street.  'A five-minute ride has turned into a 15-minute travel,' Wilkins said. Wilkins said trying to come home could also be an issue. 'Turning into my driveway, which could have taken two seconds, is that now going to take 15 minutes? Wilkins said.   Zrallack said he hears the concerns and hopes they can address them on Thursday night during their public meeting. 'We're hoping to get more of that by hearing from the community again and seeing what else we can do to refine the design,' Zrallack said. A second in-person public meeting for the project was held Thursday at the MidFlorida Credit Union Event Center.

entry.article_text: This weekend we're expected to see more heavy rain in our area. This may be exactly the kind of weekend forecast that many people in Port St. Lucie do not want to hear. Last week, parts of the city flooded when torrential rains hit Port St. According to our Stormtrac meteorologists, the city got about four inches of rain in a 48 hour period last week. Roads turned into lakes, water levels in canals rose quickly, and some drivers took their chances and drove through standing water deep enough to possibly leave them stalled with nowhere to go. One homeowner, who has a canal directly behind his house, says the flooding was unlike anything he had ever seen in the two years he's lived in Port St. See also: Trump expected at Mar-a-Lago as Palm Beach road closures, No Kings rallies are planned "When I came out, I was like, Oh, my God. I've never seen it like this before!" said Peter Rodriguez, who lives at the intersection of SW Todd Avenue and SW Broadview Street in Port St. How concerned is he about the possibility of another flood this weekend? "I don't think it's gonna get that high. If it starts getting that high, then I'm gonna start to pray. Not another flood," he said. A city spokesman says they'll have public works employees on standby this weekend if heavy rain comes, and they need to clear storm drains or move pumps into position to lower water levels in certain areas such as near the intersection of Savona Boulevard California Boulevard.

entry.title: Palm Beach seawall replacement will close popular beach for 18 months
entry.summary: Behind the peach paint and scalloped edges of a familiar Palm Beach seawall is a structure that engineers say has reached the end of its useful life after more than a century of protecting the island. Now, the town is preparing for a major replacement project that will change the look of the beachfront and close the beach for about a year and a half. WATCH BELOW: Seawall replacement will close this beach for 18 months Palm Beach seawall replacement to close beach for 18 months The pastel-colored seawall has long blended into the scenery along a beach frequented by tourists and locals. Sandra Greenberg, who was visiting with her family from Virginia and has a condo in West Palm Beach, described it simply: 'It's a great beach, love it.' A tourist visiting from Costa Rica shared the sentiment, saying, 'Yes, it's perfect.' For people who live nearby, however, the beach can be more than a destination. It is part of their regular routine. 'This is where I come to, like, relax,' said Bridget St. Laurent, a local and owner of Palm Beach Beauty Lab on Palm Beach. 'It's my life, it's my backyard, I grew up here, and the fact I can just take a five-minute drive to the ocean means so much.' St. Laurent told WPTV she tries to visit once a week, if not more. But that routine is about to be interrupted. The seawall is one line of defense from hurricanes and storm surges that, over more than a century, has protected the island from what is estimated to be $7 billion in private property, along with critical infrastructure on Palm Beach. Replacing it will require a lengthy beach closure, with the project expected to keep beachgoers away for approximately a year and a half. 'A year and a half? That's so sad,' St. Laurent said after learning from WPTV how long the closure would last. For regular visitors, the project means they will have to find another stretch of sand until the work is complete. Other beach options include Singer Island to the north, as well as Phipps Beach and Lake Worth Beach to the south. When WPTV reporter Joel Lopez asked Greenberg where she might go during the closure, she didn't have an alternative in mind. 'No, you're going to have to tell me where to go,' she said. entry.title: Port St. Lucie residents weigh in on proposed Prima Vista Boulevard safety changes - WPEC
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie residents weigh in on proposed Prima Vista Boulevard safety changes    WPEC
entry.article_text: Lucie community members had a chance to learn more about and comment on proposed safety changes to Prima Vista Boulevard during a county information session at the MidFlorida Credit Union Event Center Thursday. The proposal focuses on the stretch between Aroso Boulevard and U.S. It would replace the center turn lane with a raised median and add landscaping designed to make the road feel narrower and encourage drivers to slow down. A majority of the community members spoke out against the plan, saying they don't believe the changes would improve safety. County officials say the changes are intended to improve safety, reduce crashes, and help slow traffic along the corridor. "We understand it's not popular. That's why we have these," said St. Lucie County engineer Dan Zrallack. "We're taking away the ease of access for people who live along this corridor. There's a lot of driveways. There's a lot of residences that have historically been able to turn directly into their driveway. It's no longer safe to do that. We have to control the traffic so that we have less accidents." County staff estimate the project could cost about $6.1 million dollars, but don't know where that money would come from yet. See also: Jupiter woman sues DoorDash, alleges delivery driver sexually assaulted her County leaders said feedback from the meeting will help shape the project. The proposal is in the early stages. Lucie County still needs to design the roadway, and identify funding sources before any work can move forward. Residents who couldn’t attend the workshop can review plans and submit comments to Christopher.arnold@stlucieco.gov.

entry.title: Policyholder advocates warn Florida homeowners of insurance challenges after Hurricane Isaias
entry.summary: As homeowners in Florida's Panhandle begin navigating insurance claims after Hurricane Isaias , policyholder advocates are sounding a warning. 'The storm after the storm is already on the way,' says Doug Quinn of the American Policyholder Association. 'An insurance system that charges more, covers less, and too often fails homeowners when they need it most.' WATCH BELOW: 'Storm after the storm': Advocates warn homeowners about insurance claims Advocates warn Florida homeowners about insurance claims after Hurricane Isaias Quinn's organization, along with Rebuild: The National Disaster Survivors Association, says insurance companies may leave many homeowners with denied claims and reduced benefits. 'America is facing a home insurance affordability crisis, and Florida families are on the front line,' said Quinn, who is currently in the Panhandle to assist homeowners. The insurance industry responded to the comments by strongly denying them. 'Bottom line is legitimate claims are not being denied,' Mark Friedlander of the Insurance Information Institute said. 'If a storm loss is covered by your wind storm coverage in your home insurance policy, those claims are covered.' Leaders in Tallahassee and insurance executives insist the insurance landscape in Florida is improving with lower rates as more insurers enter the market after litigation reforms. A poll released by the University of North Florida in September revealed that 63% of Floridians are more concerned about insurance costs than property taxes.

entry.summary: Martin County Sheriff’s Office investigates fatal shooting in Hobe Sound    WPBF
entry.article_text: A shooting in the Banner Lake area of Hobe Sound on Wednesday night left one person dead, according to the Martin County Sheriff’s Office. Deputies responded to the scene along Southeast Citrus Way and spent hours investigating. Authorities said one person was detained for questioning. Harriet Ford Greg, who said the victim was her grandson, shared that he lived with her. She recalled hearing three gunshots while she was in bed and immediately worrying about him, knowing he was out that night. When she stepped outside, she said she saw him on the ground as first responders tried to save him. " laying on the ground out there and the police officer was reviving him," Greg said. "I thought that he's not going to make it. Somebody shot him." entry.title: Will Port St. Lucie see more floods this weekend? - cw34.com
entry.summary: Will Port St. Lucie see more floods this weekend?    cw34.com
entry.article_text: This weekend we're expected to see more heavy rain in our area. This may be exactly the kind of weekend forecast that many people in Port St. Lucie do not want to hear. Last week, parts of the city flooded when torrential rains hit Port St. According to our Stormtrac meteorologists, the city got about four inches of rain in a 48 hour period last week. Roads turned into lakes, water levels in canals rose quickly, and some drivers took their chances and drove through standing water deep enough to possibly leave them stalled with nowhere to go. One homeowner, who has a canal directly behind his house, says he was stunned to see the extent of the flooding. It was the worst he's seen in the two years he's lived in Port St. See also: Trump expected at Mar-a-Lago as Palm Beach road closures, No Kings rallies are planned "When I came out, I was like, Oh, my God! I've never seen it like this before!" said Peter Rodriguez, who lives at the intersection of SW Todd Avenue and SW Broadview Street in Port St. How concerned is he about the possibility of another flood this weekend? "I don't think it's gonna get that high. If it starts getting that high, then I'm gonna start to pray. Not another flood," he said. Luckily floodwater did not get into his house. But the water was deep enough he says, to prevent him from driving out of his driveway. One resident says he feels the city of Port St. Lucie could be doing more to prevent such flooding. "I really think they should do something, I mean really to take care of business, you know because we pay our taxes," said Frank Camarda, a Port St. Lucie resident on SW Leisure Lane. A city spokesman says they'll have Public Works employees on standby this weekend if heavy rain comes, if they need to clear storm drains or move pumps into position to lower water levels in certain areas such as near the intersection of Savona Boulevard and SW California Boulevard. That area has been prone to flooding in the past. "They've been monitoring the canals and the retention ponds. And again, they haven't had to lower them this week which is a good sign. They're where they think they need to be. So, we're as prepared as we can be. You never know what Mother Nature is going to throw at you, but this team is doing everything it can to try to to mitigate the risks as much as possible," said Scott Samples, Strategic Communications Manager and Public Information Officer, city of Port St. He says the city of Port St. Lucie received no reports last week that floodwaters got into any homes or businesses.

entry.title: 'He just tried to ram me': Port St. Lucie man arrested after a chase ends on South Hutchinson Island - WPBF
entry.summary: 'He just tried to ram me': Port St. Lucie man arrested after a chase ends on South Hutchinson Island    WPBF
entry.article_text: Lucie man was arrested Thursday night after leading St. Lucie County deputies on a high-speed chase that ended on South Hutchinson Island. The pursuit began in the 9600 block of South Ocean Boulevard when a Patrol Operations deputy attempted to stop the driver of a pickup truck for a traffic violation. Andrew Bolonka, the director of communications for the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office, said the driver fled instead of stopping, making a U-turn and spinning donuts in the roadway, forcing other motorists to take evasive action. Deep Dive: WPBF 25 News Investigates After briefly stopping, the driver made another U-turn, cut across lanes of traffic, and accelerated toward the deputy's patrol vehicle. "The deputy tries to stop the vehicle; all of a sudden, the vehicle lunges, takes off, accelerates, does another U-turn, and then starts allegedly heading straight toward the deputy. Which you can see in the body-worn camera, where the deputy makes an evasive maneuver and says, 'Oh, he almost hit me,'" Bolonka said. Members of the department's Special Investigations Unit and deputies in the air assisted in the pursuit. The driver continued to flee even after stop sticks were deployed. Deputies eventually executed a PIT maneuver along Seaway Drive, bringing the vehicle to a stop. Despite repeated verbal commands to exit the truck, the driver refused, prompting deputies to deploy pepper balls into the vehicle. The driver then surrendered and was taken into custody without further incident. The suspect, identified as 37-year-old Joshua Gallagher of Port St. Lucie, faces several charges, including aggravated assault with a deadly weapon, possession of a controlled substance without a prescription, and resisting arrest without violence. He remains in custody at the St. "When people make decisions like this, and they commit an act that puts not only the deputies and other law enforcement officers in peril, but they are also putting the general public in peril. If we can do so safely, we're going to put it to an end," Bolonka said. Authorities expressed relief that no one was injured during the incident. entry.title: Port St. Lucie ICU nurse arrested on charges involving patient's IV - WPBF
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie ICU nurse arrested on charges involving patient's IV    WPBF
entry.article_text: A 54-year-old Jupiter woman is facing felony charges after she allegedly removed fentanyl from a critically ill patient's IV infusion while working at Cleveland Clinic Tradition Hospital, the Port St. Lucie Police Department said Monday. On Thursday, Leslie Pope was arrested in Jupiter in conjunction with the Palm Beach Marshals Task Force and faces three felonies: grand theft of a controlled substance, possession of a controlled substance without a prescription and fraudulently obtaining a controlled substance. Pope was booked into the Palm Beach County Jail on Thursday morning on an out-of-county warrant. She was released on Saturday morning after posting an original bond of $150,000. Pope is not an inmate at the St. "We take these allegations very seriously," Cleveland Clinic spokeswoman Rebecca Astorga told WPBF in a statement. "She individual no longer works with us, and we are fully cooperating with law enforcement. Because this is an active investigation, we are unable to comment further at this time." https://www.facebook.com/PortStLuciePolice/posts/pfbid02W5HqPQihHo4JSGqHsePU1wjBMmTubGN5HyptojT8wtSJU5Pft8YBVYsKgckEN7mDl Port St. Lucie police arrested Pope after an investigation into the allegations. Investigators learned a family member reported witnessing Pope use a syringe to withdraw fluid from the patient's fentanyl infusion, place the syringe in her pocket and leave the room. Pope was not assigned to the patient's care. The next evening, Pope allegedly returned to the patient's room and again approached the IV equipment, police said. The family member intervened. Detectives later reviewed video footage that shows Pope manipulating protective caps on the equipment. No additional medication was removed during the second incident, according to investigators. A 15-page arrest affidavit includes witness interviews, hospital video footage, medical and administrative records, medication transaction reviews and coordination with the Drug Enforcement Administration. "PSLPD takes allegations of criminal misconduct seriously, particularly when they involve individuals entrusted with the safety and well-being of others," the police agency said in a news release. "We remain committed to thorough, evidence-based investigations and pursuing accountability when the evidence supports criminal charges." This remains an active criminal case. entry.title: 33 years after uncle's murder, family asks Gov. Ron DeSantis to sign killer's death warrant
entry.summary: Thirty-three years after his uncle was murdered, Brian Kunkel is still waiting for what he considers justice. 'There's a whole host of emotions with this,' Kunkel said. 'There's a tremendous amount of anger, and now as we speak, it kind of starts to build back up again.' WATCH BELOW: 'It's time': Family seeks execution 33 years after loved one murdered Family seeks execution 33 years after man killed in West Palm Beach His uncle, Richard Kunkel, was a 32-year-old local florist remembered by his family as outgoing, generous and full of life. 'Richard was a fun-loving guy,' Brian Kunkel said. 'He had a great spirit. Very friendly. Very outgoing the type of person that literally would give you the shirt off his back.' In 1993, Richard Kunkel went to Roosters nightclub in West Palm Beach. Court records show Ronald Knight and two other men went to the gay bar looking for a man to lure away, rob and beat. 'This was all premeditated,' Brian Kunkel said. 'He knew what he was doing.' Court records show the men befriended Kunkel and convinced him to leave with them. Knight then drove him to a secluded area, where he shot and killed him. The men robbed Kunkel, stole his car and burglarized his home. 'Richard begged for his life,' Brian Kunkel said. 'He pleaded not to be shot. He was murdered in cold blood.' Two years later, Knight was charged in another killing. In May 1995, 22-year-old Brendan Meehan was lured from Heartbreakers, then a gay nightclub on Olive Avenue in West Palm Beach, taken to a secluded area and killed. Knight was convicted of both murders and sentenced to death in 1998. 'These people had purposes in life, and it's gone,' Kunkel said. A family waiting for an execution More than three decades after Richard Kunkel's murder, Knight remains on death row. Now, Kunkel is asking Gov. Ron DeSantis to sign his death warrant. 'It's been a long and arduous process,' he said. 'My grandparents are gone. They've passed without closure, and I know, at least in my grandmother's case, she died of really a broken heart.' 'This needs to be done. It needs to be finalized,' Kunkel added. His request comes as Florida carries out executions at a pace rarely seen in the state. Florida executed a record 19 people in 2025. Seventeen people have been executed so far in 2026, with two more executions scheduled. 'Richard was a fun-loving guy,' Brian Kunkel said. 'He had a great spirit. Very friendly. Very outgoing the type of person that literally would give you the shirt off his back.' In 1993, Richard Kunkel went to Roosters nightclub in West Palm Beach. Court records show Ronald Knight and two other men went to the gay bar looking for a man to lure away, rob and beat. 'This was all premeditated,' Brian Kunkel said. 'He knew what he was doing.' Court records show the men befriended Kunkel and convinced him to leave with them. Knight then drove him to a secluded area, where he shot and killed him. The men robbed Kunkel, stole his car and burglarized his home. 'Richard begged for his life,' Brian Kunkel said. 'He pleaded not to be shot. He was murdered in cold blood.' Two years later, Knight was charged in another killing. In May 1995, 22-year-old Brendan Meehan was lured from Heartbreakers, then a gay nightclub on Olive Avenue in West Palm Beach, taken to a secluded area and killed. Knight was convicted of both murders and sentenced to death in 1998. 'These people had purposes in life, and it's gone,' Kunkel said. 'This needs to be done. It needs to be finalized,' Kunkel added. His request comes as Florida carries out executions at a pace rarely seen in the state. Florida executed a record 19 people in 2025. Seventeen people have been executed so far in 2026, with two more executions scheduled. entry.title: Will Port St. Lucie see more floods this weekend? - WPEC
entry.summary: Will Port St. Lucie see more floods this weekend?    WPEC
entry.article_text: This weekend we're expected to see more heavy rain in our area. This may be exactly the kind of weekend forecast that many people in Port St. Lucie do not want to hear. Last week, parts of the city flooded when torrential rains hit Port St. According to our Stormtrac meteorologists, the city got about four inches of rain in a 48 hour period last week. Roads turned into lakes, water levels in canals rose quickly, and some drivers took their chances and drove through standing water deep enough to possibly leave them stalled with nowhere to go. One homeowner, who has a canal directly behind his house, says he was stunned to see the extent of the flooding. It was the worst he's seen in the two years he's lived in Port St. See also: Trump expected at Mar-a-Lago as Palm Beach road closures, No Kings rallies are planned "When I came out, I was like, Oh, my God! I've never seen it like this before!" said Peter Rodriguez, who lives at the intersection of SW Todd Avenue and SW Broadview Street in Port St. How concerned is he about the possibility of another flood this weekend? "I don't think it's gonna get that high. If it starts getting that high, then I'm gonna start to pray. Not another flood," he said. Luckily floodwater did not get into his house. But the water was deep enough he says, to prevent him from driving out of his driveway. One resident says he feels the city of Port St. Lucie could be doing more to prevent such flooding. "I really think they should do something, I mean really to take care of business, you know because we pay our taxes," said Frank Camarda, a Port St. Lucie resident on SW Leisure Lane. A city spokesman says they'll have Public Works employees on standby this weekend if heavy rain comes, if they need to clear storm drains or move pumps into position to lower water levels in certain areas such as near the intersection of Savona Boulevard and SW California Boulevard. That area has been prone to flooding in the past. "They've been monitoring the canals and the retention ponds. And again, they haven't had to lower them this week which is a good sign. They're where they think they need to be. So, we're as prepared as we can be. You never know what Mother Nature is going to throw at you, but this team is doing everything it can to try to to mitigate the risks as much as possible," said Scott Samples, Strategic Communications Manager and Public Information Officer, city of Port St. He says the city of Port St. Lucie received no reports last week that floodwaters got into any homes or businesses.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie tests new water sensors as weekend rain threatens flood-prone areas - WFLX
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie tests new water sensors as weekend rain threatens flood-prone areas    WFLX
entry.article_text: More rain is expected this weekend across South Florida and the Treasure Coast, and WPTV is learning that Port St. Lucie Public Works is preparing. Scott Samples, communications manager with the City of Port St. Lucie, said crews spent the week clearing debris from drains and grates. Lucie prepares for rain, flooding concerns Samples added that water levels in retention ponds and canals are at an adequate level and won't need to be lowered. Staff have also been testing their new pilot water sensors, which will send alerts to select staff if water levels rise. "It's a way for us to respond faster to very specific locations," Samples said. Jennifer Collins, owner of Pets Play Grooming off California and Savona boulevards, said her staff is preparing too. "We're nervous about this storm coming up this week," Collins said. "Every time it rains, we get scared." Collins is no stranger to flooding on California and Savona boulevards. She said flooding has occurred there for years. WPTV was there when water levels rose at the intersection last week. Collins said she already sent messages to her customers for Saturday. "We may have to reschedule their dogs. We may have to push them off to next week," Collins said. "Saturdays are one of our busiest days, so it does really affect us as a small business." For long-term solutions at the intersection, the city is working on a large-scale drainage project for the Oak Hammock neighborhood, which includes raising portions of the roadway. "When this project is completed, those problems won't be problems anymore," Samples said. The drainage project is still in data collection before moving on to design. "We can't work if it's raining, and that's in Florida," Collins said. "That's just not OK." The project may take years until completion, but Collins said she already thought about moving her business. "We've also talked about possibly moving, and you know that would be hard too," Collins said. "I just feel like it's not, not getting better."

entry.summary: Prima Vista Boulevard safety plan in St. Lucie County would add raised median after 578 crashes since 2020    WPTV
entry.article_text: Lucie County staff are sharing designs and want to hear input from neighbors about a proposed project on Prima Vista Boulevard.WATCH BELOW: Neighbors weigh in on Prima Vista Boulevard changesThey plan to improve a section of the roadway from Airoso Boulevard to U.S. Highway 1 by removing the center left turn lanesDan Zrallack, county engineer, said their plan is to replace the center left-turn lanes with a raised median."The center turn lane is often referred to as a suicide lane," Zrallack said. "The more turning movements you have, the more chances you have for accidents by restricting access and putting in the median turn lanes. We can kind of control where those turning movements are and protect the drivers as well as pedestrians walking along the roadway." According to the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office, there have been 578 crashes on that section of the Prima Vista Boulevard since 2020. Zrallack said the median will make the road safer.

entry.title: South Florida fitness company brings personal trainers directly to clients
entry.summary: Having access to a gym is one thing. Actually using it is another. For Jennifer Frink, working out at home means avoiding some of the things she dislikes about going to a traditional gym. WATCH BELOW: Fitness at Your Door brings fitness trainers to your doorstep Fitness at Your Door: South Florida fitness company brings personal trainers directly to clients 'I don't really like the gym, and I usually work out at home,' Frink said. 'You don't have to wait for machines or deal with people at the gym if you don't want to.' It's one of the barriers Kashawn Fraser is trying to address through Fitness at Your Door, a South Florida wellness company that brings personal trainers directly to clients. Fraser said the company has grown to more than 250 certified personal trainers who undergo background checks, serving clients from Miami to Jupiter. The program is also expanding to the Treasure Coast. 'You can order Uber food to your door ... but to have someone show up for you where it matters the most, that's why this company was born,' Fraser said. WPTV reporter Christy Waite connected with Fraser to learn why he founded the organization. After playing professional football in the Canadian Football League and having multiple knee surgeries, he shifted his focus from his own fitness to helping others with theirs. 'I had three reconstructive knee surgeries back to back,' Fraser said. 'I have been in your shoes. I've been hurt, I've been down, I've been out of shape, I've been in shape.' For clients like Frink, having a trainer come to them can also take some of the anxiety out of going to a gym. 'You don't want to be on one of those YouTube videos where you are doing it wrong, and people are laughing at you,' Frink said. The program also works with people living in 55-and-older communities. Fraser said staying active can be especially meaningful for people approaching retirement who want the energy to enjoy time with their families. 'You work so hard to get to retirement to enjoy your kids and grandkids and have the best energy you can,' Fraser said. Across residential communities, gyms, fitness centers and clubhouses can go underused, even though residents have those amenities close to home. Fraser saw an opportunity to bring the workout into those spaces by having personal trainers meet clients where they already live.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie residents weigh in on proposed Prima Vista Boulevard safety changes - WPEC
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie residents weigh in on proposed Prima Vista Boulevard safety changes    WPEC
entry.article_text: Lucie community members had a chance to learn more about and comment on proposed safety changes to Prima Vista Boulevard during a county information session at the MidFlorida Credit Union Event Center Thursday. The proposal focuses on the stretch between Aroso Boulevard and U.S. It would replace the center turn lane with a raised median and add landscaping designed to make the road feel narrower and encourage drivers to slow down. A majority of the community members spoke out against the plan, saying they don't believe the changes would improve safety. County officials say the changes are intended to improve safety, reduce crashes, and help slow traffic along the corridor. "We understand it's not popular. That's why we have these," said St. Lucie County engineer Dan Zrallack. "We're taking away the ease of access for people who live along this corridor. There's a lot of driveways. There's a lot of residences that have historically been able to turn directly into their driveway. It's no longer safe to do that. We have to control the traffic so that we have less accidents." County staff estimate the project could cost about $6.1 million dollars, but don't know where that money would come from yet. See also: Jupiter woman sues DoorDash, alleges delivery driver sexually assaulted her County leaders said feedback from the meeting will help shape the project. The proposal is in the early stages. Lucie County still needs to design the roadway, and identify funding sources before any work can move forward. Residents who couldn’t attend the workshop can review plans and submit comments to Christopher.arnold@stlucieco.gov.

entry.title: Amendment 3 could bring rush of Florida homebuyers, impact property values
entry.summary: Amendment 3 aims to change the property tax structure in Florida by saving money for homeowners and cutting revenue for cities and counties. It could also have an impact on the Florida real estate market. A 2025 study by Realtor.com suggests home values in Florida could rise 7% to 9% if the referendum passes, and some real estate professionals say there will likely be an impact. WATCH BELOW: Amendment 3 could shake up Florida housing market Amendment 3 and Real Estate 'I don't see them going up to like the 7, 8, 9, 10 percent,' says Jeff Lichtenstein of Echo Fine Properties in Palm Beach Gardens. However, he does see a possible rush of buyers entering the market. 'You better be prepared because if it happens, it will happen fast,' Lichtenstein said. 'I think there will be a mad rush to get in here, because if not, then you're waiting five years.' That's because the referendum requires homeowners to be homesteaded in Florida by Dec 31 to receive the full tax savings right away. New home buyers entering the state would have a five-year waiting period to get the full homestead exemption.
