entry.title: AmeriCorps returns to Martin County with renewed focus on boosting students' reading skills - WFLX
entry.summary: AmeriCorps returns to Martin County with renewed focus on boosting students' reading skills    WFLX
entry.article_text: A program that has worked with thousands of Martin County children is returning after a brief hiatus, with a renewed focus on helping young students strengthen their reading skills. The Boys Girls Clubs of Martin County is celebrating the return of its AmeriCorps program, which places volunteers directly with students to provide individualized and small-group academic support. WATCH BELOW: Literacy program returns to Martin County after hiatus “We missed it. It was an extremely important piece to our success and moving the district forward,” Martin County Schools Superintendent Michael Maine said. The Boys Girls Clubs of Martin County first introduced the federal mentorship program to the area in 2019. For six years, AmeriCorps volunteers worked with thousands of local students before federal funding shortfalls forced the program to pause. Now, program leaders have set new goals for its return. WPTV reporter Christy Waite connected with AmeriCorps Program Director for Martin County Boys and Girls Club, Russell Lamberti. “We want to serve 575 students, and we want to see an increase of 65% growth, and that can be in vocabulary, fluency and grammar,” AmeriCorps Program Director Russell Lamberti said. AmeriCorps volunteers will work one-on-one and in small groups with kindergarten through fifth-grade students at four Boys Girls Club locations, with an emphasis on literacy. For AmeriCorps Volunteer Experience Specialist Abelard Cesar, the mission also has a personal connection. I learned English at 13 years old, and I had mentors that helped me grow,” Cesar said. The Boys Girls Clubs says the program delivered significant academic results during its previous six-year run. In some cases, as many as eight in 10 participating students moved their reading from Level 1 to Level 4. About the same percentage maintained or improved their English Language Arts grades, according to the organization. The organization said students also showed improvements in literacy rates, assessment scores, school attendance and behavioral patterns. AmeriCorps members’ work previously extended beyond the classroom. According to the Boys Girls Clubs, volunteers completed nearly 50 service projects in Martin County and contributed more than 60,000 hours to community cleanup efforts and other acts of service. The return comes as literacy remains a focus across the county. Earlier this year, the Martin County School District reported that local kindergarten students tied for fourth place statewide in readiness scores and literacy assessments. The AmeriCorps program is part of a broader academic effort by the Boys Girls Clubs of Martin County, which serves more than 1,000 members ages 6 to 18 in its daily programs. The organization also provides after-school academic assistance through certified teachers. Beyond its Clubs, the organization runs or manages several programs serving local children, including Reading Buddies, Character Counts!, career training using virtual reality technology, culinary programs and skilled-trades programs. With AmeriCorps volunteers returning, the Boys Girls Clubs says it hopes to build on the program’s previous results while giving more Martin County students the individual attention and support they need.

entry.title: Do you know the difference between a macaroon and a macaron?
entry.summary: Do you know the difference between a macaroon and a macaron? WPTVs Christy Waite visited the GreenMarket in downtown West Palm Beach, where she learned the difference between the two and caught up with a popular local vendor making its return after a yearlong hiatus. WATCH: Do you know the difference between a macaroon and a macaron? Small business Saturday The West Palm Beach GreenMarket is more than a weekend destination. For local entrepreneurs like Jonathan Aviv, it has also provided a place to grow a small business. Aviv is the owner and master baker behind Macaroner, a small French macaron bakery offering both traditional, vegan, and gluten-free macarons in 24 flavors. Aviv said he decided to turn his love for macarons into a business during the COVID-19 pandemic. Getting the recipe right, however, took plenty of trial and error. It took a long time, thousands of macarons thrown away and wasted in the process, but eventually I cracked the code, Aviv said. For six years, Macaroner has called South Florida and Palm Beach County home. At Avivs booth, customers can find an assortment of colorful flavors, including lemon basil and salted caramel. But Aviv said theres one flavor he is especially proud of and that's his lavender honey. The lavender is a classic French flavor and he uses Mnuka honey from New Zealand. After nearly four years at the GreenMarket, Macaroner took a yearlong hiatus to focus on wholesale business. This season, the bakery is back. Aviv said he typically prepares between 1,000 and 2,000 macarons for a day at the GreenMarket so he doesn't run out of flavors. Some flavors are especially popular with younger customers. The kids go for the fun and cute flavors like birthday cake, Fruity Tooty, strawberry hibiscus and Oreo cookie, Aviv said. Aviv said he is excited to be back at the GreenMarket, where his customers dont just come from Palm Beach County. We get people from out of state who come here to purchase them. Then they take them home because they dont have something like this where they live.

entry.title: Palm Beach County ‘No Kings’ rally urges early voting
entry.summary: Protesters gathered in Palm Beach County as part of a nationwide No Kings day of action, with local organizers putting a focus on encouraging people to vote early ahead of the November midterm elections. The rally was organized locally by Speaking Up for America - Indivisible. Group leader Susan Foley said Saturdays demonstration marked the organizations eighth rally in two years and its fourth No Kings rally. Today is a special day, our fourth No Kings rally, Foley said. This one is special because of its mission to vote early. WATCH: Palm Beach County No Kings rally urges early voting No Kings Rally Foley said organizers are encouraging people to cast their ballots early rather than waiting until Election Day. If you vote early, your vote is locked in, Foley said. But for protesters who came out Saturday, the rally was also an opportunity to speak about issues they would like to see addressed both nationally and closer to home. WPTV's Christy Waite listened to protesters like Ann Hunter. She says she wants to see more attention paid to the financial challenges facing families. More consideration to the middle class and people that are in desperate circumstances struggling with their food, healthcare, everyday living expenses, Hunter said. For Cynthia Heller, a former educator, education funding is among the issues that brought her out. I was in education, so I would like to see more money go into education, Heller said. Protesters said events like Saturdays also give members of the community an opportunity to come together around issues that are important to them. One protester emphasized that regardless of political affiliation, participating in the election is what matters. I am happy to see people here, and no matter how they vote, they have to vote, the protester said. Similar demonstrations have taken place across the region, from Palm Beach County to Vero Beach, as protesters continue to make their voices heard ahead of the November elections.

entry.title: Man found dead after barricade situation in St. Lucie County, deputies say
entry.summary: A man was found dead from an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound Saturday after a barricade situation prompted deputies to evacuate a woman and children from a St. Lucie County home, according to the sheriffs office. The St. Lucie County Sheriffs Office said deputies responded around 10:17 a.m. to a reported domestic violence incident in the 7600 block of Winter Garden Boulevard. Deputies initially encountered a man in the front yard who went back inside after seeing law enforcement. Authorities later made contact with a man and woman at the front door. During that interaction, a deputy saw what appeared to be a firearm in the mans possession and ordered him to drop it, the sheriffs office said. Instead, the man closed the door and retreated inside, creating a barricaded-subject situation while other people remained in the home. According to investigators, the man came outside several times and said he would surrender after making a phone call, but repeatedly went back inside. During his final retreat into the home, deputies heard what appeared to be a gunshot. Knowing an adult woman and children were still inside and could be in danger, deputies entered the residence and evacuated them through a side window, the sheriffs office said. Deputies later found the man dead from what appeared to be a self-inflicted gunshot wound. Authorities said there is no ongoing threat to the community. Detectives, crime scene technicians and investigators from the Medical Examiners Office are expected to remain at the scene for several hours as the investigation continues.

entry.title: Young Stuart divers take a leap toward college scholarships, international competition and Olympic dreams
entry.summary: In life, they say, take a leap of faith. Well, a group of kids in Stuart are doing just that on a diving board. WATCH BELOW: Stuart divers take leap toward big dreams Stuart's Atlantic Diving Team teaches the Olympic sport of diving to kids of all ages,experience levels 'There are different things for different people. Some people prefer platform diving, which is much higher but fun, which I prefer. Something Ive grown to love is all the friendships that I make throughout the years,' said Grace Erickson, a local diver, who admits diving has always been her passion. 'On my preschool poster I wrote what I wanted to be when I got older was a diver,' Erickson said. That preschooler who could only dream of being a diver is fulfilling her dream as an eighth grader. 'Its been really exciting; it's new things every twist and turn, both in your head and diving off the board,' Erickson said. Her longtime coach, Osvaldo 'Pito' Alberty, thanks her for her courage and wants to see Erickson and her teammates take the sport to new levels. 'We are like a family here. We treat each other with respect and courtesy, and we push each other to do better than everyone else,' said Pito, whose passion is sharing his experience, knowledge and love for diving with young athletes with the Atlantic Diving Team in Stuart. Atlantic takes divers of all ages, backgrounds and experience levels and teaches them the Olympic sport of diving. 'The younger we get them, the better it is because over time they can get scholarships. If they want to do international diving, they can qualify for international competitions or even the Olympics,' Pito said. For divers like Erickson, she wants to take her talents to the college level, but there's a new diver whos just learning the sport, Carissa Smith. 'I was recently a gymnast and just about two months ago I started diving,' said Smith. Smith is a natural-born acrobat. At 14, she hasn't participated in her first competition because she wants to learn the basics. But for now, she admits diving is pretty fun. 'It feels like you're flying; it's exhilarating just being able to get better at my diving,' said Smith.

entry.article_text: Protesters gathered in Palm Beach County as part of a nationwide “No Kings” day of action, with local organizers putting a focus on encouraging people to vote early ahead of the November midterm elections.The rally was organized locally by Speaking Up for America - Indivisible. Group leader Susan Foley said Saturday’s demonstration marked the organization’s eighth rally in two years and its fourth No Kings rally.“Today is a special day, our fourth No Kings rally,” Foley said. “This one is special because of its mission to vote early.”WATCH: Palm Beach County ‘No Kings’ rally urges early votingFoley said organizers are encouraging people to cast their ballots early rather than waiting until Election Day.“If you vote early, your vote is locked in,” Foley said.But for protesters who came out Saturday, the rally was also an opportunity to speak about issues they would like to see addressed both nationally and closer to home.WPTV's Christy Waite listened to protesters like Ann Hunter. She says she wants to see more attention paid to the financial challenges facing families.“More consideration to the middle class and people that are in desperate circumstances struggling with their food, healthcare, everyday living expenses,” Hunter said.For Cynthia Heller, a former educator, education funding is among the issues that brought her out.“I was in education, so I would like to see more money go into education,” Heller said.Protesters said events like Saturday’s also give members of the community an opportunity to come together around issues that are important to them.One protester emphasized that regardless of political affiliation, participating in the election is what matters.“I am happy to see people here, and no matter how they vote, they have to vote,” the protester said.The Republican Party of Palm Beach County also responded to Saturday’s demonstrations, pointing to Republican policies and the party’s growing voter registration advantage in Florida.In a statement, the county GOP credited Gov. Ron DeSantis’ policies with Florida’s economic performance and highlighted Amendment 3, a proposed constitutional amendment on the November ballot dealing with property taxes.The party also defended President Donald Trump’s approach to judicial appointments and said Republican voter registration and turnout show support for the party’s direction.“Florida has transitioned into a reliably red state, with the Republican Party of Florida maintaining an advantage of over 1.55 million registered voters over Democrats,” the statement said.State voter registration data as of Sept. 30 shows more than 5.67 million active registered Republicans compared with about 4.13 million Democrats, a difference of roughly 1.55 million voters.Amendment 3 would reduce the annual cap on assessment increases for non-homestead properties from 10% to 5% and make other changes involving how counties and municipalities use property tax revenue.Similar demonstrations have taken place across the region, from Palm Beach County to Vero Beach, as protesters continue to make their voices heard ahead of the November elections.

entry.title: Man dies by suicide after barricaded-subject SWAT situation in Fort Pierce - WPEC
entry.summary: Man dies by suicide after barricaded-subject SWAT situation in Fort Pierce    WPEC
entry.article_text: A man was found dead from an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound after deputies responded to a reported domestic violence incident Saturday morning in Fort Pierce's Lakewood Park neighborhood. Deputies responded around 10:17 a.m. to a home in the 7600 block of Winter Garden Boulevard, where they encountered a man in the front yard. The man went back inside after seeing law enforcement, according to the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office . Deputies say they later contacted a man and woman at the front door. A deputy saw what appeared to be a firearm in the man's possession and ordered him to drop the weapon, but he shut the door and retreated inside, prompting a barricaded-subject situation with other occupants still in the home. See also: Driver tried to ram deputy before PIT maneuver ended chase, SLCSO says During the incident, the man reportedly came outside several times and indicated he would surrender after making a phone call, but repeatedly went back inside, deputies said. During his final retreat into the home, deputies say they heard what appeared to be a gunshot. Concerned for an adult woman and children who remained inside, deputies entered the home without alerting the occupants and evacuated them through a side window, according to the sheriff's office. Deputies later found the man dead from what appeared to be a self-inflicted gunshot wound. The sheriff's office said there is no ongoing threat to the community. Detectives with the agency's Criminal Investigations Division, crime scene technicians and investigators from the Medical Examiner's Office remained at the scene to investigate the circumstances surrounding the incident. If you or someone you know is struggling with thoughts of suicide, help is available. Call or text 988 to reach the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline , available 24/7. You can also chat at 988lifeline.org

entry.title: St. Lucie County voters to decide on sales tax renewal, mosquito control expansion - WPBF
entry.summary: St. Lucie County voters to decide on sales tax renewal, mosquito control expansion    WPBF
entry.article_text: Lucie County voters will decide in November on two ballot questions aimed at addressing the county's growing population and its impact on infrastructure and services. The first question asks voters to renew the half-cent sales tax, originally approved in 2018, which is set to expire in two years. County leaders are seeking to extend the tax for another decade. This is not a new tax but would keep the total sales tax rate at 7%, with the half-cent portion funding infrastructure projects such as road improvements, sidewalks, stormwater drainage, and major projects like widening St. "Now we're seeing that impact, you know, the delayed maintenance and the increased growth we've seen picked up, we're starting to have to play catch-up with those infrastructure projects and the needs are still there," said Erick Gill, communications director for St. The second question focuses on expanding the mosquito control district to include the Tradition and southwestern areas of the county, which have grown beyond the current service boundaries. Currently, mosquito control services cover about half of the county's 600 square miles. If voters approve the expansion, affected property owners would pay about $28 more annually in taxes to fund fogging, spraying, and mosquito surveillance. Both measures will appear on the November ballot, addressing different needs as St. Lucie County continues to grow. Voters are encouraged to review their sample ballots to determine which questions apply to them before voting on Nov. entry.title: President Trump returns to Palm Beach as midterm elections approach
entry.summary: President Donald Trump returned to Palm Beach on Friday for his first trip of the season to Mar-a-Lago, bringing the heightened security and traffic impacts that accompany presidential visits as the country moves closer to the 2026 midterm elections. Trump arrived in South Florida after campaigning Friday in Dalton, Georgia, where he rallied alongside Republican candidates as the party works to turn out voters ahead of Election Day. WPTV saw supporters lining the route toward Trump's Mar-a-Lago estate as his motorcade traveled through Palm Beach. Among them was the Campbell family, who had traveled from South Carolina for a baseball tournament. 'I wasn't expecting this on my bingo card. I thought we were playing baseball,' one member of the Campbell family told WPTV. 'But I'm glad we get to see this.' Trump pushes Republican voters to turn out Trump's arrival came directly after his campaign stop at Dalton Municipal Airport in Georgia, where he appeared with Republican U.S. Senate candidate Mike Collins and gubernatorial candidate Rick Jackson. The Georgia Senate race has become a significant midterm battleground. Recent polling has shown Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff leading Collins. Trump stressed the importance of turnout during his remarks. 'When I'm not on the ballot, I guess it's a compliment, but people don't show up so much,' Trump said. 'So this is, really, I think the most important midterm election I think we've ever had.' The president also told supporters in Dalton that they should 'pretend I'm on the ballot' as he sought to boost Republican enthusiasm. Security increases around Palm Beach Back in Palm Beach, security was heightened around the island ahead of Trump's arrival. Palm Beach County Sheriff Ric Bradshaw recently told WPTV's Michael Hoffman that the county received an exemption allowing license plate reader cameras to remain on state roads as an additional layer of presidential protection. 'We filed a brief with the Department of Highway Safety up there in Tallahassee that, along with the Secret Service, and says, 'Hey, this is why we can't take them down,' and they granted us that exemption,' Bradshaw said. More presidential travel could mean traffic impacts Trump was expected to travel to Kentucky on Saturday before returning to Palm Beach later in the day, according to information provided to WPTV. Those movements are expected to bring additional closures and traffic impacts as the presidential motorcade travels through the area. Tru

entry.summary: All northbound lanes of Florida's Turnpike in Martin County are back open Friday afternoon after a jackknifed semi caused heavy delays. The crash happened shortly before noon near mile marker 125, underneath the SE Bridge Road overpass. Watch traffic camera video: Semi crash on Florida Turnpike According to the Florida Highway Patrol, the truck driver lost control, causing the crash. Paramedics took one patient with minor injuries to the hospital by ground, according to Martin County Fire Rescue spokeswoman Jillian Kay. Lanes started reopening to traffic just after 1 p.m. on Friday. Kay said that the Martin County Sheriff's Office and Florida Highway Patrol also responded to the wreck and will investigate.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie tests new water sensors as weekend rain threatens flood-prone areas
entry.summary: More rain is expected this weekend across South Florida and the Treasure Coast, and WPTV is learning that Port St. Lucie Public Works is preparing. Scott Samples, communications manager with the City of Port St. Lucie, said crews spent the week clearing debris from drains and grates. WATCH BELOW: Port St. Lucie prepares for rain, flooding concerns Port St. Lucie prepares for rain, flooding concerns Samples added that water levels in retention ponds and canals are at an adequate level and won't need to be lowered. Staff have also been testing their new pilot water sensors, which will send alerts to select staff if water levels rise. 'It's a way for us to respond faster to very specific locations,' Samples said. Jennifer Collins, owner of Pets Play Grooming off California and Savona boulevards, said her staff is preparing too. 'We're nervous about this storm coming up this week,' Collins said. 'Every time it rains, we get scared.' Collins is no stranger to flooding on California and Savona boulevards. She said flooding has occurred there for years. WPTV was there when water levels rose at the intersection last week. Collins said she already sent messages to her customers for Saturday. 'We may have to reschedule their dogs. We may have to push them off to next week,' Collins said. 'Saturdays are one of our busiest days, so it does really affect us as a small business.' For long-term solutions at the intersection, the city is working on a large-scale drainage project for the Oak Hammock neighborhood, which includes raising portions of the roadway. 'When this project is completed, those problems won't be problems anymore,' Samples said. The drainage project is still in data collection before moving on to design. 'We can't work if it's raining, and that's in Florida,' Collins said. 'That's just not OK.' The project may take years until completion, but Collins said she already thought about moving her business. 'We've also talked about possibly moving, and you know that would be hard too,' Collins said. 'I just feel like it's not, not getting better.'

entry.title: President Trump returns to Palm Beach as midterm elections approach
entry.summary: President Donald Trump returned to Palm Beach on Friday for his first trip of the season to Mar-a-Lago, bringing the heightened security and traffic impacts that accompany presidential visits as the country moves closer to the 2026 midterm elections. WATCH BELOW: President Trump returns to Mar-a-Lago as election nears President Trump returns to Palm Beach as midterm elections approach Trump arrived in South Florida after campaigning Friday in Dalton, Georgia, where he rallied alongside Republican candidates as the party works to turn out voters ahead of Election Day. WPTV saw supporters lining the route toward Trump's Mar-a-Lago estate as his motorcade traveled through Palm Beach. Among them was the Campbell family, who had traveled from South Carolina for a baseball tournament. 'I wasn't expecting this on my bingo card. I thought we were playing baseball,' one member of the Campbell family told WPTV. 'But I'm glad we get to see this.' Trump pushes Republican voters to turn out Trump's arrival came directly after his campaign stop at Dalton Municipal Airport in Georgia, where he appeared with Republican U.S. Senate candidate Mike Collins and gubernatorial candidate Rick Jackson. The Georgia Senate race has become a significant midterm battleground. Recent polling has shown Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff leading Collins. Trump stressed the importance of turnout during his remarks. 'When I'm not on the ballot, I guess it's a compliment, but people don't show up so much,' Trump said. 'So this is, really, I think the most important midterm election I think we've ever had.' The president also told supporters in Dalton that they should 'pretend I'm on the ballot' as he sought to boost Republican enthusiasm. Security increases around Palm Beach Back in Palm Beach, security was heightened around the island ahead of Trump's arrival. Palm Beach County Sheriff Ric Bradshaw recently told WPTV's Michael Hoffman that the county received an exemption allowing license plate reader cameras to remain on state roads as an additional layer of presidential protection. 'We filed a brief with the Department of Highway Safety up there in Tallahassee that, along with the Secret Service, and says, 'Hey, this is why we can't take them down,' and they granted us that exemption,' Bradshaw said. More presidential travel could mean traffic impacts Trump was expected to travel to Kentucky on Saturday before returning to Palm Beach later in the day, according to information provided to WPTV.

entry.title: Man dies by suicide after barricaded-subject SWAT situation in Fort Pierce - WPEC
entry.summary: Man dies by suicide after barricaded-subject SWAT situation in Fort Pierce    WPEC
entry.article_text: A man was found dead from an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound after deputies responded to a reported domestic violence incident Saturday morning in Fort Pierce's Lakewood Park neighborhood. Deputies responded around 10:17 a.m. to a home in the 7600 block of Winter Garden Boulevard, where they encountered a man in the front yard. The man went back inside after seeing law enforcement, according to the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office . Deputies say they later contacted a man and woman at the front door. A deputy saw what appeared to be a firearm in the man's possession and ordered him to drop the weapon, but he shut the door and retreated inside, prompting a barricaded-subject situation with other occupants still in the home. See also: Driver tried to ram deputy before PIT maneuver ended chase, SLCSO says During the incident, the man reportedly came outside several times and indicated he would surrender after making a phone call, but repeatedly went back inside, deputies said. During his final retreat into the home, deputies say they heard what appeared to be a gunshot. Concerned for an adult woman and children who remained inside, deputies entered the home without alerting the occupants and evacuated them through a side window, according to the sheriff's office. Deputies later found the man dead from what appeared to be a self-inflicted gunshot wound. The sheriff's office said there is no ongoing threat to the community. Detectives with the agency's Criminal Investigations Division, crime scene technicians and investigators from the Medical Examiner's Office remained at the scene to investigate the circumstances surrounding the incident. entry.title: Rescued Hobe Sound kittens recover with foster family after being buried alive
entry.summary: Two kittens rescued after being buried alive in Hobe Sound are recovering in foster care and showing signs of remarkable progress just days after investigators say they survived a tragic act of animal cruelty. Kali and Amara, two approximately 4-week-old kittens, are now living with a Treasure Coast family after Martin County Sheriff's Office deputies rescued them from the ground last week. Authorities say 36-year-old Alba Chavez buried multiple kittens alive because she believed they were demons. The case has drawn widespread attention across the Treasure Coast, where animal advocates and residents have followed the kittens' recovery. As the community processes the disturbing allegations, Kali and Amara's survival has become a symbol of resilience and hope. Rescued Hobe Sound kittens recover with foster family after being buried alive Deputies rescued two kittens buried alive Body camera video released by the Martin County Sheriff's Office shows deputies digging to reach the kittens after receiving reports about the incident. Video captured one deputy expressing surprise that the animals were still alive as rescue efforts unfolded. WATCH: Hobe Sound woman allegedly buried kittens alive Hobe Sound woman buries kittens alive, believes they were demons According to investigators, two kittens were rescued alive. Two others were found dead, and another kitten remains missing. The incident led to criminal charges against Chavez, who the sheriff's office says is currently being held on an Immigration and Customs Enforcement hold. Foster family stepped in immediately When the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast needed help caring for the surviving kittens, local nurse Jennifer Jagdeo and her family volunteered to take them in. 'As an animal lover, I think we're all shocked by it,' Jagdeo said. Her family has experience fostering animals, and she said the decision to help was immediate. 'For me, my focus has been them and healing them,' Jagdeo said. Kali and Amara making steady progress Just days after their rescue, the kittens are becoming increasingly active. Jagdeo said the pair were initially lethargic but have steadily gained strength while receiving around-the-clock care. 'They're walking around now, they wrestle with each other and play,' she said. 'They drink the bottle like it's nobody's business. They're just little joys.' Her son, Ryland Vick, said he was saddened by what happened to the kittens. As the community processes the disturbing allegations, Kali and Amara's survival has become a symbol of resilience and hope.Deputies rescued two kittens buried aliveBody camera video released by the Martin County Sheriff's Office shows deputies digging to reach the kittens after receiving reports about the incident.Video captured one deputy expressing surprise that the animals were still alive as rescue efforts unfolded.WATCH: Hobe Sound woman allegedly buried kittens aliveAccording to investigators, two kittens were rescued alive. Two others were found dead, and another kitten remains missing.The incident led to criminal charges against Chavez, who the sheriff's office says is currently being held on an Immigration and Customs Enforcement hold.Foster family stepped in immediatelyWhen the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast needed help caring for the surviving kittens, local nurse Jennifer Jagdeo and her family volunteered to take them in."As an animal lover, I think we're all shocked by it," Jagdeo said.Her family has experience fostering animals, and she said the decision to help was immediate."For me, my focus has been them and healing them," Jagdeo said.Kali and Amara making steady progressJust days after their rescue, the kittens are becoming increasingly active.Jagdeo said the pair were initially lethargic but have steadily gained strength while receiving around-the-clock care."They're walking around now, they wrestle with each other and play," she said. "They drink the bottle like it's nobody's business. They're just little joys."Her son, Ryland Vick, said he was saddened by what happened to the kittens."Why would they do this when they're just so cute?" he said.Humane Society continues responding to major rescue casesThe Humane Society of the Treasure Coast says the organization continues to respond to difficult animal welfare cases across the region, including large-scale rescue and hoarding investigations."We hope that there's an end to it, and it just doesn't seem like there's an end to it," said Sarah Fisher, spokesperson with the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast. But we're always here for the animals. We're always ready."Animal welfare advocates say cases like this highlight the importance of community support, foster homes and animal rescue resources throughout the Treasure Coast.Adoption expected in the coming weeksThe Humane Society of the Treasure Coast expects Kali and Amara to be ready for adoption in approximately four to six weeks.Their foster family hopes the sisters will eventually find permanent homes with people who can provide the love and care they deserve."My hope is that they find somebody that needs them as much as they need their human," Jagdeo said.How the community can helpAs Kali and Amara continue their recovery, the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast says community support remains critical to helping animals in need.The organization is looking for additional foster families willing to temporarily care for animals while they await permanent homes. Fostering provides a safe environment for pets recovering from illness, injury or neglect and helps free up shelter space for future rescues.The Humane Society is also accepting donations to its Emergency Medical Fund, which helps cover lifesaving veterinary care for animals rescued from cruelty, neglect and other emergency situations.Community members can also volunteer their time to assist with animal care, events, adoptions and other shelter operations.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. entry.title: Jupiter apartment residents raise drainage concerns after heavy rain floods parking areas
entry.summary: Residents at Marino Apartments in Jupiter are raising concerns about drainage after they say heavy rain repeatedly leaves portions of the property covered in standing water, at times forcing families to walk through the water simply to reach their vehicles. Resident James Ortman told WPTV the problem has become part of his family's routine when rain hits. He said the water has risen as high as 10 to 12 inches around the front tires of his truck at its worst. WATCH: Jupiter residents seek answers over apartment flooding Jupiter Residents Seek Answers Over Apartment Flooding | WPTV 'My 9-year-old and 5-year-old should not have to describe to me whether it's a puddle, pond, or lake outside the truck,' Ortman said. WPTV's Samantha Gutierrez has repeatedly reached out to management at Marino Apartments seeking an explanation for the drainage problems and information about what, if anything, will be done to address them. Management had not provided a comment at the time of this report. Family changes routine when water collects For Ortman, the drainage concerns are more than an inconvenience. He said the standing water can affect something as routine as getting his children into the family vehicle. 'If they do, then we may have to go more Crocs, getting them into the truck, and I'll bring their school shoes, their school socks or shoes down,' Ortman said. 'Same thing for me.' Ortman said he does not want his children walking through significant amounts of standing water to reach the vehicle. 'Would you feel comfortable walking your kids through, I don't know, 1,500 square feet of eight inches of water?' he asked. Resident wants lasting solution Ortman said he wants apartment management to understand what residents are experiencing firsthand and address why water continues to collect when heavy rain falls. 'Live through it. Live through it for a few days, and then tell me,' Ortman said. WPTV has not independently verified Ortman's estimates of the water's depth or the size of the affected area. The descriptions of those conditions are based on his account. WPTV also has not received information from Marino Apartments management explaining the cause of the reported drainage problems or whether repairs or other corrective measures are planned. For residents like Ortman, the concern now is what will happen the next time heavy rain arrives and whether conditions will change before then. entry.title: Protesters gather across Palm Beaches and Treasure Coast ahead of midterms - WPBF
entry.summary: Protesters gather across Palm Beaches and Treasure Coast ahead of midterms    WPBF
entry.article_text: Hundreds of residents across the Palm Beaches and Treasure Coast gathered this weekend for "No Kings" protests, urging civic engagement and opposing President Donald Trump’s policies ahead of the midterm elections. Anita Smith, a protester, said, "I am really fed up with the way the institution our government is running." Roger Lyle, another protester, said, "I'm out here to protest the president of the United States because the man is a criminal and he needs to be accounted for." Despite the rain, the protests drew large crowds, with organizers emphasizing the importance of ensuring voters have a plan for the midterms. Just do a little research on what these people have done that want to get into the office, and what do you think they're going to do for you?" Lyle said. Smith added, "Nationwide, it's important because our democracy is turning into fascism and authoritarianism, and we have to correct that." The "No Kings" movement opposes the policies and actions of Trump. On Saturday, protests were planned from the Treasure Coast to southern Palm Beach County. Smith drove from Okeechobee to Port St. Lucie to protest against the current administration and Amendment 3 on property taxes. "Somebody in the fine print is going to get rich off this proposition and nobody is reading the whole thing because it's in legalese and I'm afraid people are going to just vote for it and they don't really know what they're voting for. They think they're going to get money back," Smith said. There were no counterprotesters at the rally. Early voting in the area begins Monday.

entry.title: How to find your polling place in Palm Beach County and the Treasure Coast
entry.summary: Before heading to the polls for Florida's 2026 general election, voters should confirm where they are assigned to vote. Polling places can change between election cycles, and election officials recommend checking your polling location well before Election Day. Voters in Palm Beach County, St. Lucie County, Martin County, Indian River County and Okeechobee County can visit their local supervisor of elections website to verify registration information, view their sample ballot and locate their assigned polling place. How do I find my polling place? Most county election offices offer online voter lookup tools that allow voters to: Verify voter registration status View a sample ballot Find their precinct Locate their Election Day polling site Confirm district assignments Can I vote at any polling place? On Election Day, voters must generally cast a ballot at their assigned polling location. During early voting, voters may use any authorized early voting location within their county. What should I bring? Voters should bring a valid photo ID with a signature. Those who arrive without acceptable identification may be eligible to cast a provisional ballot.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie tests new water sensors as weekend rain threatens flood-prone areas - WFLX
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie tests new water sensors as weekend rain threatens flood-prone areas    WFLX
entry.article_text: More rain is expected this weekend across South Florida and the Treasure Coast, and WPTV is learning that Port St. Lucie Public Works is preparing. Scott Samples, communications manager with the City of Port St. Lucie, said crews spent the week clearing debris from drains and grates. Lucie prepares for rain, flooding concerns Samples added that water levels in retention ponds and canals are at an adequate level and won't need to be lowered. Staff have also been testing their new pilot water sensors, which will send alerts to select staff if water levels rise. "It's a way for us to respond faster to very specific locations," Samples said. Jennifer Collins, owner of Pets Play Grooming off California and Savona boulevards, said her staff is preparing too. "We're nervous about this storm coming up this week," Collins said. "Every time it rains, we get scared." Collins is no stranger to flooding on California and Savona boulevards. She said flooding has occurred there for years. WPTV was there when water levels rose at the intersection last week. Collins said she already sent messages to her customers for Saturday. "We may have to reschedule their dogs. We may have to push them off to next week," Collins said. "Saturdays are one of our busiest days, so it does really affect us as a small business." For long-term solutions at the intersection, the city is working on a large-scale drainage project for the Oak Hammock neighborhood, which includes raising portions of the roadway. "When this project is completed, those problems won't be problems anymore," Samples said. The drainage project is still in data collection before moving on to design. "We can't work if it's raining, and that's in Florida," Collins said. "That's just not OK." The project may take years until completion, but Collins said she already thought about moving her business. "We've also talked about possibly moving, and you know that would be hard too," Collins said. "I just feel like it's not, not getting better."

entry.title: No Kings protests bring demonstrators to streets across Palm Beach County, Treasure Coast - WPEC
entry.summary: No Kings protests bring demonstrators to streets across Palm Beach County, Treasure Coast    WPEC
entry.article_text: Signs reading Dump Trump and Trump for Prison rose above a crowd along Palm Beach Lakes Boulevard on Saturday as music played and demonstrators gathered to voice their opposition. Some wore Resist shirts and shirts featuring comedian Stephen Colbert. In a video posted by Palm Beach Indivisibles, a demonstrator sang songs touching on political and social issues into a microphone, drawing a chorus of Free speech chants when a West Palm Beach police officer attempted to stop her. The chanting continued until the officer left. The gathering near Target was one of several No Kings events scheduled across Palm Beach County and the Treasure Coast, as Trump returned to Palm Beach for his first visit of the season. For those who came out, the reasons varied, but several protesters interviewed by Palm Beach Indivisibles described a desire for change. See also: President Trump departs Palm Beach for Kentucky rally after Mar-a-Lago RNC fundraiser We don't have enough time to list all the reasons, but mainly we just need to take our country back and make sure that we have love and kindness and compassion in our hearts again, one demonstrator said. Another said they were there to oust Trump. A different attendee joked that former President Barack Obama had called and asked him to show up. Saturday’s demonstrations were part of a nationwide No Kings: Vote Early day of action. Organizers said more than 3,000 events were planned across the country, with a focus on encouraging voter participation ahead of the Nov. The effort marks an added focus for the coalition, which has organized demonstrations against what it describes as an expansion of presidential power. This time, organizers are also encouraging people to check their voter registration, learn about their voting options and make a plan to cast a ballot. They describe the voter outreach as nonpartisan. Where No Kings events were scheduled locally Palm Beach County Palm Beach Gardens: 10 a.m. to noon at PGA Boulevard and Campus Drive. on Palm Beach Lakes Boulevard, east of I-95, between Executive Center Drive and Congress Avenue. Wellington: 12:30 to 1:30 p.m. on the public sidewalk in front of the Veterans Memorial. Boynton Beach: 1 to 3 p.m. at Boynton Beach Boulevard and North Congress Avenue. to noon at Boca Raton City Hall. Treasure Coast Sebastian: 10 to 11 a.m. The address was private, with details available through registration. 1 and Kanner Highway/Colorado Avenue. at the MidFlorida Event Center. Protests coincide with Trump's Palm Beach visit President Trump arrived at Donald J. Trump International Airport shortly after 8 p.m. Friday after a rally in Dalton, Georgia. He left Saturday morning for a rally in Kentucky. His visit brought additional security measures and traffic impacts to Palm Beach. South Ocean Boulevard was closed between South County Road and Southern Boulevard, according to the Town of Palm Beach, which advised drivers heading to the island to use the middle or north bridge. The demonstrations came just days before Palm Beach County’s early voting period begins Oct. Voting is scheduled to continue through Nov. 1, ahead of Election Day on Nov.

entry.summary: A bomb threat near Donald J. Trump International Airport prompted a significant law enforcement response Sunday afternoon as President Donald Trump returned to Palm Beach, according to the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office. Authorities said no explosives or suspicious items were found, and airport officials confirmed operations have since returned to normal. The incident unfolded during a busy weekend of presidential travel and heightened security across Palm Beach County. Motorcades, road closures and an increased law enforcement presence were visible throughout the area as Trump traveled to Mar-a-Lago ahead of the midterm elections. Following an investigation, officials determined there was no active threat. Airport officials said normal operations resumed after the response concluded. The incident comes months after Palm Beach International Airport was renamed Donald J. Trump International Airport. entry.title: Man dies by suicide after barricaded-subject SWAT situation in Fort Pierce - WPEC
entry.summary: Man dies by suicide after barricaded-subject SWAT situation in Fort Pierce    WPEC
entry.article_text: A man was found dead from an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound after deputies responded to a reported domestic violence incident Saturday morning in Fort Pierce's Lakewood Park neighborhood. Deputies responded around 10:17 a.m. to a home in the 7600 block of Winter Garden Boulevard, where they encountered a man in the front yard. The man went back inside after seeing law enforcement, according to the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office . Deputies say they later contacted a man and woman at the front door. A deputy saw what appeared to be a firearm in the man's possession and ordered him to drop the weapon, but he shut the door and retreated inside, prompting a barricaded-subject situation with other occupants still in the home. See also: Driver tried to ram deputy before PIT maneuver ended chase, SLCSO says During the incident, the man reportedly came outside several times and indicated he would surrender after making a phone call, but repeatedly went back inside, deputies said. During his final retreat into the home, deputies say they heard what appeared to be a gunshot. Concerned for an adult woman and children who remained inside, deputies entered the home without alerting the occupants and evacuated them through a side window, according to the sheriff's office. Deputies later found the man dead from what appeared to be a self-inflicted gunshot wound. The sheriff's office said there is no ongoing threat to the community. Detectives with the agency's Criminal Investigations Division, crime scene technicians and investigators from the Medical Examiner's Office remained at the scene to investigate the circumstances surrounding the incident. If you or someone you know is struggling with thoughts of suicide, help is available. Call or text 988 to reach the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline , available 24/7. You can also chat at 988lifeline.org

WPTV News got an exclusive first look at the new facility, which features fresh-cut grass, new dirt, fencing, bases, a scoreboard and shady dugouts. The new facilities kick off a new era of baseball for the Thunderwolves. The field is a significant upgrade for a team that previously had to leave campus to practice. 'We used to go drive to Dyer Park and that was where we practiced at. So it was a lot harder, but we made it work. We used to practice on the soccer field, Vasquez said. It's going to be easier to get the work in, Vasquez said. Leading the program is head coach Juan Bustabad, who brings more than 30 years of professional baseball experience to Oxbridge. entry.title: Protesters gather across Palm Beaches and Treasure Coast ahead of midterms - WPBF
entry.summary: Protesters gather across Palm Beaches and Treasure Coast ahead of midterms    WPBF
entry.article_text: Hundreds of residents across the Palm Beaches and Treasure Coast gathered this weekend for "No Kings" protests, urging civic engagement and opposing President Donald Trump’s policies ahead of the midterm elections. Anita Smith, a protester, said, "I am really fed up with the way the institution our government is running." Roger Lyle, another protester, said, "I'm out here to protest the president of the United States because the man is a criminal and he needs to be accounted for." Despite the rain, the protests drew large crowds, with organizers emphasizing the importance of ensuring voters have a plan for the midterms. Just do a little research on what these people have done that want to get into the office, and what do you think they're going to do for you?" Lyle said. Smith added, "Nationwide, it's important because our democracy is turning into fascism and authoritarianism, and we have to correct that." The "No Kings" movement opposes the policies and actions of Trump. On Saturday, protests were planned from the Treasure Coast to southern Palm Beach County. Smith drove from Okeechobee to Port St. Lucie to protest against the current administration and Amendment 3 on property taxes. "Somebody in the fine print is going to get rich off this proposition and nobody is reading the whole thing because it's in legalese and I'm afraid people are going to just vote for it and they don't really know what they're voting for. entry.summary: Before heading to the polls for Florida's 2026 general election, voters should confirm where they are assigned to vote. Polling places can change between election cycles, and election officials recommend checking your polling location well before Election Day. Voters in Palm Beach County, St. Lucie County, Martin County, Indian River County and Okeechobee County can visit their local supervisor of elections website to verify registration information, view their sample ballot and locate their assigned polling place. How do I find my polling place? Most county election offices offer online voter lookup tools that allow voters to: Verify voter registration status View a sample ballot Find their precinct Locate their Election Day polling site Confirm district assignments Can I vote at any polling place? On Election Day, voters must generally cast a ballot at their assigned polling location. During early voting, voters may use any authorized early voting location within their county. What should I bring? Voters should bring a valid photo ID with a signature. Those who arrive without acceptable identification may be eligible to cast a provisional ballot.

entry.summary: No Kings protests bring demonstrators to streets across Palm Beach County, Treasure Coast    WPEC
entry.article_text: Signs reading Dump Trump and Trump for Prison rose above a crowd along Palm Beach Lakes Boulevard on Saturday as music played and demonstrators gathered to voice their opposition. Some wore Resist shirts and shirts featuring comedian Stephen Colbert. In a video posted by Palm Beach Indivisibles, a demonstrator sang songs touching on political and social issues into a microphone, drawing a chorus of Free speech chants when a West Palm Beach police officer attempted to stop her. The chanting continued until the officer left. The gathering near Target was one of several No Kings events scheduled across Palm Beach County and the Treasure Coast, as Trump returned to Palm Beach for his first visit of the season. For those who came out, the reasons varied, but several protesters interviewed by Palm Beach Indivisibles described a desire for change. See also: President Trump departs Palm Beach for Kentucky rally after Mar-a-Lago RNC fundraiser We don't have enough time to list all the reasons, but mainly we just need to take our country back and make sure that we have love and kindness and compassion in our hearts again, one demonstrator said. Another said they were there to oust Trump. A different attendee joked that former President Barack Obama had called and asked him to show up. Saturday’s demonstrations were part of a nationwide No Kings: Vote Early day of action. Organizers said more than 3,000 events were planned across the country, with a focus on encouraging voter participation ahead of the Nov. The effort marks an added focus for the coalition, which has organized demonstrations against what it describes as an expansion of presidential power. This time, organizers are also encouraging people to check their voter registration, learn about their voting options and make a plan to cast a ballot. They describe the voter outreach as nonpartisan. Where No Kings events were scheduled locally Palm Beach County Palm Beach Gardens: 10 a.m. to noon at PGA Boulevard and Campus Drive. on Palm Beach Lakes Boulevard, east of I-95, between Executive Center Drive and Congress Avenue. Wellington: 12:30 to 1:30 p.m. on the public sidewalk in front of the Veterans Memorial. Boynton Beach: 1 to 3 p.m. at Boynton Beach Boulevard and North Congress Avenue. to noon at Boca Raton City Hall. Treasure Coast Sebastian: 10 to 11 a.m. The address was private, with details available through registration. 1 and Kanner Highway/Colorado Avenue. at the MidFlorida Event Center. Protests coincide with Trump's Palm Beach visit President Trump arrived at Donald J. Trump International Airport shortly after 8 p.m. Friday after a rally in Dalton, Georgia. He left Saturday morning for a rally in Kentucky. His visit brought additional security measures and traffic impacts to Palm Beach. South Ocean Boulevard was closed between South County Road and Southern Boulevard, according to the Town of Palm Beach, which advised drivers heading to the island to use the middle or north bridge. The demonstrations came just days before Palm Beach County’s early voting period begins Oct. Voting is scheduled to continue through Nov. 1, ahead of Election Day on Nov.

entry.article_text: Early voting begins Monday across Palm Beach County and parts of the Treasure Coast, giving voters an opportunity to cast their ballots ahead of the Nov. The start of early voting comes after a weekend of No Kings protests across South Florida, where organizers encouraged voter participation and urged residents to make a plan to vote early. The demonstrations, held Saturday in communities including West Palm Beach and Palm Beach Gardens, were part of a nationwide movement protesting President Donald Trump and his administration. This weekend’s events placed an additional focus on voter turnout ahead of the 2026 general elections. When and where can you vote early? Early voting schedules vary by county, with some polling locations opening Monday and others later in the week. There are 28 early voting locations. An additional day of early voting is available Nov. to 4 p.m., with extended hours until 6 p.m. Eligible voters can cast their ballots at any designated early voting location within the county where they are registered. Voters should bring a valid photo ID with a signature. Those without acceptable identification may still cast a provisional ballot. In Palm Beach County, voters can check polling location wait times online and use an optional appointment program to schedule their check-in time. Important election deadlines: The deadline to register to vote in the general election was Oct. Voters planning to cast a ballot by mail have until Thursday, Oct. to request that a ballot be mailed to them. Completed vote-by-mail ballots must be received by election officials no later than 7 p.m. In Palm Beach County, ballots returned to a branch office or secure ballot intake station must arrive by 5 p.m. Election Day polling locations will be open from 7 a.m. Find your early voting location: Voters can find polling locations, county-specific hours and additional election information through their local supervisor of elections: Palm Beach County : VotePalmBeach.gov St. Lucie County: StLucieVotes.gov Martin County: MartinVotes.gov Indian River County: VoteIndianRiver.gov Okeechobee County: VoteOkeechobee.gov

entry.title: Strong winds, dangerous surf hit Treasure Coast, Palm Beaches - WPBF
entry.summary: Strong winds, dangerous surf hit Treasure Coast, Palm Beaches    WPBF
entry.article_text: Impact weather is creating hazardous conditions across the Treasure Coast and Palm Beaches on Sunday. A wind advisory is in effect for parts of Indian River County, with sustained winds of 20 to 25 miles per hour and gusts up to 40 miles per hour. Wind gusts around 30 miles per hour have already been recorded this Sunday morning from Sebastian and Vero Beach south through Jupiter, West Palm Beach, Boynton Beach and Boca Raton. Meanwhile, a high surf advisory remains in effect along the Atlantic coast, where seas are expected to reach seven to 12 feet. The rough surf is creating dangerous swimming conditions, a high risk of rip currents and the potential for beach erosion. Forecasters are also monitoring an area in the Atlantic with a 30% chance of tropical development over the next seven days, though no immediate impacts to Florida are expected. Residents are urged to secure loose outdoor items, use caution on the roads and stay out of rough ocean waters.

entry.title: Do seatbelts put students at risk in a school bus rollover? An NTSB expert weighs in
entry.summary: A deadly school bus crash in Polk County is raising new questions about how students are protected when a bus rolls over, including whether wearing a seat belt could create an additional danger. WATCH: AN NTSB EXPERT WEIGHS IN ON SCHOOL BUS SEAT BELTS NTSB on school buses seat belt safety Two weeks after the crash, investigative reporter Katie LaGrone put that question directly to Dr. Kristin Poland, a school bus safety expert with the National Transportation Safety Board . The crash killed 16-year-old Adinaluz Prieto Oyola during the morning commute on Oct. 5. According to investigators, the school bus carrying 37 high school students was on its way to Winter Haven High School when another cut slammed into its rear, causing the bus to collide head-on with another vehicle and flip over. Following the crash, Polk County Sheriff Grady Judd was asked whether any of the dozens of students aboard were wearing seat belts at the time of impact. 'Quite frankly, if you try to make everyone put a seat belt on, then we would have had 37 kids hanging from the roof by a seat belt,' Judd said. His comments raise a key safety question: In a rollover crash, do seat belts protect students or potentially put them at greater risk? While Poland said the NTSB cannot yet discuss specifics of its investigation into the Polk County crash, she pointed to what the agency has learned from other school bus crashes. 'The real risk is when theyre violently thrown during the crash sequence about the inside of the bus, where they hit other occupants, or they could potentially hit hard points inside the school bus,' Poland said. According to Poland, properly worn three-point restraints, which include both a lap and shoulder belt, provide the best protection even when a bus overturns. 'Those seat belts are designed so that students can still release the belts even if they're under tension, like if a student is hanging from the belt,' she said. Poland acknowledged that the image of a child hanging by a seat belt after a rollover may sound frightening. But she said the greater danger comes during the crash itself, when an unrestrained student can be thrown around the bus. The NTSB has not determined whether a three-point seat belt could have changed the outcome of the Polk County crash. The school district confirmed the bus involved was only equipped with lap belts as are all the school buses in its fleet, according to a district spokesperson. "Quite frankly, if you try to make everyone put a seat belt on, then we would have had 37 kids hanging from the roof by a seat belt," Judd said.His comments raise a key safety question: In a rollover crash, do seat belts protect students or potentially put them at greater risk?While Poland said the NTSB cannot yet discuss specifics of its investigation into the Polk County crash, she pointed to what the agency has learned from other school bus crashes."The real risk is when they’re violently thrown during the crash sequence about the inside of the bus, where they hit other occupants, or they could potentially hit hard points inside the school bus," Poland said.According to Poland, properly worn three-point restraints, which include both a lap and shoulder belt, provide the best protection even when a bus overturns."Those seat belts are designed so that students can still release the belts even if they're under tension, like if a student is hanging from the belt," she said.Poland acknowledged that the image of a child hanging by a seat belt after a rollover may sound frightening. But she said the greater danger comes during the crash itself, when an unrestrained student can be thrown around the bus.The NTSB has not determined whether a three-point seat belt could have changed the outcome of the Polk County crash. The school district confirmed the bus involved was only equipped with lap belts as are all the school buses in its fleet, according to a district spokesperson.A safety issue investigated for yearsFor reporter LaGrone, the questions surrounding school bus restraints aren't new. More than a decade ago, she investigated a St. Lucie County school bus crash that killed 9-year-old Aaron Beauchamp, who was wearing a lap belt at the time.The NTSB investigated that crash and produced simulations demonstrating the difference between the protection provided by a lap belt and the protection provided when a shoulder belt is added.A few years later, the agency formally recommended that school districts in the U.S. upgrade school bus restraints to include both lap and shoulder belts. Florida was among the states called on to make three-point seat belts state law.What does Florida require?Currently, Florida only requires school buses to be equipped with lap belts, but students are not required to wear them.Nearly a decade after the NTSB's recommendation, Poland said some Florida school districts are moving toward three-point lap-and-shoulder belts. “We're seeing some progress with some of the school districts in Florida moving to the passenger lap shoulder belts,” she said.But our investigation found that the majority of public school buses in the state still have lap belts only.Cost is one hurdle. Still, Poland said installing the equipment is only part of improving student safety. "It's not enough just to have the lap shoulder belts on the bus, there also has to be an entire layered approach to ensure that the students are wearing the belts properly," she said. That approach also requires involvement and oversight from school districts and parents, Poland said.But Poland wants to emphasize that school buses remain the safest mode of transportation for students traveling to and from school, regardless of what kind of seat belts are on board. For Poland, seat belt use on school buses is a major step toward the agency's ultimate goal. "We think we can get to zero fatalities in school buses and that's what we're looking towards," Poland said.

entry.title: Ballet Palm Beach brings Mary Shelley's 'Frankenstein' to the Kravis Center in West Palm Beach
entry.summary: Ballet Palm Beach is bringing one of literature's most iconic stories to the stage this month with its original production of Mary Shelley's Frankenstein at the Kravis Center in West Palm Beach. The production runs Oct. 22 through Oct. 24 at the Marshall E. Rinker Sr. Playhouse and reimagines Mary Shelley's classic novel through contemporary ballet. Ballet Palm Beach describes the performance as a dramatic exploration of ambition, abandonment and identity. The company is the professional ballet company of Palm Beach County and the Treasure Coast. WATCH BELOW: Ballet Palm Beach brings 'Frankenstein' to the Kravis Center Inside Ballet Palm Beach's world-premiere Frankenstein According to Founding Artistic and Executive Director Colleen Smith, the story begins before Frankenstein's monster ever comes to life. 'It's a gorgeous production about Mary Shelley and her haunting book Frankenstein,' Smith said. During the broadcast, Smith explained how the famous story was born during a gathering at Lake Geneva. 'They were gathered together on the shores of Lake Geneva on a stormy night, and Lord Byron was reading ghost stories and said, 'You know what, guys, let's create our own ghost stories,' and she did,' Smith said. 'First science fiction novel ever written by an 18-year-old woman.' Dancer Leah Walker said audiences can expect something different from a traditional ballet. 'Most classical ballets are fantasy, but ours does follow the real story of Mary Shelley and her process as she writes it,' Leah said. 'It's a horror. It's a very contemporary, very artistic take.' The production is recommended for ages 9 and older and features two 45-minute acts separated by a 20-minute intermission. For audiences looking for a Halloween-season experience with a local arts connection, the performance offers a fresh take on a familiar tale. The production combines historical elements from Mary Shelley's life with the themes that have made Frankenstein one of the most enduring stories ever written. Tickets and performance information are available through Ballet Palm Beach and the Kravis Center. entry.title: Bomb threat prompts heavy law enforcement response near Trump airport in Palm Beach County
entry.summary: A bomb threat near Donald J. Trump International Airport prompted a significant law enforcement response Sunday afternoon as President Donald Trump returned to Palm Beach , according to the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office. Authorities said no explosives or suspicious items were found, and airport officials confirmed operations have since returned to normal. WATCH BELOW: Bomb threat prompts heavy law enforcement response near Trump airport Bomb threat near Trump airport prompts major law enforcement response The incident unfolded during a busy weekend of presidential travel and heightened security across Palm Beach County. Motorcades, road closures and an increased law enforcement presence were visible throughout the area as Trump traveled to Mar-a-Lago ahead of the midterm elections. Airport operations return to normal The Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office said deputies responded after receiving information about a bomb threat near the airport. Following an investigation, officials determined there was no active threat. Airport officials said normal operations resumed after the response concluded. The incident comes months after Palm Beach International Airport was renamed Donald J. Trump International Airport. WPTV has previously reported on security concerns and threats involving the airport since the name change, although authorities have not identified any connection between Sundays threat and the airports new name. Neighbors say heavy security is expected Residents who live near the airport said large law enforcement operations and traffic disruptions have become familiar whenever the president visits Palm Beach County. Phil, who lives near the airport, told WPTV drivers often encounter road closures and extensive security measures during presidential visits. 'Any time he's coming in town, traffic is locked down,' he said. 'We've seen cops, sheriffs, Palm Beach sheriffs all around the whole airport.' Residents said major roadways, including Belvedere Road, Southern Boulevard and surrounding routes, can experience lengthy traffic delays. 'If he's coming through, they'll lock it all down and you're stuck in traffic for at least an hour,' said Phil. Businesses deal with temporary disruptions Business owners along Southern Boulevard told WPTV security operations tied to presidential travel can temporarily affect customers and employees. entry.title: Palm Beach County 'No Kings' rally urges early voting
entry.summary: Protesters gathered in Palm Beach County as part of a nationwide 'No Kings' day of action, with local organizers putting a focus on encouraging people to vote early ahead of the November midterm elections. The rally was organized locally by Speaking Up for America - Indivisible. Group leader Susan Foley said Saturday's demonstration marked the organization's eighth rally in two years and its fourth No Kings rally. 'Today is a special day, our fourth No Kings rally,' Foley said. 'This one is special because of its mission to vote early.' WATCH: Palm Beach County No Kings' rally urges early voting No Kings Rally Foley said organizers are encouraging people to cast their ballots early rather than waiting until Election Day. 'If you vote early, your vote is locked in,' Foley said. But for protesters who came out Saturday, the rally was also an opportunity to speak about issues they would like to see addressed both nationally and closer to home. WPTV's Christy Waite listened to protesters like Ann Hunter. She says she wants to see more attention paid to the financial challenges facing families. 'More consideration to the middle class and people that are in desperate circumstances struggling with their food, healthcare, everyday living expenses,' Hunter said. For Cynthia Heller, a former educator, education funding is among the issues that brought her out. 'I was in education, so I would like to see more money go into education,' Heller said. Protesters said events like Saturday's also give members of the community an opportunity to come together around issues that are important to them. One protester emphasized that regardless of political affiliation, participating in the election is what matters. 'I am happy to see people here, and no matter how they vote, they have to vote,' the protester said. The Republican Party of Palm Beach County also responded to Saturday's demonstrations, pointing to Republican policies and the party's growing voter registration advantage in Florida. entry.title: Man found dead after barricade situation in St. Lucie County, deputies say
entry.summary: A man was found dead from an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound Saturday after a barricade situation prompted deputies to evacuate a woman and children from a St. Lucie County home, according to the sheriffs office. The St. Lucie County Sheriffs Office said deputies responded around 10:17 a.m. to a reported domestic violence incident in the 7600 block of Winter Garden Boulevard. WATCH BELOW: Man found dead after St. Lucie County barricade situation Man found dead after barricade situation in St. Lucie County Deputies initially encountered a man in the front yard who went back inside after seeing law enforcement. Authorities later made contact with a man and woman at the front door. During that interaction, a deputy saw what appeared to be a firearm in the man's possession and ordered him to drop it, the sheriffs office said. Instead, the man closed the door and retreated inside, creating a barricaded-subject situation while other people remained in the home. According to investigators, the man came outside several times and said he would surrender after making a phone call, but repeatedly went back inside. During his final retreat into the home, deputies heard what appeared to be a gunshot. Knowing a woman and children were still inside and could be in danger, deputies entered the residence and evacuated them through a side window, the sheriffs office said. Deputies later found the man dead from what appeared to be a self-inflicted gunshot wound. Authorities said there is no ongoing threat to the community. Detectives, crime scene technicians and investigators from the Medical Examiners Office are expected to remain at the scene for several hours as the investigation continues.

entry.title: Florida Panthers host fifth annual 'Pink in the Rink' night to honor breast and cervical cancer survivors
entry.summary: The Florida Panthers' fifth annual 'Pink in the Rink' Night returned to Amerant Bank Arena on Saturday during a home game against the Seattle Kraken, honoring those who have battled breast and cervical cancer and the medical professionals working to treat the diseases and find a cure. entry.summary: Baseball Hall of Famer Andre Dawson received the Governors Medal of Freedom. Governor Ron DeSantis said the award recognizes Dawsons baseball career, his contributions to Florida AM University, and his lasting impact on the state of Florida. Dawson was born in Miami and went to Southwest Miami Senior High School. He then went to Florida AM and walked on to the Rattlers baseball team. His performance led the Montreal Expos to select him in the 1975 MLB draft. His distinguished career in Major League Baseball, his contributions to the sport, and his lasting impact on our state have earned him this award. The Hawk has represented Florida in the best possible way for decades. His generous support of FAMU and its baseball program has helped generations of student-athletes succeed. The Governors Medal of Freedom is the highest honor I can bestow on any Floridian, and Andre Dawson truly deserves this recognition, DeSantis said. Past recipients of the Governors Medal of Freedom include Florida State University football coach Bobby Bowden, golfer Barbara Nicklaus, musician Jimmy Buffett, Coach Lee Corso, and former Florida Supreme Court Justice Charles Canady. entry.title: Florida secures arrest warrant for Raúl Castro in 1996 Brothers to the Rescue shootdown
entry.summary: Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier announced Monday that state prosecutors and the Florida Department of Law Enforcement (FDLE) have secured an arrest warrant for former Cuban leader Ral Castro, accusing him of conspiring to murder four men in the 1996 shootdown of two civilian aircraft operated by the anti-Castro group Brothers to the Rescue. According to the Attorney General's Office, Castro has been charged with one count of conspiracy to commit first-degree murder in connection with an incident in which Cuban military fighter jets shot down two unarmed Brothers to the Rescue planes over international waters. Authorities said three unarmed Cessna aircraft departed Opa-locka Airport in Miami-Dade County on Feb. 24, 1996. After crossing the 24th parallel and flying outside Cuba's territorial waters, two of the planes were destroyed by air-to-air missiles fired by Cuban MiG fighter jets. According to the affidavit, the aircraft were traveling away from Cuba at the time and received no warning before being shot down. The warrant, obtained by the Office of Statewide Prosecution and FDLE, alleges Castro played a key role in authorizing the attack that killed four men with ties to Florida: Carlos Costa, Pablo Morales, Mario de la Pea and Armando Alejandre Jr. 'Ral Castro ordered the murder of four Floridians in cold blood, and Florida will never stop pursuing accountability for that communist conspiracy,' Uthmeier said in a statement. According to a probable cause affidavit, Castro, who at the time served as Cuba's minister of the Revolutionary Armed Forces and first vice president, was among the final decision-makers who authorized the operation. Investigators allege Castro issued standing orders to military leaders to shoot down aircraft associated with Brothers to the Rescue if they appeared over the sea. State investigators also allege Cuban intelligence agents operating in South Florida infiltrated Brothers to the Rescue and provided flight information to the Cuban government as part of what was known as 'Operation Scorpion.' Miami-Dade Sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz called the warrant a 'historic step toward accountability' for the four men killed in the attack, while FDLE Special Agent in Charge Michael Stein said the case demonstrates that 'the passage of time does not diminish the pursuit of justice.' The warrant charges Castro under Florida statutes governing conspiracy and first-degree murder. Prosecutors said the offense is a first-degree felony,
