entry.summary: Vero Beach man, 60, dies in crash involving tractor-trailer in Indian River County    cw34.com
entry.article_text: A 60-year-old Vero Beach man died after the SUV he was driving collided with a semi-trailer at an intersection in Indian River County on Thursday. The crash happened as a 2026 Freightliner truck-tractor pulling a flatbed trailer attempted to turn left from a stop sign on westbound 49th Street, according to a crash report from the Florida Highway Patrol . The Freightliner entered the path of a northbound 2006 Dodge Durango traveling on 66th Avenue, and the front of the SUV struck the left side of the trailer. The Durango driver was taken to Health First’s Holmes Regional Medical Center in Melbourne, where he was pronounced dead at 8:02 a.m. His next of kin had not been notified, according to the report. See also: West Palm Beach man faces up to life after conviction in child sex trafficking case The 59-year-old Jacksonville man driving the Freightliner did not report any injuries. The traffic homicide investigation is ongoing.

entry.title: Missing girl, 5, found dead in Fort Pierce body of water - WPBF
entry.summary: Missing girl, 5, found dead in Fort Pierce body of water    WPBF
entry.article_text: A 5-year-old nonverbal girl was located deceased in a body of water near her home in Fort Pierce three hours after she was reported missing, police said Saturday afternoon. The Fort Pierce Police Department was looking for Mayra Glory Odelus, who was last seen in the 5100 block of Portofino Landing Apartments east of Interstate 95 before noon. A diving team was utilized to search for her. "Our deepest condolences are with Mayra’s family and loved ones during this tragic time," the agency posted in an update at 4:15 p.m. Michael Santiago told WPBF's Angela Rozier they received the report of the missing girl at 11:39 a.m., with family members saying she was autistic and nonverbal. Officers searched the surrounding area and distributed flyers with the girl's name and photo. She was last seen wearing a dark oversized shirt with two white beads in her hair, the agency said. They also launched drones, and requested assistance from Port St. Lucie bloodhounds and the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office dive team. The child's body was found in the pond at about 3 p.m. Police said the child's father told them the pond is directly across from their apartment and she loved the water. The father and her 18-year-old sister were home at the time the girl went missing. The girl's mother lives in Haiti and is expected to arrive Sunday. "It's very tragic when anything like this happens, but with our kids we have to make sure we're paying attention all the time -- especially when kids are challenged with autism," Santiago said. https://www.facebook.com/FortPiercePD/posts/pfbid0ZTmVUzd2J1ZLNLpPFPiyFLf8PwQX9X66AaqDEee6Ujz4VXk1w1gs9qGwLGKEy3MCl Drowning is the leading cause of unintentional death among children 1-3. "Drowning can really happen in seconds, I mean 20 seconds, 30 seconds, and you can even start to get brain injury because of the lack of oxygen within minutes," Dr. Elizabeth Feldman, of Cleveland Clinic Florida, told Rozier. The Children's Services Council of Palm Beach said 39 children with autism or who were suspected of having autism drowned in Florida in 2025 -- the highest number ever recorded in the state. Several specialized tracking and safety devices help prevent or respond to water hazards. "One of the interesting things about this is that she actually had a tablet with her and the family was able to ping the tablet to try and locate where she was," Santiago said. "And the tablet led to where we're standing right now, but there were no signs of her, and up to this point, we still cannot locate that tablet." entry.article_text: A firefighter/paramedic died Saturday morning while on duty, one year after his brother, also with the St. Lucie County Fire District, passed away, the agency said. Austin Hodge, 34, joined the St. Lucie County Fire District on July 17, 2017. He was assigned to Station 9 in Fort Pierce. A procession of firefighters and personnel from other agencies went from HCA Lawnwood Hospital to the morgue in Fort Pierce on Saturday morning. His brother, Jarius Hodge, died on July 22, 2025, after falling ill at work at Station 3. His family said he had the flu, felt weak and was later rushed to the hospital, where he died hours later. People gathered on May 30 to celebrate what would have been his 27th birthday with a cookout and balloon release. Austin Hodge told WPBF at the time: "He was a quiet leader, and we take a lot from him. He was my younger brother, but I looked up to him in many ways to keep me poised, keep me patient. And I think that's what he's teaching everybody today." In June, another firefighter, Connor Whitehead, 21, died on May 31 but the cause of death wasn't released. Stay up to date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25 There are 20 fire stations and 523 firefighters in the county, according to the agency's website. Information regarding memorial arrangements and opportunities to honor Hodge's service iwll be shared in coordination with his family as details are finalized. "His death is a profound loss to the St. Lucie County Fire District and the fire service community," the agency said. "The District extends its heartfelt condolences to Hodge’s family, friends, and fellow firefighters during this difficult time." Several agencies offered their condolences, including Port St. Lucie Fire Rescue, Fort Pierce Police Officers Association, Port St. Lucie Police Department, Indian River County Sheriff's Office, Indian River County Emergency Services Department, Indian River County Fire Rescue, Palm Beach County Fire Rescue, Riviera Beach Fire Rescue. https://www.facebook.com/stluciesheriff/posts/pfbid0cPopWYk7mLx2z6QfJqkd99ZUoP9dWGSRx3Y7yjuN21oLAqBUmr6n8RYoUYP9RGaZl The St. Lucie agency thanked other agencieson Facebook. https://www.facebook.com/slcfd/posts/pfbid02FGoAgmLryFmnkCkLqRQfwhzpBpGAX3Bh285A6jFqKysGajonPUPDHeKjxdFm2KQvl "In the hours following this heartbreaking loss, our firefighters, Honor Guard, and public safety partners came together to honor our fallen brother and stand alongside one another during an incredibly difficult time. The brotherhood of the fire service extends far beyond the walls of a fire station. It is a bond built on trust, shared experiences, and an unwavering commitment to one another. "Today, that bond was especially evident through the incredible support of the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office, Fort Pierce Police Department, Port St. Lucie Police Department, and peer support teams from Martin and Indian River counties. "Together, they offered strength, compassion, and support while ensuring Austin was honored with the dignity and respect he deserves. Our hearts are with Austin’s family, loved ones, and everyone who had the privilege of serving alongside him. We are deeply grateful to our fellow first responders and community for the outpouring of support during this tremendous loss." Get the latest news updates with the WPBF 25 News app.

entry.title: Martin County parents win push for a school zone outside Citrus Grove Elementary - WPTV
entry.summary: Martin County parents win push for a school zone outside Citrus Grove Elementary    WPTV
entry.article_text: Martin County parents are celebrating a victory in a long battle to improve safety around their children's school.Citrus Grove Elementary School parents say the 45 mph speed limit outside the school puts their children's safety in jeopardy. They say a recently approved school zone is the first step to making Newfield Parkway a safer place for children who walk to school.On Southwest Newfield Parkway, morning and afternoon traffic is an obstacle for young students."It scares me," parent Kendall George said. "These cars are driving 45 miles an hour plus."Kendall is among the many families who live in the Canopy Creek community across the street from Citrus Grove Elementary, so their children walk to school. Kelly Ribaudo, the PTA president and Martin County PTA Advocacy Chair, told WPTV she's spent the last five years asking the county to put in a school zone."We've had so many near misses with the kids just from people not paying attention," Ribaudo said. "Everyone has a right to a free and public education and they should be safe getting there. Our main priority should be the kids not the traffic."At the previous Martin County Commission meeting, commissioners unanimously answered their call."Whatever the number is there is no price to someone getting hurt," Martin County Commissioner Edward Ciampi said. "You will absolutely get a school zone."School Principal Rose Rynca told WPTV the need is greater than ever, with enrollment growing as new communities pop up in the area."The amount of students crossing Newfield Parkway has definitely increased," Rynca said. "This speed zone is going to really really improve the safety of students.""It's letting drivers know that, hey there's a school here, there's children crossing, and we have to slow down," George said.WPTV's Cassandra Garcia followed up with the county on Thursday to find out the timeline for adding a school zone on SW Newfield Parkway. In a statement they said:In the meantime, these parents are asking drivers to be cautious."Slow down if you see a school — even if there's not a school zone sign, slow down," Ribaudo said.With a school zone on the horizon, these parents said the next step is getting better street lighting.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. Our editorial team verifies all reporting on all platforms for fairness and accuracy.

entry.article_text: A 60-year-old man was arrested in connection with a hit-and-run crash that critically injured a 63-year-old Port St. Lucie resident, police said. The crash happened shortly before 1 a.m. 9 on NW California Boulevard just south of the intersection with NW University Boulevard. The victim was found unconscious in the road with severe head injuries and remains in critical condition at HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital in Ft. Lucie Police Chief Leo Niemczyk said detectives arrested Eric Saint Aude on Oct. 22 and charged him with leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury. He said Aude was working as a newspaper delivery driver and was on his way to pick up newspapers when the crash happened. Investigators reviewed video, physical evidence and other leads since the crash two weeks ago. Niemczyk said a geofence warrant which sought cellphone location data from a specific area during a specific time produced a lead showing Aude's phone had pinged off cell phone towers in that area at the time of the crash. That helped detectives identify Aude as the alleged hit and run driver and the vehicles registered to him. Detectives then located and examined the man’s vehicle, which had damage consistent with striking a pedestrian, including damage to the front bumper and hood, Niemczyk said. Investigators also found presumptive positive results for blood on the vehicle. Further testing is needed. Police also recovered pieces of the vehicle’s inner fender-well fasteners at the scene, Niemczyk said. Detectives found that several matching fasteners were missing from the suspect’s vehicle. Investigators are still looking for a second vehicle that was traveling southbound near the crash. Niemczyk said distant video showed a vehicle traveling in each direction, but it was difficult to determine what happened. Police are trying to learn whether the second vehicle also struck the victim or if the driver of the second vehicle witnessed the accident. We’re very confident that the vehicle that we have and the person that we’ve arrested are responsible for the majority of what occurred, Niemczyk said. The Police Chief said the victim was in the middle of the road when he was struck, but investigators could not determine from the video whether he was walking or jogging. Police learned he often exercised at night when the weather was cooler and he was known to walk on the road and medians. "I've been doing this for 30 years. I'm not surprised by a whole lot anymore. I've seen pedestrians left for dead on the side of the road before. It doesn't make it any easier, but it doesn't surprise me at this point either. It's just difficult to understand how one human being could be so, you know, without compassion for another," Chief Niemczyk said. See also: 2 arrested in killing of transgender woman Jayla McGee in Belle Glade The victim had no identification or cellphone with him, Niemczyk said. Investigators used data from a Garmin exercise watch he was wearing to trace his route back to his house and were able to identify him. Niemczyk said the victim has significant head trauma and is unable to speak. He is expected to survive, but the chief said his quality of life may not be the same as it was before the crash. "An arrest cannot undo the harm or uncertainty imposed upon a victim, Niemczyk said, but it’s the first step in accountability. Police have not released a description of the southbound vehicle. Anyone with information is asked to call the Port St. Lucie Police Department at 772-871-5000. Aude is being held on $45,000 bond.

entry.title: Missing girl, 5, found dead in Fort Pierce water near home - WPBF
entry.summary: Missing girl, 5, found dead in Fort Pierce water near home    WPBF
entry.article_text: A 5-year-old nonverbal girl was located deceased in a body of water near her home in Fort Pierce three hours after she was reported missing, police said Saturday afternoon. The Fort Pierce Police Department was looking for Mayra Glory Odelus, who was last seen in the 5100 block of Portofino Landing Apartments east of Interstate 95 before noon. A diving team was utilized to search for her. "Our deepest condolences are with Mayra’s family and loved ones during this tragic time," the agency posted in an update at 4:15 p.m. Michael Santiago told WPBF's Angela Rozier they received the report of the missing girl at 11:39 a.m., with family members saying she was autistic and nonverbal. Officers searched the surrounding area and distributed flyers with the girl's name and photo. She was last seen wearing a dark oversized shirt with two white beads in her hair, the agency said. They also launched drones, and requested assistance from Port St. Lucie bloodhounds and the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office dive team. The child's body was found in the pond at about 3 p.m. about 75 yards from hert apartment. Police said the child's father told them the pond is directly across from their apartment and she loved the water. The father and her 18-year-old sister were home at the time the girl went missing. The girl's mother lives in Haiti and is expected to arrive Sunday. "It's very tragic when anything like this happens, but with our kids we have to make sure we're paying attention all the time -- especially when kids are challenged with autism," Santiago said. https://www.facebook.com/FortPiercePD/posts/pfbid0ZTmVUzd2J1ZLNLpPFPiyFLf8PwQX9X66AaqDEee6Ujz4VXk1w1gs9qGwLGKEy3MCl Drowning is the leading cause of unintentional death among children 1-3. "Drowning can really happen in seconds, I mean 20 seconds, 30 seconds, and you can even start to get brain injury because of the lack of oxygen within minutes," Dr. Elizabeth Feldman, of Cleveland Clinic Florida, told Rozier. The Children's Services Council of Palm Beach said 39 children with autism or who were suspected of having autism drowned in Florida in 2025 -- the highest number ever recorded in the state. Several specialized tracking and safety devices help prevent or respond to water hazards. "One of the interesting things about this is that she actually had a tablet with her and the family was able to ping the tablet to try and locate where she was," Santiago said. "And the tablet led to where we're standing right now, but there were no signs of her, and up to this point, we still cannot locate that tablet." The action marks an escalation in the Trump administrations efforts to scrutinize voter rolls ahead of the midterm elections as it continues to double down on claims of voter fraud, fueled by President Donald Trumps baseless allegations of widespread election cheating. entry.article_text: The Justice Department on Friday ordered California election officials to identify suspected noncitizens on voter rolls and set aside their mail-in ballots — warning that officials who knowingly count ballots cast by noncitizens could face criminal liability.The action marks an escalation in the Trump administration’s efforts to scrutinize voter rolls ahead of the midterm elections as it continues to double down on claims of voter fraud, fueled by President Donald Trump’s baseless allegations of widespread election cheating.Letters sent to California county election officials asked them to work with the Justice Department and Department of Homeland Security to “identify who on the accompanying list is a citizen and who is not.”“If persons knowingly tabulate ballots cast by individuals identified by federal agencies as noncitizens, they risk becoming aiders and abettors to a federal crime,” First Assistant US Attorney Bill Essayli said to San Bernardino County officials in a letter, which was seen by CNN.Santa Cruz County received a letter with 81 names, which it said is still under review. So far, officials have found most of the records belong to voters who are no longer actively registered in the county, County Clerk Tricia Webber told CNN on Saturday.“They are either canceled or inactive records,” Webber said. At least one name has never been registered in the county, Webber added.RELATED STORY | DOJ threatens California with legal action over claim of noncitizens on voter rollsRural Modoc County also received a list with one voter who appears to have never been registered in the county, according to an election official.Marin County, north of San Francisco, received a list of 48 “likely aliens,” according to a letter seen by CNN. Nearby Solano County said its list had 170 names.Nevada County has reviewed a list of 10 names and is “confident that state and federal laws are being followed,” according to a statement shared with CNN.Santa Clara, Napa, Butte and Amador counties confirmed they have also received a letter but Riverside County told CNN as of Saturday afternoon, it had not.“All of this is simply meant to raise huge doubts about the integrity of this election,” John Tuteur, registrar of voters for Napa County, told The Associated Press.Tuteur said two uniformed Department of Homeland Security officers delivered a letter with 42 names to his office late on Friday afternoon, according to the AP.“We’re not changing anything we’re doing. We’re proceeding with the election,” Tuteur added.The letters follow a demand earlier this month from acting Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter, who gave Los Angeles County and California Secretary of State Shirley Weber 48 hours to review a federal list of suspected noncitizens who had been sent mail-in ballots. McCotter threatened to seek “emergency relief” if officials did not comply.The earlier letter, sent October 13, included a password-protected thumb drive containing names of people the administration “believes are likely non-citizens” who had been sent ballots for the November election. It asked officials to temporarily set aside ballots from people whose citizenship could not be confirmed, rather than cancel their registrations.“Maintaining accurate voter registration records is a fundamental responsibility of our office,” Los Angeles County Clerk Dean C. Logan said in a statement, after receiving the October 13 letter.“Federal and state laws are clear on how voter eligibility is established – and any action to remove a voter from eligibility must be based on verifiable information, not assertions of unconfirmed data matching.”RELATED STORY | Records show ICE reviewed tens of millions of voter records looking for noncitizen votersLogan sent an email to the California Association of Clerks and Election Officials on Friday, saying the latest DOJ letter includes a “posture of intimidation and threats leveled against local election officials just twelve days before the election.”Logan said that the DOJ “misrepresents” the county’s response to the earlier letter as “resistance to a civil lawsuit that was not yet filed” and is now giving an “unenforceable 48-hour deadline” to provide information that it has previously “obtained through subpoenas.”The Justice Department last week sued California and Los Angeles County, seeking to prevent officials from counting more than 20,000 mail-in ballots associated with people the government believes are likely noncitizens. A federal judge scheduled a hearing on the case for next week, but the Justice Department on Friday asked the 9th US Circuit Court of Appeals to intervene before then.“Every minute of processing that occurs without segregating the ballots of suspected ineligible voters causes untraceable disenfranchisement and dilution of the votes of United States citizens,” the motion noted.Logan, in Friday’s email, said the DOJ provided in its letter a list of the 20,000 noncitizens it believes are on the county’s voter rolls. But a review of those names, he said, showed that many “were associated with addresses throughout California, not solely within Los Angeles County.”A similar legal battle is unfolding in Alaska, where the Trump administration is seeking to block certification of the state’s Senate race under certain circumstances if Republican Sen. The race is being closely watched as Democrats seek to regain control of the Senate.The administration has repeatedly alleged that hundreds of thousands of noncitizens are on voter rolls. Only US citizens are allowed to vote in federal and state elections. But some states, including California, have passed laws allowing noncitizens to cast ballots in local or school board elections.In August, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said his department had identified 250,000 people it believed were noncitizens and registered to vote in four states — California, Pennsylvania, New Jersey and Nevada — by comparing voter-registration records with federal immigration data.But the administration’s claims have faced scrutiny, and some initial findings have not held up under further review. In Nevada, for example, DHS told state officials that its initial finding of 15,900 potentially noncitizen registrants was preliminary and unvetted, and that it had confirmed only 185 through manual review.Last month, Nevada officials told DHS their subsequent review found that all 185 were US citizens, a conclusion the federal agency disputes.In response to Friday’s letters, California Sen. Alex Padilla, a ranking member of the Senate Rules and Administration Committee with oversight over federal elections, called the administration “afraid and desperate.”“Trump’s DOJ has not provided any evidence for their claims of massive voter fraud. They’ve admitted that the data they point to is inaccurate and unreliable. No matter how many lawsuits they file or how many election officials they threaten, they do not have the authority to interfere,” Padilla said.“The Trump administration is afraid and desperate. Their attempts to take over our elections will fail. Election officials: We have your back. California: Your vote is your voice. Use it and let’s hold this administration accountable.”The-CNN-Wire™ & © 2026 Cable News Network, Inc., a Warner Bros.

entry.article_text: Lucie County Fire District firefighter who died unexpectedly Saturday morning has been identified as Austin Hodge, a firefighter paramedic and nine-year veteran of the department. The fire district announced Saturday evening that Hodge, who was assigned to Firehouse 9, died while on duty earlier in the day. Lucie County Fire District family mourns the loss of one of our own," the district said in a statement. In the hours following his death, firefighters, the department's Honor Guard and fellow first responders gathered to honor Hodge and support one another. The district said the response reflected the strong bond shared throughout the fire service. The district thanked the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office, Fort Pierce Police Department, Port St. Lucie Police Department and peer support teams from Martin and Indian River counties for providing assistance and standing alongside firefighters during the difficult day. "Together, they offered strength, compassion, and support while ensuring Austin was honored with the dignity and respect he deserves," the district said. The district said its thoughts are with Hodge's family, loved ones and everyone who served alongside him. "We are deeply grateful to our fellow first responders and community for the outpouring of support during this tremendous loss," the district said. "Today and always, we stand together." WPTV has reached out to the fire district for additional information. This remains a developing story.

entry.article_text: A firefighter/paramedic died Saturday morning while on duty, one year after his brother, also with the St. Lucie County Fire District, passed away, the agency said. Austin Hodge, 34, joined the St. Lucie County Fire District on July 17, 2017. He was assigned to Station 9 in Fort Pierce. A procession of firefighters and personnel from other agencies went from HCA Lawnwood Hospital to the morgue in Fort Pierce on Saturday morning. His brother, Jarius Hodge, died on July 22, 2025, after falling ill at work at Station 3. His family said he had the flu, felt weak and was later rushed to the hospital, where he died hours later. People gathered on May 30 to celebrate what would have been his 27th birthday with a cookout and balloon release. Austin Hodge told WPBF at the time: "He was a quiet leader, and we take a lot from him. He was my younger brother, but I looked up to him in many ways to keep me poised, keep me patient. And I think that's what he's teaching everybody today." In June, another firefighter, Connor Whitehead, 21, died on May 31 but the cause of death wasn't released. Stay up to date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25 There are 20 fire stations and 523 firefighters in the county, according to the agency's website. Information regarding memorial arrangements and opportunities to honor Hodge's service iwll be shared in coordination with his family as details are finalized. "His death is a profound loss to the St. Lucie County Fire District and the fire service community," the agency said. "The District extends its heartfelt condolences to Hodge’s family, friends, and fellow firefighters during this difficult time." Several agencies offered their condolences, including Port St. Lucie Fire Rescue, Fort Pierce Police Officers Association, Port St. Lucie Police Department, Indian River County Sheriff's Office, Indian River County Emergency Services Department, Indian River County Fire Rescue, Palm Beach County Fire Rescue, Riviera Beach Fire Rescue. https://www.facebook.com/stluciesheriff/posts/pfbid0cPopWYk7mLx2z6QfJqkd99ZUoP9dWGSRx3Y7yjuN21oLAqBUmr6n8RYoUYP9RGaZl The St. Lucie agency thanked other agencieson Facebook. https://www.facebook.com/slcfd/posts/pfbid02FGoAgmLryFmnkCkLqRQfwhzpBpGAX3Bh285A6jFqKysGajonPUPDHeKjxdFm2KQvl "In the hours following this heartbreaking loss, our firefighters, Honor Guard, and public safety partners came together to honor our fallen brother and stand alongside one another during an incredibly difficult time. The brotherhood of the fire service extends far beyond the walls of a fire station. It is a bond built on trust, shared experiences, and an unwavering commitment to one another. "Today, that bond was especially evident through the incredible support of the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office, Fort Pierce Police Department, Port St. Lucie Police Department, and peer support teams from Martin and Indian River counties. "Together, they offered strength, compassion, and support while ensuring Austin was honored with the dignity and respect he deserves. Our hearts are with Austin’s family, loved ones, and everyone who had the privilege of serving alongside him. We are deeply grateful to our fellow first responders and community for the outpouring of support during this tremendous loss." Get the latest news updates with the WPBF 25 News app.

entry.title: 11-year-old, other minors among 11 shot near Florida A&M University stadium
entry.summary: A shooting near a college stadium in Tallahassee, Florida, left 11 people with gunshot wounds Saturday night, officials said. Among the victims near Florida AM University were six juveniles, including an 11-year-old, Tallahassee Police Chief Lawrence Revell told reporters at a news conference late Saturday. No deaths had been reported, police said. The shooting took place just hours after a homecoming football game at the stadium, where the ArkansasPine Bluff Golden Lions beat the Florida AM Rattlers 31-28. Its unclear whether the shooting was connected to the game. In addition to those shot, a victims grandmother was injured while fleeing the scene near Florida AMs Bragg Memorial Stadium. As of Sunday morning, five victims had been released from the hospital, while six remained hospitalized, Tallahassee police said. Of those still being treated, one was in critical condition, police said. There have been at least 383 mass shootings in the US so far this year, according to the Gun Violence Archive, which, like CNN, defines a mass shooting as one in which four or more people are shot, not including the shooter. The police chief told reporters the shooting likely stemmed from an altercation between two to three individuals and that the departments Violent Crimes Unit would lead the ongoing investigation. Tallahassee police detectives have reviewed digital evidence and canvassed the area, police said in a statement Sunday. We need our communitys help. No detail is too small, and no piece of information should go unreported, the statement said. If you know something, please share it with our detectives. Your information could be the key to holding those responsible accountable. Investigators established a tip hotline and a link for people to submit evidence. As our detectives work to determine exactly what happened and identify those responsible, we remain committed to getting answers for these families. Tallahassee Mayor John Dailey called the incident a truly horrific and heartbreaking tragedy. Tonight and in the days ahead, the FAMU family is not alone. Our entire community stands with you, Dailey wrote on X. Florida AM said in a statement late Saturday it was aware of an incident that occurred near campus on Perry Street on the evening of October 24. Our hearts go out to the victims and all those affected by this tragic incident. entry.title: St. Lucie County Fire District confirms firefighter’s death - WPBF
entry.summary: St. Lucie County Fire District confirms firefighter’s death    WPBF
entry.article_text: A firefighter/paramedic died Saturday morning while on duty, one year after his brother, also with the St. Lucie County Fire District, passed away, the agency said. Austin Hodge, 34, joined the St. Lucie County Fire District on July 17, 2017. He was assigned to Station 9 in Fort Pierce. A procession of firefighters and personnel from other agencies went from HCA Lawnwood Hospital to the morgue in Fort Pierce on Saturday morning. His brother, Jarius Hodge, died on July 22, 2025, after falling ill at work at Station 3. His family said he had the flu, felt weak and was later rushed to the hospital, where he died hours later. People gathered on May 30 to celebrate what would have been his 27th birthday with a cookout and balloon release. Austin Hodge told WPBF at the time: "He was a quiet leader, and we take a lot from him. He was my younger brother, but I looked up to him in many ways to keep me poised, keep me patient. And I think that's what he's teaching everybody today." In June, another firefighter, Connor Whitehead, 21, died on May 31 but the cause of death wasn't released. Stay up to date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25 There are 20 fire stations and 523 firefighters in the county, according to the agency's website. Information regarding memorial arrangements and opportunities to honor Hodge's service iwll be shared in coordination with his family as details are finalized. "His death is a profound loss to the St. Lucie County Fire District and the fire service community," the agency said. "The District extends its heartfelt condolences to Hodge’s family, friends, and fellow firefighters during this difficult time." Several agencies offered their condolences, including Port St. Lucie Fire Rescue, Fort Pierce Police Officers Association, Port St. Lucie Police Department, Indian River County Sheriff's Office, Indian River County Emergency Services Department, Indian River County Fire Rescue, Palm Beach County Fire Rescue, Riviera Beach Fire Rescue. https://www.facebook.com/stluciesheriff/posts/pfbid0cPopWYk7mLx2z6QfJqkd99ZUoP9dWGSRx3Y7yjuN21oLAqBUmr6n8RYoUYP9RGaZl The St. Lucie agency thanked other agencieson Facebook. https://www.facebook.com/slcfd/posts/pfbid02FGoAgmLryFmnkCkLqRQfwhzpBpGAX3Bh285A6jFqKysGajonPUPDHeKjxdFm2KQvl "In the hours following this heartbreaking loss, our firefighters, Honor Guard, and public safety partners came together to honor our fallen brother and stand alongside one another during an incredibly difficult time. The brotherhood of the fire service extends far beyond the walls of a fire station. It is a bond built on trust, shared experiences, and an unwavering commitment to one another. "Today, that bond was especially evident through the incredible support of the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office, Fort Pierce Police Department, Port St. Lucie Police Department, and peer support teams from Martin and Indian River counties. "Together, they offered strength, compassion, and support while ensuring Austin was honored with the dignity and respect he deserves. Our hearts are with Austin’s family, loved ones, and everyone who had the privilege of serving alongside him. We are deeply grateful to our fellow first responders and community for the outpouring of support during this tremendous loss." Get the latest news updates with the WPBF 25 News app.

entry.title: St. Lucie County Fire District mourns unexpected loss of firefighter - cw34.com
entry.summary: St. Lucie County Fire District mourns unexpected loss of firefighter    cw34.com
entry.article_text: Lucie County firefighter-paramedic died while on duty Saturday, more than a year after his younger brother, who also served as a firefighter-paramedic, died at age 26. Lucie County Fire District announced the line-of-duty death of Austin Hodge on Saturday, Oct. 24, calling his death a profound loss to the department and the fire service community. Hodge joined the district on July 17, 2017, and served the community for more than nine years. He was assigned to Station 9. Neighboring Indian River County Fire Rescue also shared condolences following the firefighter’s unexpected death Saturday morning. Lucie County Fire District asked the public to respect Hodge’s family as they grieve. Information about memorial arrangements will be shared as details are finalized. Read more: Missing 5-year-old girl found dead in Fort Pierce body of water Brothers shared a career in firefighting Austin Hodge’s death comes more than a year after his younger brother, Jarius Hodge, also a St. Lucie County firefighter-paramedic, died on July 22, 2025. The brothers shared a close bond and a passion for serving their community. This was my best friend, my twin, Austin Hodge previously told CBS12 News. We had the same hairstyle. He described Jarius as someone who loved his family and his work as a first responder. He loved going to work, loved working beside me. I loved working beside him, Austin said. He always pushed me to keep going. He was someone who loved his family, his community and his country. Family sought accountability after Jarius’ death In an interview with CBS12 News , Austin said Jarius became ill after catching the flu from a patient at work in July 2025. Austin said his younger brother went to Cleveland Clinic Tradition Hospital in Port St. Lucie on July 22, struggling to breathe, but died hours later. He alleged that medical staff made critical errors in treating his brother, including taking three attempts to intubate him. He said Jarius had been healthy before becoming ill. Austin also spoke publicly about Florida’s medical malpractice laws, arguing that restrictions on who can pursue certain wrongful-death claims prevented his family from seeking legal accountability for Jarius’ death. This is unjust, and it's been going on for too long, Austin said in the earlier interview. He emphasized that his family was seeking accountability rather than financial compensation. For me personally, for my family, this has nothing to do with any type of dollar, he said. We just want those physicians to be held accountable. The circumstances surrounding Austin Hodge’s death have not been released. Lucie County Fire District said additional information about ways to honor his service will be shared in coordination with his family.
